News.title: Teacher ‘who had sex with pupil’ tells court ‘I wasn’t going to dress like Margaret Thatcher’ after tight-clothing claim
News.content:
'PAEDO' MISS Teacher ‘who had sex with pupil’ tells court ‘I wasn’t going to dress like Margaret Thatcher’ after tight-clothing claim

A TEACHER accused of having sex with a pupil today told a court “I wasn’t going to dress like Margaret Thatcher” in her mid-20s.

Sally-Anne Bowen, 65, allegedly abused two boys at Christ’s College in Finchley, North London when they were aged 14 and 15 in the 1980s.



The teacher – then aged 25 – allegedly “engaged in flirtatious conduct” with the pupils and “engaged in sexual relationships with them both”.

Jurors heard she allegedly dressed in “short, very tight skirts” and would walk around the school with her “t**s sticking out”.



Giving evidence, Bowen denied wearing short outfits and said she “would not have been allowed to get away it”.

She was asked to step out of the witness box at Harrow Crown Court to show the general length of her skirts at the time.



Placing her hands a few inches above her knees, Bowen said: “They were shorter than I’m wearing now – they were not mini skirts.”

She reminded jurors that she was then aged in her mid-20s, adding as she stepped back into the witness box: “I wasn’t going to dress like Margaret Thatcher.”

One former pupil Tobias Oliver, who did not know the two alleged victims, previously told how Bowen caused “a stir” when she started at the school, which normally had male or older female teachers.

He said: “She dressed and behaved more like my teenage female friends than the other teachers. She would wear short, very tight skirts, a tight T-shirt or vest top and a loose cardigan.



“The topics of conversation in class often strayed away from chemistry and became quite sexual.

“She would often chew on the end of her hair or cardigan. She would brush her hand over her breasts … it was more like what you would see in a Sabrina Carpenter video than what you would see in a classroom.”

Mr Oliver also told jurors that Bowen had no boundaries and “felt more like trying to be one of us, like our friend, than a teacher”.



Bowen claimed she would be subject to some inappropriate comments from pupils as she was young and one of the only female teachers at the school – but insisted she simply ignored the behaviours.

Giving evidence previously, the first alleged victim told jurors he slept with Bowen “about 20 or 30 times”.

He also denied being a “fantasist” who invented the allegations – branding the suggestion “quite insulting”.

In a police interview, the boy said Bowen would dress in a “sexually provocative” way while teaching chemistry at the all-boys’ school.

He described her outfits as “tight Levi’s jeans and black skinny pants that you could see everything in, and a black mini skirt”.



The victim also told police how on one occasion, the boys were looking at a porn magazine when Bowen took it from them.

Jurors heard he expected her to confiscate it but she instead “pointed to an image of a naked woman” and said “that’s what my p***y looks like”.

Bowen later told the boy she was leaving the UK to stay at a kibbutz in Israel, the court heard.



The boy first disclosed the alleged abuse to a partner, who told him to go to police.

When Bowen was interviewed in 2015, she claimed he was a “bit of a nuisance” and “besotted” with her.

Jurors heard she described the sexual relationship claims as “just pure fantasy”.

As a result of the allegations, Bowen faced a Teaching Regulation Authority (TRA) hearing in 2022.

The teacher is also accused of letting the second boy touch her breasts and kiss her during lunch at a cafe near the school.



The court heard he later read about the TRA hearing online and came forward after encouragement from his wife and family.

He claimed he was “goaded” by other boys at the school into kissing “young and attractive” Bowen.

The pupil also remembered touching her breasts and putting his hand near her crotch – to which “she would not react negatively”, it was said.

In his police interview, he said Bowen was “possibly the hottest teacher in our school”.

He added: “She was young, she was pretty. She had long straight blonde hair. She had nice eyes.



‘She walked around in a Levi 501 T-shirt. You know I said not good language, but she would walk around with her t*ts sticking out.

“I think she knew it. She had that level of confidence. Some people like that, want that, appreciate it.

“But she never really caught my eye. I was a bit of a goth. I liked girls with dark hair and she wasn’t.

“People would always have conversations. ‘Who’s the fittest teacher? Who would you want to be with the most?’ And she was always at the top of everyone’s list.”

Bowen denies eight counts of indecent assault.



The trial continues.

News.title: Mob of meerkats including pregnant mum tragically die after tunnel collapses at UK wildlife park
News.content:
MEERKAT TRAGEDY Mob of meerkats including pregnant mum tragically die after tunnel collapses at UK wildlife park

A MOB of meerkats in a Leicestershire wildlife park have died after a tunnel collapsed on them during a sudden period of heavy rainfall.

The tragic animals, including a pregnant mother, died at Tropical Birdland, in Lindridge Lane, Desford – with only one meerkat surviving the catastrophe.



The mammals had dug a tunnel for a new litter during the hot weather.

But sadly, heavy downpours meant the tunnel caved in, trapping them inside.



The park announced today that all the meerkats died in the awful incident, including a pregnant mum called Big Mama, with staff said to be “heartbroken”.

However, they managed to save one lucky meerkat from the terrible ordeal.

Staff are spending as much time as possible with the sole meerkat to provide comfort during this traumatic time.

In a post on social media, the site said: “It is with heavy hearts that we announce the news of the passing of our beloved meerkats.

“Most of last week, our matriarch ‘Big Mama’ had her mob digging out and preparing a fresh chamber underground, ready for the arrival of her next litter of pups.

“Big Mama was an experienced mother, having several litters over the years, and her mob were very well practised in digging tunnels and chambers.



“After an unusually long heatwave, the ground was ideal for digging.

“In an unexpected and catastrophic turn of events, the sudden heavy rainfall after such a long, hot, dry spell compromised the structure of the tunnels, causing them to collapse.

“Staff were able to locate where the meerkats were underground and were able to rescue one member of the mob, but were heartbroken to find the rest of the group had passed away.

“The team is regularly spending time with the surviving member of the group to comfort and monitor them closely.

“This has been an incredibly distressing and heartbreaking time for all the team.



“We thank you all for your continued support during this difficult and upsetting time.”

News.title: Brit dad swept away to his death after getting caught in rip while swimming with wife & three children on holiday island
News.content:
HOLIDAY TRAGEDY Brit dad swept away to his death after getting caught in rip while swimming with wife & three children on holiday island

A BRIT dad has died after being swept away in a riptide while swimming with his wife and three kids on a holiday island.

The family got into trouble off the coast of Senggigi, Indonesia.



They were out swimming at Kerandangan Beach at around 3.30pm on Wednesday when the father was suddenly taken by a rip tide.

He was missing underwater for 18 minutes before being pulled unconscious from the waves.



Local residents had rushed to his aid with a jet ski and diving equipment.

The dad was rushed to hospital but could not be saved.



His wife and three children survived the ordeal.

They had been staying at the Rinjani Eco Resort in Tanjung, North Lombok, a holiday island near Bali.

Mataram Search and Rescue (SAR) spokesperson I Gusti Lanang Wiswananda said in a statement: “There were five foreign nationals from Britain who were swept away.

“Four survived, including the mother and three children.”



He added: “According to the latest information, the victim was taken to Bhayangkara Hospital and was declared dead.”

An FCDO spokesperson told The Sun: “We are providing consular assistance to the family of a British national who died in Indonesia and are in contact with the local authorities.”

It comes after another Brit tourist died on neighbouring Bali in March.

The 39-year-old was swimming at Nyang-Nyang Beach when he is believed to have been struck by the swell and pulled away by a rip current.

Footage shows two tourists braving the strong waves as they battled to pull the man’s body ashore.



Paramedics arrived and confirmed that he was dead before taking him to the local hospital for a post-mortem examination.

Nyoman Sidakarya, Head of the Denpasar Search and Rescue Office, said: “The search and rescue standby officer on duty received information from the Pecatu community officer requesting evacuation assistance regarding the discovery of a body in the middle of the sea.

“The evacuation involved several agencies, including the Denpasar Search and Rescue Office, the Water Police, South Kuta Police, Pecatu village authorities, Balawista South Kuta lifeguards, and members of the local community.”

Authorities said they were investigating the cause of his death.

A spokesperson for the Foreign Office (FCDO) said: “We are supporting the family of a British man who has died in Bali, Indonesia, and are in contact with the local authorities.”

News.title: Twelve arrested over A66 wrong-way crash that killed 2 cops & 5 joyriders – as police probe second car ‘ramming homes’
News.content:
TWELVE people have been arrested over the horror crash that killed two cops and 5 joyriders with police probing a second car “ramming homes”.

The shocking smash saw a Volkswagen Passat crash into a cop car while driving in the wrong direction on the A66, killing PC Matthew Blades, 37, and PC Tom Clough, 38.



The five young men in the Passat, who also died, were named as Michael Robert Cahill, 23, Theo Rae, 17, Cole Robert Worthy, 17, Jacob Matusiak, 23, and Makai Saddington, 18.

Cleveland Police said today that four of those killed in the vehicle – Worthy , Matusiak, Saddington and Rae – which hit the cop car had previous police convictions.



Now, cops have also confirmed that nine men and three women aged between 19 and 61, have been arrested on suspicion of several offences.

The alleged offences include possession of a firearm and participating in the activities of an organised crime group.

Some of those arrested over the A66 investigation are suspected of “participating in the activities of an organised crime group” Cleveland Police added.

Cops are continuing to investigate the moments leading up to the fatal smash on Saturday.



It comes after…

In the early hours of Saturday 22 August, police received several reports of two vehicles being driven dangerously.

The first vehicle, which is believed to be a Volvo XC60, was witnessed to be ramming properties in the Middlesbrough area.



The second vehicle, a Volkswagen Passat, is believed to have been associated with the activities of the Volvo XC60.

The Volvo XC60 involved in the initial reports has been traced and recovered in Middlesbrough as part of the criminal investigation.

Cleveland Police believes the Passat was being driven with cloned number plates and had been linked to several suspicious incidents.

And just moments before the horrifying fatal smash, officers had been chasing the car in a highspeed pursuit for seven minutes through residential streets.

Previous convictions of four occupants Cole Worthy Use threatening abusive language to cause harassment, alarm and distress on 27 October 2024 and pleaded guilty Failing to surrender to custody on 14 May 2025 and pleaded guilty Common assault of a police officer on 27 April 2025 and pleaded guilty Driving without a licence on 7 June 2026 and pleaded guilty Using a vehicle without insurance on 7 June 2026 and pleaded guilty Driving without reasonable consideration on 7 June 2026 and pleaded guilty Driving using a mobile phone on 7 June 2026b and pleaded guilty Jakub Matusiak Using a vehicle without insurance on 22 March 2026 and pleaded guilty Driving without a licence on 22 March 2026 and pleaded guilty Makai Saddington Possession of a controlled class C drug on 31 May 2025 and pleaded guilty Possession of a knife in a public place on 31 May 2025 and pleaded guilty 11 October 2025 three offences for assaulting a police officer and pleaded guilty Assaulted a police officer on 9 June 2026 and pleaded guilty Racially aggravated intentional harassment, alarm and distress on 9 June 2026 and pleaded guilty Theo Rae 12 shoplifting offences between 21 October 2023 and 4 May 2024 and pleaded guilty to all offences Three thefts from motor vehicle offences between 31 January 2024 and 25 September 2024 and pleaded guilty to all offences One theft of vehicle on 13 April 2024 and pleaded guilty Possession of cannabis on 22 April 2024 and pleaded guilty Aggravated vehicle taking on 16 May 2024 and pleaded guilty Aggravated vehicle taking 2 January 2025 and pleaded guilty Conviction of an offence while a youth rehabilitation order is in force on 26 February 2025 and pleaded guilty Assaulted a police officer on 30 April 2026 and pleaded guilty Michael Robert Cahill No convictions

Ring doorbell footage captured it being driven at speed through streets in Middlesbrough at around 3.36am.



Cops called off the pursuit when the Passat went on to the A66 because it had begun travelling the wrong way down the road.

But just ten seconds later, the car slammed into a different marked police vehicle travelling correctly on the A66.

Cleveland police have also said there is no evidence to indicate that filming of the activities that took place on Friday night and Saturday morning has taken place for the purposes of TikTok.



Assistant Chief Constable Wayne Fox, responsible for the strategic leadership of the investigation, said: “This has been a fast moving and complex investigation, with significant links to serious and organised criminal activity.

“The events of that tragic night will have a lasting and profound impact on the Cleveland area and the communities we seek to protect.

“We have a duty to respond to, and thoroughly investigate, the serious criminal activity that resulted in this fatal incident, and to bring all those responsible to justice.

“Our robust response will continue in the weeks and months to come, as we continue to tackle those that seek to cause harm to our communities and tackle serious and organised crime.



“Officers and staff across Cleveland have shown incredible resilience in continuing their work in the face of tragedy.

“Two of their colleagues lost their lives while serving the people of Cleveland and, while the impact will be felt by our people for a long time to come, they have continued to act with the upmost professionalism.

“I am also extremely grateful for the support we have received, and continue to receive, from the public of Cleveland and our wider police family.”

The devastating crash has now left two police families grieving officers who had gone to work to protect others.



PC Blades was a husband and father-of-two who had recently taken on a new role coaching Seaton Carew FC and was preparing to coach the club’s under-sevens team, where his own son plays.

His wife has paid a heartbreaking tribute to her “beloved husband”, “best friend” and “the most devoted father to our two young boys”.

PC Clough, 38, had previously served with the British Transport Police and was also a former soldier.

His family described him as their “hero” and a man with a “fantastic” sense of humour who would always jump into action when needed.

The five young men who died in the Passat have also been mourned by relatives and friends.

News.title: Year-round dog beach ban sparks uproar in UK seaside resort as locals slam ‘ludicrous’ plans
News.content:
HUNDREDS of protestors have hit back at proposals to ban dogs from the beach in a UK seaside village.

The plans have been called “ludicrous” by locals and many dog owners descended on the beach to object to the year-round ban.



The ban would see pooches banished from a large stretch of the beach in Rhos-on-Sea, a seaside resort in North Wales.

Conwy Borough Council has plans to exclude dogs from the beach’s new “tideless” zone, making it a canine-free area all year round.



The proposals have been put forward in the hope’s of updating the council’s current Public Spaces Protection Order.

Plans outlined include a “dog exclusion zone on the area of beach fronting the Cayley Promenade” as well as designated dog exercise areas, with dog-related issues having been dubbed a “key concern” by the council.



Proposal forms state that dog fouling is among the reasons for the proposed ban, as they state: “The Council recognise that the vast majority of dog owners are responsible and clean up after their dogs when they foul, unfortunately however, a few irresponsible dog owners who fail to clean up still remain.”

The proposal continues: “Besides the unpleasant smell and the mess created by dog fouling when it gets on for example pram wheels, wheelchairs, shoes and clothing etc.

“The dangers to health from dog faeces are well documented.”

Opposers took to the beach on August 23 in a bid to force the council to reconsider the plans.



The protest was organised by Councillor Jo Nuttall, who is pleading with the council to “reassess” the decision.

“This permanent ban is disproportionate. You can see by the turnout today just how strong feelings are about allowing dogs on the beach,” she told the North Wales Pioneer.

“Most of us are responsible dog owners. It’s a really large section of the beach. It completely cuts off people’s walking routes,” she added.

“My message to the council is please reassess. A permanent dog ban makes no sense.”

Residents who showed up to protest also shared their hopes for the proposals to be rethought, with one calling them “absolutely ludicrous”.



Wendy Routledge, who walks her dog on the beach every day, suggested the council implement wardens to ensure the beach is kept clean

She added: “Humans leave behind far more mess on this beach than dogs do.

“Of course, there are dog owners who don’t pick mess up. If there was someone visible, like a dog warden, making sure people are doing it, that would be far better for the town than just banning everybody.”

In a statement, Councillor Stephen Price, cabinet member housing, regulatory and audit told The Sun: “Dog fouling and irresponsible dog ownership are issues that councillors hear about regularly from residents.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“These Dog Control Orders are intended to strike a fair balance, giving dog owners the freedom to enjoy public spaces with their pets while ensuring everyone can use those spaces safely and comfortably,” he added.



“The vast majority of dog owners are responsible, but these measures are aimed at tackling the small number who allow their dogs to foul, stray or be out of control in public places. I’d encourage everyone to get involved in the consultation and share their views.”

News.title: Brit, 33, becomes first UK national to die fighting for Putin after being hit by Ukrainian suicide drone on frontline
News.content:
A FISHERMAN who betrayed his country to fight for Vladimir Putin has become the first Brit to die on the Ukrainian frontline.

Bradley Townsend, from Yorkshire, was killed after being struck by a suicide bomb in Ukraine.



The self-proclaimed “normal working-class lad” joined Mad Vlad’s army to repay Russia for supporting the miner’s strike in the 1980s.

The 33-year-old ran off and joined Putin’s army in April, despite having no military experience.



Just ten days later on June 10 Townsend was killed in a drone strike while fighting in Lyman, the frontline in the hotly contested Donetsk region.

Fellow Brit traitor Aiden Minnis said Townsend had “sacrificed his life for our cause”.

The pair claimed to be fighting a “Holy War” and have accused the Ukrainian army of being “Nazis”.

Former security minister and Conservative MP Tom Tugendhat said he felt “very sorry for him and his family” but that joining the Russian army was “unbelievably stupid”.

“It’s extremely misguided and, no question about it, it’s criminal because you’re engaging in an army that is committing the most barbarous war crimes that the world has seen in decades”, he said.

Townsend is believed to be the first British volunteer to be killed while fighting for the Russians in Ukraine.



The British Government have said that they are aware of reports of his death and are “in contact with his family”.

Enlisting with Putin’s army “could be breaking UK laws”, the government warned.

Brits who return to Britain after fighting for Putin may face criminal charges.

In an interview in April, Townsend said: “I came here with the idea that I probably won’t be able to go home. I’d definitely get prosecuted if I went back.

“I’m not here for a suicide mission, but I understand that’s what can happen.



“This was my own decision, I wasn’t pushed into anything.”

News.title: Man, 33, charged after couple ‘caught having sex’ on Ferris wheel at Download Festival in front of thousands
News.content:
ROMP CHARGE Man, 33, charged after couple ‘caught having sex’ on Ferris wheel at Download Festival in front of thousands

A 33-YEAR-OLD man has been charged with outraging public decency after a couple was caught allegedly having sex on a Ferris wheel in front of thousands of revellers.

Leicestershire Police launched a probe into the incident after the pair were filmed reportedly engaging in sexual acts at Download Festival in June.



Fans were waiting to see Guns ‘n’ Roses play at the festival in Castle Donington, Leicestershire, when they spotted the couple.

The duo were seen, apparently engaged in sexual activity, in one of the cabins of the ferris wheel as it rotated.



Images and video of the indecent act was shared widely on social media at the time.

Police were alerted to the incident and launched a probe into the alleged public romp.

Following enquiries cops confirmed they had charged Innes Miller, 33, of Edwalton, Nottinghamshire, with outraging public decency.

The force says a woman has already been identified and voluntarily interviewed as part of their enquiries.

Miller is now due to appear at Leicester Magistrates’ Court on September 10.

When the couple were spotted romping on the ferris wheel, a stunned witness told The Sun: “Originally for the first rotation of the wheel people thought he was just standing behind her with his arms around her, looking at the view.



“But, as it got lower, somebody shouted ‘I can see her pants pulled aside!’”

Download Festival is the biggest rock and metal event in the UK and is attended by 80,000 every year.

But, the witness, who is a regular festival attendee, said: “I have never seen anything like this.

“They were literally in a glass pod above everyone’s heads at the busiest point of the night, just before Guns ‘n Roses were due on.

“It sort of brought everyone together in a weird way, before they were spotted the atmosphere was nervous apprehension because they’re always late on.



“As soon as the cameras came out and word started getting around about what happened the atmosphere completely changed – they made the night.

“All I can think is they thought the glass was tinted, but it wasn’t at all, it was actually spotless, you could see everything.”

News.title: Sharing dangerous driving videos is 'truly reprehensible', PM says
News.content:
The government has urged social media companies to remove posts celebrating dangerous driving, as Prime Minister Andy Burnham branded sharing them "truly reprehensible".

Earlier Defence Minister Luke Pollard told BBC Breakfast on Monday that "social media companies could take the content down easily and adjust their algorithms to stop it being distributed".

Two police officers died when a car going the wrong way down a dual carriageway crashed into their vehicle near Middlesbrough on Saturday. The five passengers in the other car were also killed.

A TikTok account believed to belong to one of the five passengers, 18-year-old Makai Saddington, shared videos appearing to show dangerous driving, which have since been removed.

Pollard said the government had "already taken steps" to tell social media companies to take down such content.

He added: "They know exactly what content is on their site, they know how their algorithm works.

"They also know that people post content to get views and the more views you get, sometimes you get money for it, so it's a financial incentive to post outrageous content that gets more people watching it."

Speaking to reporters in Kyiv, Burnham said the people who share footage glorifying dangerous driving are "doing something that's truly reprehensible".

A Downing Street spokeswoman said "the glorification of dangerous driving for clips and entertainment is utterly disgraceful".

She added that the culture secretary has been clear that footage should be removed by social media platforms "in line with their legal obligations", and that Ofcom has the government's "full backing to take action" against those that fail in their duties.

News.title: UK missiles offer may help Ukraine - but they are not what Zelensky needs most
News.content:
Instead, under Project Brakestop, it's developing its own long range cruise missiles, free of foreign components, and less than half the price of a Storm Shadow.

Project Brakestop is also being done at break-neck speed. The UK hopes to have a new cruise missile ready by the end of the year. It's promising to supply the new weapon to Ukraine.

It is Ukraine which has shown the world how to produce relatively cheap, mass produced weapons, necessary for a long protracted conflict.

Douglas Barrie, IISS Senior Fellow for Military Aerospace told the BBC: "The decision to share UK classified information on the MBDA SCALP missiles with Ukraine, as France and Ukraine work toward local assembly lines in Ukraine is notable. Any impact, however, will in part depend on how quickly Ukrainian assembled SCALP cruise missiles can be introduced into service.

"Given that Ukraine has already operated both Storm Shadow and SCALP familiarity with the missile may help speed the overall process, but this will also be dependent on the extent and pace at which local assembly can be established."

At the start of the war its armed forces relied on old Cold War-era Soviet weaponry.

A slow supply of Western weapons helped it adapt. But now Ukraine produces 70% of its own weapons.

Key has been its rapid development of drone technology â from small First Person View (FPV) one-way attack drones for the front line, to larger long-range drones capable of striking deep into Russian territory, further than Storm Shadows can strike.

Kyiv is on track to build 10 million drones by the end of this year. And they can do it cheaper than the West, by using mass-produced Chinese parts.

Nato allies' equivalent drones can be twice as expensive as they try to shun Chinese components.

However, there are still weapons that Ukraine needs and struggles to produce on its own. From fast fighter jets to the most urgent example, interceptors to take down Russian ballistic missiles

The most effective weapon to do that, by far, is the US made Patriot interceptor. Ukraine has all but run out of them and Russian ballistic missiles now make it through Ukrainian air defences with ease.

America's war in Iran has meant they're in even shorter supply.

They're also expensive â at around Â£3m a missile â and production rates have been slow. The US is planning to double production rates from around 600 Patriot missiles per annum to 2,000, but that'll take several years.

President Trump signalled last month he'd be willing to share Patriot technology with Ukraine, but has since rowed back.

Even if he had given approval it would have taken a while for Ukraine to make Patriots themselves - some estimate at least a year. Ukraine would also be relying on the same sophisticated components that are in high demand across the globe.

Ukraine has embarked on a programme to develop its own interceptor missiles with European support â known as Project Freya.

But there are huge technological challenges in building a high speed missile to take down another missile travelling at thousands of miles per hour. It is expensive and often time consuming.

Ukraine's military and its weapons manufacturers have shown themselves to be fast learners.

One of its own companies, Fire Point, is developing its own ballistic missiles which it hopes will be ready to fire in anger next year.

But Russia's already ramped up its own ballistic missile production, to around one hundred a month.

Developing sophisticated weapons is expensive and can't be done quickly. Ukraine is short of both time and money.

So, the move to hand missile blueprints to Ukraine will be welcome, but it isn't an immediate fix for Ukraine's most pressing problems, and it won't dramatically alter Kyiv's ability to strike Russia in new ways.

News.title: Divorce, smartphones and control - BBC sees how Taliban run Afghanistan
News.content:
Governor Abdullah Sarhadi gives money to treat a boy's broken arm and hands out funds for a local mosque - then, in his office in northern Afghanistan, an astonishing exchange unfolds.

A young woman tells the grey-bearded former Taliban commander that she wants to divorce her husband, who she accuses of months of abuse and beatings.

She will not take no for an answer.

In a country where girls are banned from secondary education, the 18-year-old argues her case calmly and confidently, her face completely hidden behind a full-face veil and sunglasses.

"If there was any chance to live together, I wouldn't be hereâ¦ I have taken my decision," she says.

After trying to persuade her to avoid divorce, the governor later comments that women are "mindless" and "deficient in intellect", to laughter from the male officials, bodyguards and elders around him.

The moment gives a rare glimpse into the day-to-day realities of the Taliban's rule, five years after they swept aside the US-backed government in 2021.

News.title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott guilty of child sex abuse
News.content:
Former world snooker champion Graeme Dott has been found guilty of child sexual abuse.

The 49-year-old denied two charges of lewd and libidinous behaviour towards a girl and a boy between 1993 and 2010.

During a trial, the High Court in Glasgow heard that Dott had exposed himself and inappropriately touched a primary school girl in the 1990s and attacked a young boy between 2006 and 2010.

Dott, who won the sport's world championship at The Crucible in 2006, will be sentenced at a separate hearing in Edinburgh on 29 September.

Dott covered his face with his hands and shook his head while the verdict was delivered by jurors following a five-day trial.

He had previously called the allegations made against him "disgusting".

During the trial, the court heard how he had "caressed" the girl's bottom while giving her a piggyback and that, on another occasion, he had exposed himself to her.

Police previously contacted Dott about the allegations in 2001, but no charges were brought.

The woman gave a new statement to police in 2025.

The court was also told how Dott "rewarded" the boy with money, crisps and fizzy drinks after molesting him in the shower at a home in South Lanarkshire.

The boy, now a man in his 20s, also said he was abused in a car on a number of occasions.

News.title: Race Across the World star Jo Gardiner dies aged 61 one year after son's death
News.content:
A former Race Across the World contestant has died, a year after her son and co-star's death in a car crash.

Jo Gardiner, 61, died "following a long and courageous battle with cancer", her family said.

Gardiner, a physiotherapist from Manchester, travelled across South America with her son Sam in the second series of the BBC show, which aired in 2020.

Her family said she was "one of a kind" who "lived fully, fiercely and never did anything by halves".

News.title: Graduate job vacancies drop by almost 50% in a year, survey suggests
News.content:
The number of graduate jobs has fallen almost in half in the past year, according to new figures, as employers cut entry-level roles in favour of AI and battle rising costs.

Jobs website Adzuna said it had just 8,383 graduate vacancies listed in July, down from 15,397 at the same point last year.

Adzuna also found competition among job seekers across all levels is rising, with an average of 2.14 job seekers per vacancy in July, up from 1.93 a year earlier.

Businesses have said employer national insurance and minimum wage hikes have made hiring more expensive, particularly for junior staff.

The number of graduate vacancies listed hit its lowest level since Adzuna started recording such data in 2016. The firm pointed to a peak for graduate roles in 2017, when it had more than 55,800 listed on its website. That is more than six times the number of roles listed on the site in July.

Andrew Hunter, the co-founder of Adzuna, said the figures show "employers still haven't found a reason to open up hiring" for recent graduates.

Official figures show the UK's youth unemployment rate - which covers 16-to-24-year-olds - was 16.2% in the three months to March 2026. The number of young people not in education, employment or training (Neet) is now over one million.

Young people have told BBC News previously they have applied for hundreds of jobs before even receiving a response.

They also expressed frustration at the growing number of employers using AI to screen applications.

Many university graduates also face mounting student debt.

Former government minister Alan Milburn is leading a major review of the youth unemployment crisis. He has previously said the number of entry-level jobs is shrinking, as is the number of part-time jobs traditionally filled by teenagers and students.

The Adzuna data also showed vacancies for jobs in travel, teaching and construction rose in recent weeks.

But sectors including healthcare, nursing, hospitality and logistics posted fewer vacancies.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham recently changed the rules for public contracts so that companies bidding for them have to show how they will create jobs and training opportunities.

News.title: Victims describe 'house of terror' abuse by mother, grandmother and stepfather
News.content:
A mother, grandmother and stepfather who subjected three children to years of abuse in a "house of terror" have avoided jail.

Shirley Freeman, Julia Stephen and David McColl's victims were beaten, starved and psychologically tormented between 2003 and 2012.

Freeman, 51, and Stephen, 69, were earlier found guilty of cruel and unnatural treatment. McColl, 50, admitted the crimes.

At Aberdeen Sheriff Court, Sheriff Craig Findlater said no sentence could "repair the awful childhoods" of the trio's victims.

Warning: This article contains descriptions of child abuse

One of their victims, Rebekah Simpson, 23, said the abuse she received has had a lifelong impact on her mental and physical health.

She said she felt that court did not fully consider the impact the experience has had on her - but she was not disappointed with the sentences.

"Not having to speak to them again is justice for me," she said.

"I want to be able to walk the streets and know they will be punished if they try and approach me."

Her siblings, William and Meaghann Murphy, who are now 25 and 28, told BBC Scotland News the violence and cruelty they experienced as children became normal.

News.title: 'It's not Alton Towers' - rows break out over queuing at Wales' highest mountain
News.content:
Visitors to Wales' highest mountain are being urged to respect others by not skipping queues to reach the top following rows among climbers.

Recent hot weather means there have been bumper summer crowds at Yr Wyddfa, also known as Snowdon, where people have reportedly waited more than one hour to reach the 1,085m (3,560ft)-high summit.

Social media videos have shown arguments among queue-jumpers and those patiently waiting their turn to touch the metal plate that marks the top.

A recent video showed Marc Screeton, from Manchester, being heckled as he bypassed the line, saying: "Imagine queuing on a mountain? No chance."

But others have said queuing is necessary for safety reasons.

News.title: Woman pleads guilty to breaching anonymity order in Jeffrey Donaldson case
News.content:
A 55-year-old Ballynahinch woman has pleaded guilty to breaching a lifetime anonymity order by posting information likely to reveal the alleged identity of a victim in the Jeffrey Donaldson sex abuse case.

Donna Toman of Lord Moira Park appeared at Downpatrick Magistrates' Court on Monday.

A defence lawyer said she was entering a guilty plea to a charge relating to a social media post earlier this year.

The charge states the post "was likely to lead members of the public to identify a person as the person against whom a qualifying offence is alleged to have been committed".

On 29 July police stated that the woman's arrest related to the Jeffrey Donaldson trial.

District Judge Magill said he wanted a pre-sentence report by 12 October adding that it was a "serious offence".

The court heard the offence can bring a six-month sentence.

Donaldson, who was an MP from 1997 until 2024, was convicted in June of 18 counts of sex abuse including one count of rape, which he committed against two women when they were children.

He was told by the judge that the sentence would be a lengthy one.

It has since been confirmed he is to appeal his convictions.

News.title: Pubs and hotels could see business rates reformed after review
News.content:
A review is being launched into the way business rates are calculated for pubs and hotels in England and Wales, and could lead to a reform of the system.

The Treasury says business rates expert Jerry Schurder will lead the review into rate valuations and report back in March 2027, with the government calling for the views of landlords, hoteliers and business owners to feed in to the process.

Last month, Andy Burnham announced a 20% cut in business rates for pubs, social clubs and live music venues in England, to come into effect in April.

Pub groups have argued they face disproportionately higher rates bills, but other businesses have called for a wider reform of the rates system.

According to the British Beer and Pub Association (BBPA), 161 pubs closed in the first three months of this year across England, Scotland and Wales, equating to the loss of around 2,400 jobs.

Rising business rates are cited as one issue facing the sector, although there have also been complaints that increases in National Insurance and the minimum wage have made staff costs more expensive.

James Murray, financial secretary to the Treasury, said the new review would look at "a rethink of valuations - so that we can build a fairer system for the future".

Emma McClarkin, chief executive of the BBPA, said: "For years pubs have paid a disproportionately higher business rates bill which has ground down their ability to keep the doors open, so this review is sorely needed and hugely welcome."

The BBPA says pubs are valued differently for rates than retail venues. Instead of being based just on floor area, they are judged by a measure called Fair Maintainable Trade (FMT) - which means when a pub's turnover increases, so does its rates bill.

Jonathan Lawson, the chief executive of Butcombe Group, which has 120 pubs across the south and south west of England, told the BBC's Today programme that the use of FMT meant pubs were effectively being "punished for success", while large online retailers that operate out of warehouses were not subject to revenue-based rates calculations.

Their rates, he said, "are calculated based on what is deemed to be the market rent for that area, and takes very little on board in terms of revenue driven through that site".

"You can have a very large site paying a relatively low level of business rates versus a relatively small pub... paying a very high level of business rates."

Schurder is a former business rates policy lead at advisory firm Newmark UK, and his review will feed into the next rates revaluation in 2029.

Northern Ireland and Scotland set their own valuations, while Wales presently chooses to align its methodology with England. As the same approach is used across England and Wales, the review will be looking for responses from both nations.

Schurder's appointment was welcomed by Craig Beaumont of the Federation of Small Businesses (FSB) who said he would bring "crucial heavyweight business rates expertise into the Treasury".

However, Beaumont said the government needed to address the wider business rates system and exempt more smaller firms by increasing the rates relief threshold for small businesses.

Jonny Haseldine from the British Chambers of Commerce (BCC) also said the review of valuations should be wider.

"The full reform of business rates, promised by the government at the last election, is urgently needed. This continued piecemeal approach to reform is the wrong approach," he said.

While the BCC said hospitality was the sector most worried about rates, Haseldine warned firms in every sector were struggling with the "complex and outdated" system.

Shadow Chancellor Sir Mel Stride said the review was "far too late for a sector this Labour government has already done its best to kill off".

"Tax hikes on business premises and jobs, alongside job-destroying regulation in the Employment Rights Act, have left many hospitality businesses on the brink," he said.

Liberal Democrat Treasury spokesperson Daisy Cooper said reform of business rates was "long overdue", but also called for an emergency VAT cut and a reverse to jobs tax changes "which have hammered hospitality in particular".

News.title: Girl gets tumour diagnosis 12 hours after eye test
News.content:
A mum said she "fell apart" after finding out her four-year-old daughter had a brain tumour, just 12 hours after an eye test.

Katie, 41, said her daughter Phoebe, now five, started to be sick and was getting severe headaches in February, but was told "it was just migraines" by a GP.

Following an eye test in May, Katie was called by the optician who told her to take her daughter straight to A&E at Addenbrooke's Hospital in Cambridge. Just hours later, she was diagnosed with a brain tumour.

"I fell apart and just sobbed and sobbed," said the mum from St Neots, Cambridgeshire. Thankfully, Phoebe's tumour was not cancerous and she is now under the care of specialists.

Katie said: "I felt like we were probably wasting the hospital's time because Phoebe was running around playing like normal but, looking back, she was probably the sickest kid there.

"I kept thinking, how am I going to tell her dad and the other children?

"I kept asking if Phoebe would survive but the doctors said they were unable to answer that at that time, which is the worst thing in the world as a parent."

News.title: Reform says it will prioritise British-born workers for social housing
News.content:
Tice said he wanted the rules on who was allocated a home to be changed away from need to suitability, putting British families, workers and veterans at the front of the queue, saying: "This comes down to fairness."

"We're saying that the first people we should be looking after are young, British workers - under 35, young British married couples, young British veterans - who have done the right thing," he said.

"They've got a job, they're doing their best, working in their community, setting a fine example, because the role of the British government is actually to look after British citizens first."

Rules would be changed to reserve at least half of all social homes in England for British-born workers aged under 35, with prioritisation also given to married couples, veterans, victims of domestic violence and care leavers.

Tice claimed there were currently 540,000 existing affordable social homes occupied by overseas nationals and he wanted that to change.

"It's not fair that young British working families can't get on the housing ladder when overseas nationals have come to the UK and, because of the current rules based on need rather than suitability, they have jumped ahead in the queue," he said.

"We just don't think that's right: I can't think of another country where you rock up with a family and you expect the local taxpayer in that country to pay for your housing needs."

UK or Irish nationals made up 88.5% of main social home householders in 2024/25, according to the English Housing Survey.

That means around 11.5% of main householders, the perÂ­son in whose name the social home is renÂ­ted, were non-UK or Irish nationÂ­als.

For its part, Reform estimates 540,000 social homes are currently occupied by foreign nationals.

Reform has previously announced it would evict foreign nationals from social housing - a plan criticised by housing charity Shelter which said building more homes is the solution, rather than "changing the order of the queue" and "stoking division".

Tice also said Reform would raise Â£10bn a year to build new homes, in part by reintroducing the Right to Buy scheme of the 1980s, allowing people to buy council homes at a discount.

"The failure then was they didn't reinvest the proceeds into building more affordable homes," he said, adding he believed reinvestment would raise a third of the investment needed to build 50,000 homes a year over a decade.

Tice said another third would be raised via housing authorities, and the final third would be money from local government pension schemes.

A Labour Party spokesperson said the plan was "unworkable and unserious", adding: "It would blow a Â£10bn blackhole in the public finances, would create years of wrangling with the EU, and could leave British citizens without a place to call home.

"This Labour government is investing billions to deliver the biggest boost to social and affordable housing in a generation, to fix the housing crisis we inherited from the Tories."

The Conservative Party, which also said it would revoke the right of foreign nationals to social housing, accused Reform of "trying to catch up" with its policies.

The Tories have said their plan, which would allow Irish citizens and some EU nationals to remain in social housing, would free up around 230,000 homes.

Sir James Cleverly, shadow housing secretary, added: "The Conservatives have already set out comprehensive plans to ensure British nationals are at the front of the queue for social housing. Now Reform are trying to catch up.

"We also believe in a home owning society and that those who work hard should be able to buy their own home, without unnecessary barriers standing in their way."

Liberal Democrat spokesperson Gideon Amos said that Reform's plan was a "cruel gimmick".

Green MP SiÃ¢n Berry said her party would tackle housing issues by ending Right to Buy, building and buying hundreds of thousands of new council homes, and introducing rent controls.

She added: "Another blatantly racist and cruel policy from Reform, adding to a host of plans to create a two-tier Britain â one for those born in the UK and one for everyone else."

News.title: Rain to return this week with chance of thunderstorms and flooding
News.content:
The weather is set to turn more unsettled this week as rain returns with a chance of thunderstorms and localised flooding.

Some places could see a return to showery conditions by Tuesday, but it is from Wednesday onwards that more widespread and persistent rain will arrive from the south.

The wet weather will be welcome for parched regions of the UK, but a lot more will be needed before drought conditions start to ease.

As well as the rain, temperatures will also be on the rise once more, as warmer air moving in could push midweek highs close to 27C (81F) in places.

News.title: CrossCountry to run full train service after power outage causes major disruption
News.content:
Train operator CrossCountry says it expects to run a full service on Monday after cancelling nearly all of its UK services the day before following a power cut at its control centre.

The outage in Birmingham at the weekend brought disruption from Glasgow to Penzance.

Major routes were affected between Birmingham and Manchester, which pass through Stoke-on-Trent, Coventry and Wolverhampton. Journeys from Leeds to York and Cheltenham to Cardiff were also caught in the travel chaos, leaving passengers frustrated.

On Monday morning, CrossCountry reported a handful of service cancellations, although these were put down to trains departing late and staff shortages.

Customers are advised to check their journey before travelling.

The operator on Sunday thanked passengers for their patience and understanding during the disruption.

Tickets purchased for travel on CrossCountry services on Sunday will be valid for travel on CrossCountry services until Wednesday, the company has said.

News.title: 'It took 30 years to talk about my teacher raping me'
News.content:
It wasn't until 2022 when she had grief counselling that she confronted what had happened.

The following year she made a formal complaint to police.

"I am a mum now and my children are the age that I was then - and that cannot happen to them," she said.

She said finding the courage to contact police was difficult and it "took me a few days just to pluck up the courage".

Det Con Andrew Jones, from West Midlands Police's Major Crime Team, said: "I would like to express my gratitude to the brave woman who came forward to report what Allen had done to her as a child.

"She has been so brave throughout the investigation and court process."

Allen was sentenced at Birmingham Crown Court in July.

His defence argued the offence was committed during a difficult period in his life while he was experiencing anxiety.

But, during his sentencing remarks, His Honour Judge Paul Farrer KC, said he did not accept Allen's judgement was impaired at the time and said he had abused a position of trust.

That his offending remained undiscovered for more than three decades meant he was able to enjoy life in the community, the court heard.

It was noted the defendant was now in poor health, had diabetes, glaucoma and impaired hearing, had previously had a heart attack and might be experiencing the onset of Parkinson's disease.

The woman said it was not the sentencing but the guilty verdict that had been most important to her.

"I felt heard, I felt people have listened and they believe me," she added. "It is really validating and it raises your self-esteem a little bit, it means a lot."

News.title: Wicker Man director's sons complete their late father's film trilogy
News.content:
Robin Hardy always envisaged his iconic 1973 folk horror film The Wicker Man as the first part of a trilogy.

The Wicker Tree, released in 2011, brought him closer to that ambition, but his death in 2016 at the age of 86 left the project incomplete.

Now his sons, Justin and Dominic, have been able to complete their father's trilogy, after finding a script for the final film.

Wrath of the Gods has its premiere at the FrightFest horror festival in London, external on Friday, a family dream made possible thanks to the surprise discovery of some long-lost family archive.

"The person who bought Justin's old family home said they'd discovered six sacks of letters, scripts and other material pertaining to Robin Hardy and The Wicker Man in the attic," says Dominic, an art historian at the University of Quebec in Montreal.

"Justin's first instinct was to burn them, but we couldn't ignore this original source material. Although we left it unopened for six months or more."

Russ Abbot, who was once one of the BBC’s biggest stars, has opened up about leaving showbiz behind – saying his brand of comedy fell out of fashion when “alternative” comics and “political correctness came in”.

The retired comedian, 78, first rose to fame as a singer and drummer in British comedy show band, the Black Abbots, before he moved into TV presenting, hosting Russ Abbot’s Madhouse and The Russ Abbot Show for the BBC in the Eighties.

His last TV role was in BBC comedy Boomers with Alison Steadman, Philip Jackson, and June Whitfield. When the show was cancelled after two seasons in 2016, he officially retired and moved to Portugal.

open image in gallery Russ Abbot with his wife Patricia ( Getty )

Speaking about leaving show business, Abbot – who was born Russell Allan Roberts – told The Guardian that while he was disappointed when Boomers was cancelled, it isn’t true that he was embittered by the comedy landscape changing and that he wasn’t being offered any “straight roles”. He actually chose to leave the industry as his manager was retiring and he “thought it was a good time to call it quits and spend more time with [wife] Trish”, according to the publication.

“I’ve seen something on YouTube saying ‘The tragedy of Russ Abbot’ and ‘He’s run away to Portugal’,” he said. “I’ve had a wonderful career. Wonderful!”

Although he did note that his brand of sketch comedy fell by the wayside in the Nineties when “new wave” comedy came in.

“Alternative comedy. I thought, alternative comedy? What’s it alternative to? If the thing’s funny, it’s funny,” he said. “Political correctness came in, and you can’t laugh at each other and you can’t laugh at yourself.

“At the same time, a lot of comedy started going blue and I think: I’m not going down that road.”

Abbot now splits his time between Barbados and the Algarve with his wife Patricia, whom he married in 1967. The couple share four children.

open image in gallery Russ Abbot with Philip Jackson, James Smith and Nigel Planer in ‘Boomers’ ( BBC )

Abbot joined the cast of BBC One’s Last of the Summer Wine in 2008, taking on the role of Luther “Hobbo” Hobdyke in the last few series before its cancellation in 2010. He also appeared in Hotel Babylon, Casualty, The Sarah Jane Adventures, and The Last Detective.

In the Eighties, Abbot briefly launched a pop career, releasing the single “Atmosphere” in 1987. The track made it to number seven in the British music charts and in 2020, a campaign was launched by two university students to make it Christmas number one, with the song getting airtime on BBC Radio Nottingham.

President Donald Trump waved the green flag to start the Freedom 250 Grand Prix IndyCar race in Washington, D.C. Sunday — a brief, ceremonial moment that quickly swept social media.

The gesture produced a familiar divide online: mockery from Trump’s critics, celebration by his supporters and a steady stream of memes from everyone in between.

The first-of-its-kind IndyCar race, part of the nation’s 250th-anniversary festivities, drew an estimated 140,000 spectators to the capital. Drivers tore around a 1.7-mile circuit, past the National Mall and other monuments, bringing an unusually high-octane form of pageantry to Washington.

Before the race, Trump and First Lady Melania Trump took a lap around the course in the presidential limousine, known as the Beast, as onlookers gathered along the route. The couple were then joined in a box by members of Trump’s family and political inner circle, including his sons Eric and Don Jr, and close aide Natalie Harp.

Shortly before 1:20 p.m., Medal of Honor recipients Command Sgt. Maj. Matt Williams and Col. Paris Davis delivered the green flag to the president. With the first lady looking on, Trump raised the banner and quickly jerked it up and down.

Whether it was the flag’s position, Trump’s rapid-fire motion or the smirk on his face, the moment immediately became one of the day’s most replayed clips.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump waved a green flag to kick off the Freedom 250 Grand Prix IndyCar race in Washington on Sunday — a brief ceremonial moment that quickly took off on social media ( Getty Images )

Some commenters fixated on the way the 80-year-old president held the flag, remarking that he had grabbed it from the wrong side.

“Lmao they had to tell Donald Trump to hold the green flag the right way,” one X user wrote, sharing a clip that appeared to show Melania Trump and Medal of Honor recipient Matt Williams directing the president to reposition it.

Others mocked the wave itself. “This has to be the most [embarrassing] way to wave a flag [I have] ever seen in my life,” the account Call to Activism wrote. Another chimed in: “‘Wave’ is a stretch … more like spasmodic gesticulation.”

The clip also became a vehicle for broader political criticism, touching on everything from Trump’s Washington renovation projects to his foreign policy. “Considering he lost the war with Iran, it probably should be white,” one X user quipped, referring to the conflict that has now dragged on for nearly five months with no apparent end in sight.

open image in gallery The historic race, which saw drivers tearing across a 1.7-mile circuit around the National Mall, drew an expected crowd of 140,000 spectators ( Getty Images )

“Trump waves an ‘American flag blue’ color flag to start the IndyCar race in DC today,” another user joked, an apparent reference to the president’s renovation of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool. The pool was coated in a layer of “American flag blue” sealant before becoming covered in algae earlier this year.

Still others treated the green flag as an invitation for digital mischief. One user used it as a green screen, superimposing footage of Trump partying with Jeffrey Epstein at Mar-a-Lago in 1992.

The White House also reposted the clip, where it quickly surpassed one million views. “When someone says Trust in Trump,” the account wrote in the caption.

The post prompted some commenters to accuse the White House of cropping Natalie Harp out of the frame.

Harp, the president’s 35-year-old aide who was seated behind Melania Trump, has drawn scrutiny for what critics have characterized as an unusual level of devotion to the president.

Not all of the online reaction was hostile, however.

“Biden would have licked that flag,” wrote one user. “I’ll take Trump’s awkward wave, thanks.”

Another Trump supporter added: “Oh my god who gives a damn how he waves a flag. You democrats are grasping at straws trying to find stuff about him.”

Still a third user chimed in: “I’m not a fan of Trump, but this race on DC streets is cool.”

News.title: Disgraced ex-snooker champion Graeme Dott found guilty of sexually abusing children
News.content:

Read our Privacy notice

Former snooker world champion Graeme Dott has been found guilty of sexually abusing two primary school-aged children.

The 49-year-old subjected a girl and a boy to multiple incidents of abuse, with the girl targeted between 1993-1996 and the boy between 2006-2010.

In a five-day trial, the High Court in Glasgow heard Dott exposed himself in front of both children, touched them inappropriately, and kissed them.

On Monday, he was found guilty of two counts of lewd, indecent and libidinous behaviour towards them.

In both cases the abuse happened in the Glasgow area.

During the trial, jurors heard from one of Dott’s victims, a woman now in her 40s, who told the court Dott had sexually abused her on multiple separate occasions while she was a child.

She said the abuse had started with Dott “caressing” her bottom over her clothing while giving her a piggy back.

open image in gallery A five-day trial the High Court in Glasgow heard Former snooker world champion Graeme Dott exposed himself in front of both children, touched them inappropriately, and kissed them ( Reuters )

The woman also described an occasion when she said Dott suggested playing a “guessing game” where she had to guess what he was doing.

She told the court she lay down and he exposed himself to her and then began touching her with different parts of his body, including his penis.

The woman told the court that Dott told her not to tell anyone he was sexually abusing her.

The second victim, a man who is now in his late 20s, said he was sexually abused by Dott on multiple occasions, with the snooker player touching him inappropriately, kissing him, and performing sexual acts.

He told the court a lot of the abuse took place while he was in a shower, when Dott would come in either partly or completely undressed.

“He would… come into the shower and put soap on my body and wash me in the shower,” the man told the court.

“While he was washing me he would touch me in inappropriate places.”

He said looking back at it now, Dott was “clearly getting sexual gratification from it”, and he was “pleasuring himself” while this was taking place.

open image in gallery During the trial, jurors heard from one of Dott’s victims, a woman now in her 40s, who told the court Dott had sexually abused her on multiple separate occasions while she was a child ( PA Archive )

The man said that because of his age at the time, he “did not know what was going on”, and it was only later he realised the interaction “wasn’t right”.

The witness also described abuse which took place in a car, where he said Dott would kiss him on the face, head and lips, and “push himself up against me”.

Giving evidence last week, Dott had said there was “absolutely no way” he sexually abused two children.

Under cross-examination by prosecutor Lindsey Dalziel, Dott denied being attracted to the girl when she was young, calling the idea “disgusting”.

When Ms Dalziel put it to Dott that he touched the first victim and told her what to do, he denied the allegation and called it “lies”.

Speaking about the second victim, Dott said he was “never in my company” and denied all allegations of abuse.

open image in gallery Graeme Dott won snooker’s world championship at The Crucible in 2006

In her closing speech on Friday, Ms Dalziel called on the jury to find Dott guilty of both charges.

She said: “The Crown’s case is that Graeme Dott subjected vulnerable children to the worst kind of abuse with a course of conduct which relied on opportunity, for his own gratification.”

Dott’s lawyer, Euan Dow, had invited jurors to clear his client of both charges.

But Dott was found guilty on Monday following the trial which began on Tuesday, 18 August.

“Ffs RKID announce the tour we’re all losing our minds.” So said the latest tantalising post from the world’s biggest wind-up merchant Liam Gallagher. Fans might stay sceptical... but could this in fact be the clearest indicator yet that another Oasis reunion is on the cards?

By now, a new tour might seem less of a surprise than those long-awaited 2025 shows. The rock band made history when brothers Noel and Liam Gallagher put an end to their years-long feud and reunited onstage for the first time in almost 16 years, to play a record-breaking world tour including a series of homecoming shows in Manchester.

Even before the 2025 tour concluded, fans predicted that Oasis would be keen to get back out on the road again, given the run of shows were a defining cultural event – as well as a very lucrative one. Oasis Live ‘25 was estimated by Forbes to have generated over $400m (£294m) in revenue, with Noel and Liam each pocketing between $50m-$100m. As a result, the pair cracked the Sunday Times Rich List this year with a combined net worth of $375m.

The Independent’s sources have said they understand that a Knebworth residency is on the cards but have yet to confirm any specific dates. This year marked the 30th anniversary of the band’s legendary Knebworth shows in 1996, where they played to a combined audience of 250,000 (more than four per cent of the population applied for tickets), including the rumoured 7,000-strong guestlist.

open image in gallery Oasis at Knebworth, August 1996 (Stefan Rousseau/PA) ( PA )

Sources have also said that Noel has been writing new music – it remains to be seen if this will emerge in the shape of the first Oasis album since 2008’s Dig Out Your Soul, with Liam on vocal duties.

Earlier this month, it was announced that SJM Concerts, the promoter behind the Oasis reunion tour, had secured a licence to host events at Knebworth indefinitely.

The promoter has also worked on shows with acts such as Take That and The Prodigy, as well as comedian Peter Kay.

The licence allows events for up to 125,000 people, with live music and dance performances permitted until 3am.

In July, The Sun claimed that Oasis would play six nights at Knebworth over a three-week period in September 2027. Meanwhile, the Manchester Evening News reported that same month that the rock’n’roll stars would headline 12 nights at the Etihad stadium, with an insider telling the paper: “It will be 12 nights at the Etihad Stadium across May and June. They could even add more dates to that as well, there's talk of up to 20. The wider tour is also going to include a return to Knebworth.”

Before that, there was speculation in 2024 – after the band announced their comeback tour – that they would return to the site. Oasis denied this on X in a statement that said: “Contrary to reports in some UK tabloid media today, Oasis will not be playing Knebworth Park in the future.”

The Independent has contacted Oasis’s representatives for comment.

open image in gallery Brothers Liam and Noel Gallagher during their 2025 reunion tour ( AFP/Getty )

Contrary to tabloid media reports, sources told The Independent that the mood backstage during Oasis’s 2025 reunion was jubilant, with both Noel and Liam in great spirits as their famous friends – from football stars to pop singers including Manchester City star Jack Grealish and the Happy Mondays’ Shaun Ryder – rubbed elbows.

“It’s been a proper love-in backstage,” one source said. “There’s a friends and family bar which is basically free booze – Guinness on draft (of course), beer, wine and champagne. It’s like going to a wedding every night.”

They continued: “Cast and Richard Ashcroft [Oasis’s support acts] are having the time of their lives – it’s been so nice to see Noel and Liam’s guests vibing off each other. Everyone’s been making new friends.”

And while it was true that Liam had left early each night – this was nothing to do with animosity towards his older brother and everything to do with him ensuring he was in peak condition for each concert.

“Liam has been completely zen, focusing on his voice and arriving shortly before each show then getting straight off to avoid temptation,” a source told The Independent.

The 2025 reunion tour is the subject of a forthcoming documentary directed by Peaky Blinders creator Steven Knight, due for release in IMAX cinemas on 9 September and on Disney+. Titled, Don’t Look Back In Anger, the film follows Noel and Liam, they undertake their Live ’25 tour, which kicked off just over a year ago in Cardiff.

A 46-second teaser trailer, released last month, showed cheering fans before cutting to footage of the Gallagher siblings backstage getting ready for their first shows together since their split in 2009.

“Oasis Live ‘25, one of the most anticipated rock ‘n’ roll comebacks of our time,” Disney+ said in a statement. “The film is an unapologetically uplifting account of the biggest musical event of 2025, capturing the experience and emotions of the band and their fans across the world.

“The unique perspective includes rehearsal, backstage, and onstage access as well as the first joint interviews with Noel and Liam in over 20 years.

When it comes to Glastonbury… Liam insisted over the weekend that an Oasis headline performance is “not happening” next year. Organiser Emily Eavis recently confirmed that all headliners have been booked.

As for a 2027 tour, for now, Oasis fans will just have to roll with it... the band are taking their time.

News.title: The science behind ‘lymphatic walking’ — and what it can do to reduce bloating
News.content:

Walking is having a wellness makeover on social media. The latest trend, “lymphatic walking”, involves swinging your arms more, maintaining an upright posture and taking deeper breaths while you walk. These actions are said to help move lymph around the body. Its followers claim it can reduce bloating and improve circulation, support immune function, and even help “flush toxins” from the body.

There is some science behind the idea. Our muscles already help move lymph every time they contract and relax. But what does the lymphatic system actually do, and can a particular style of walking really change how it works?

The lymphatic system is a network of vessels, tissues and organs that works alongside the cardiovascular system. Fluid is constantly moving out of tiny blood vessels into the tissues around our cells, and the lymphatic system’s main job is collecting this excess fluid and protein and returning it to the circulation.

It also supports digestion by absorbing dietary fats and fat-soluble vitamins from the small intestine, while intestinal lymphatic vessels interact with the gut microbiome and immune system, helping to maintain intestinal health and regulate inflammation.

open image in gallery The latest trend, “lymphatic walking”, involves swinging your arms more, maintaining an upright posture and taking deeper breaths while you walk ( Getty Images )

Beyond the gut, the lymphatic system plays an important role in immunity, transporting immune cells through lymphatic vessels and lymph nodes, where immune responses can be coordinated.

Unlike the cardiovascular system, though, the lymphatic system does not have one large central pump like the heart. Instead, lymph – a clear to straw-coloured, watery liquid – moves in several ways. Lymphatic vessels can contract on their own, but lymph flow is also driven by pressure changes from breathing and by the contraction and relaxation of surrounding skeletal muscles.

Our muscles act as pumps. As they contract, they compress blood and lymphatic vessels running through and around them. Combined with one-way valves inside these vessels, this helps move fluid forwards and, particularly in the lower limbs, upwards against gravity.

Second heart

The calf muscles are probably the best-known example. Each time we take a step, muscles in the lower leg contract and relax, helping to push blood in the veins back towards the heart. This is why the calves are sometimes described as a “second heart”.

But this effect is not limited to the calves, or to walking. Exercise can support lymphatic flow through skeletal-muscle contraction. Deliberately using muscles throughout the arms, legs and trunk while moving therefore has a sound physiological basis.

open image in gallery Calves are sometimes described as a ‘second heart’ ( Getty Images )

Breathing plays a role too. The diaphragm is our main breathing muscle, and every breath changes pressure within the chest and abdomen. Deeper diaphragmatic breathing creates larger pressure changes, which can help move blood and lymph from the lower body towards the chest and circulation. These pressure changes around the digestive organs can also help move food through the gut, supporting the circulation and lymphatic flow that transport absorbed nutrients and metabolic waste products.

So walking with more arm movement, taking deeper breaths and actively using more muscles is physiologically meaningful. The problem comes when this is presented as something unique or necessary to “activate” the lymphatic system.

About the author Hannah Campbell is a Lecturer in Applied Human Physiology | Researcher Female Health in Sports, Exercise & Physical Activity | Registered Clinical Exercise Physiologist, University of Leeds. This article was first published by The Conversation and is republished under a Creative Commons licence. Read the original article .

At the moment, there is no clear evidence that lymphatic walking is better than ordinary walking for healthy people. The specific combination of arm swinging, posture and breathing being promoted online has not been shown to provide special detoxifying, fat-burning or immune-boosting effects.

However, the broader idea – moving purposefully, engaging more muscle and breathing more deeply while doing so – does make physiological sense.

Exercise is already an important part of managing lymphoedema, a condition where the lymphatic system cannot drain fluid effectively and swelling develops. Muscle-pumping exercises, including walking, can help support this drainage.

For most people, though, the useful message is probably not that they need to start lymphatic walking. It is to make every movement count.

Walking, climbing stairs, dancing, strength training, swimming, gardening or running all involve repeated muscle contraction. Even simply getting up after sitting for a long period activates muscles that have been relatively inactive.

Actively engaging with movement may also have benefits that extend well beyond lymphatic flow.

Regularly and deliberately using our muscles helps maintain strength and physical function, while also supporting cardiovascular, metabolic and mental health. Over time, this can help build greater physical resilience and reduce vulnerability to injury, illness and loss of function.

The best thing most people can do for their lymphatic system is therefore much less complicated than this wellness trend makes it sound: move regularly, purposefully and often. Every step, stretch and muscle contraction counts.

News.title: What happens when someone goes overboard on a cruise ship?
News.content:
