It is rare for anyone to fall off a cruise ship, but incidents attract plenty of attention when they unfortunately do happen.

In the latest case, Ambassador Cruise Line’s Ambition cruise ship was sailing in the North Sea on 21 August and discovered that a passenger was missing. A man’s body was later found.

There have been nine “man overboard” cases so far this year, according to Cruise Junkie, a media monitoring site. This includes passengers and crew members who have fallen overboard.

Other high-profile incidents this year include a 77-year-old woman who went overboard from Holland America Line’s Nieuw Statendam cruise ship on New Year’s Day during a Caribbean cruise. The search was abandoned after eight hours, with the passenger still missing.

There were 12 cases in 2025. These included a five-year-old girl who fell from the fourth deck of Disney Dream as it sailed back from the Bahamas to Florida. Her father jumped off the side and managed to grab her and tread water until they were rescued by the ship’s crew after nine minutes.

In another case, Kimberly Burch, fiancée of Faster Pussycat singer Taime Downe, died after she fell overboard from a Royal Caribbean 1980s-themed cruise from Miami in March.

Passengers should not, however, be deterred.These cases are very much in the minority and cruise lines have strict measures in place to keep people safe and help launch a rescue when there is a man overboard.

Andy Harmer, director of the Cruise Lines International Association (CLIA), told The Independent: “A cruise holiday is one of the safest forms of travel. Cruise ships today are the safest that ever sailed, thanks to the rules, regulations and technological innovations that govern their design. There are no known cases of someone acting responsibly who has accidentally fallen over the railing of a cruise ship.”

How often do people fall off cruise ships?

Of all the announcements you may hear on a cruise, “Code Oscar” can be one of the most alarming for passengers and crew.

This message alerts crew members when someone falls off a cruise ship.

Data from the CLIA shows that between 2009 and 2019, there were 212 man overboard incidents on cruise ships. That works out to roughly 19 each year.

More recent figures from the Cruise Junkie site for between 2000 and the end of August 2026 puts the figure at 440. This is still a tiny amount compared with the 32 million passengers who typically go on a cruise each year.

Cruise blogger Emma Le Teace, who runs the Emma Cruises YouTube channel, says this makes the chance of falling overboard on a cruise around one in 1.4 million.

Can you fall off a cruise ship?

Research by the CLIA shows that every man overboard incident recorded between 2009 and 2019 was found to be an “intentional or reckless act.”

Legal expert Brad Huffman adds that cruise line liability can be complicated if there is a man overboard incident.

He said: “While they have a legal duty to maintain passenger safety, cruise line liability is often capped by the fine print in their ticket contracts, which few passengers fully read or understand.

“Maritime law gives them a certain amount of leeway, so a family’s options for seeking compensation can be limited.”

Some cases have resulted in legal action.

One family is suing Royal Caribbean after their mother fell overboard on one of the cruise line’s Taylor Swift-themed cruises in October 2024. Dulcie White, 66, fell overboard and vanished on 22 October 2024, while the other guests partied through the night. The family blames for cruise line for continuing to serving her drinks despite her reportedly slurring her words and struggling to stand up.

open image in gallery If you see someone in the water, throw a lifebuoy to help them float ( Getty/iStock )

What happens if you see someone fall off a cruise ship?

One of the first things you will be asked to do on a cruise ship is attend a safety briefing or watch a video that explains what happens if there is an issue.

The procedure across most ships if you see someone fall into the water is to shout “man overboard”.

For example, Princess Cruises advises guests in its pre-cruise pack to alert a crew member if someone goes overboard and throw a lifebuoy or anything that will float.

Some cruise ships have sensor systems to detect if someone goes overboard, while ships that go in and out of US ports with more than 250 passengers are required to have cameras so someone can be easily located if they fall.

The general procedure if someone falls off a cruise is to stop the ship, while outer decks may be closed.

Rescue boats will enter the water and the coastguard will be contacted, while other nearby ships will also be notified to keep a lookout.

Unfortunately, CLIA data shows that out of the 212 incidents between 2009 and 2019, just 48 – or 28.2 per cent – ended in a successful rescue.

What safety measures are in place to stop people falling off a cruise ship?

The rescue rate may look scary but it is pretty hard to fall off a cruise ship.

The vessels may be getting taller and more intricate, such as Royal Caribbean’s Legend of the Seas, but all ships are designed with safety in mind.

The outer decks have glass-panelled railings, which must be at least 42 inches tall, while balconies must be at least one metre high.

Harmer adds: “Cruise lines are highly regulated with robust enforcement. The average ship undergoes dozens of announced and unannounced safety inspections per year, involving hundreds of man hours and covering thousands of specific requirements set by the International Maritime Organisation.”

Passengers, of course, have to be responsible and avoid dangerous acts such as climbing over balconies and running on slippery decks, especially after a few drinks, but in most cases you should be able to have a smooth sailing without worrying about falling off a cruise ship.

President Donald Trump’s insistence that his $600 million White House ballroom is justified because of the security upgrades it will bring is undermined by the fact that the complex already has a secret bunker, according to former officials.

The Washington Post cites three ex-officials who point to the existence of the nuclear-proof underground base as a basis for rejecting Trump’s case for proceeding with his pet project.

The bunker was commissioned in response to the 9/11 attacks and completed during Barack Obama’s tenure to keep the commander-in-chief safe.

It is reportedly situated 60 feet below street level, is accessible by private elevator, stores a month’s supply of food, has its own air supply system and is intended to shield its inhabitants from a range of threats, including the blast of a weapon of mass destruction.

It was itself constructed as a successor to the existing Presidential Emergency Operations Center in the basement of the East Wing, which was built to protect Franklin D Roosevelt in the Second World War and served to safeguard first lady Laura Bush and vice president Dick Cheney when al-Qaeda struck 25 years ago.

open image in gallery The existence of a secret bunker beneath the White House undermines the case for President Donald Trump’s $600 million ballroom in place of the East Wing, ex-officials have argued ( Reuters )

The unnamed former officials told The Post the arguments put forward for the bunker during the War on Terror are similar to those being made by the Trump administration now to explain the need for the new ballroom, raising questions about whether the latter is really essential.

“The East Wing Modernization Project is inextricably tied to the security of the president, the White House grounds and the certain security infrastructure assets,” White House spokesman Davis Ingle countered in a statement to The Independent.

“Recent events such as the foiled attack on the historic UFC Freedom 250 event at the White House proves exactly why the East Wing Modernization Project is severely needed for large scale events, which include drone-proof structures and drone ports among other critical security enhancements.”

The fate of the construction project currently sits with the U.S. Supreme Court. Chief Justice John Roberts issued an order Friday allowing work to continue while his bench considers an emergency appeal arguing that it must be halted unless congressional approval is granted.

Both a U.S. district judge and a federal appeals panel have found that the support of a majority of lawmakers in the House of Representatives and Senate is required before the undertaking can proceed but did make an exception for the planned subterranean military complex.

open image in gallery Work is currently continuing on the project but its future ultimately rests with the Supreme Court ( Reuters )

White House Deputy Chief of Staff Stephen Miller said in an August filing that the proposed complex “serves continuity-of-government interests by ensuring that the president and senior national security staff are able to operate from a protected facility during any attack on the nation’s capital.”

Army Secretary Dan Driscoll has similarly claimed: “Securing this reinforced subterranean node guarantees uninterrupted command and control in place.”

Driscoll called it “a nondiscretionary prerequisite to ensure the president can maintain continuity of government, uninterrupted operations, and effectively exercise National Command Authority during an attack or global crisis.”

open image in gallery Trump has enthusiastically promoted his ballroom project since its inception ( AFP/Getty )

Lawyers for the White House told the Supreme Court earlier this month the complex is 65 percent complete and that a 250-strong construction crew was working on it 20 hours per day, seven days a week to get it done.

Trump himself has meanwhile claimed that opposition to the project is “disloyal” and attacked the National Trust for Historic Preservation, the organization tasked by Congress with preserving D.C. institutions and landmarks, for challenging the ballroom in court, suggesting their lawsuit risked compromising national security.

“I said the problem with the suit – I told them this – is that we have many military things in this ballroom, and ideally, they shouldn’t be revealed,” he complained in the Oval Office last week.

“But now they are revealed, so the world knows about it.”

News.title: English cricket’s latest shame raises deeper question about sport’s relationship with alcohol
News.content:

One need not be an expert in crisis communications to know that seeing the words “nightclub incident” in a headline for the third time in nine months is far from ideal. After Harry Brook, Jacob Bethell and Josh Tongue in Wellington came Gus Atkinson and Ben Stokes in Chelsea and, now, Brydon Carse in Derby. And that’s without even mentioning the supposed mid-Ashes boozing of Noosa.

This England team simply don’t know how to get out of their own way. Two comprehensive Test wins this summer have each been overshadowed almost immediately by an off-field misdemeanour. Now, it is worth stressing that this latest fracas is distinct from the Stokes/Atkinson incident of June. While Carse ended up in handcuffs, he was released without charge after what is understood to have been a minor incident, one which occurred not on England time but while celebrating Durham’s County Championship success over Derbyshire. But come on, chaps, read the room – it was not even a fortnight ago that new captain Joe Root was telling his team to “be adults” after abandoning a curfew brought in after the Ashes.

Though this current crop of cricketers would be far from the first set of sportsmen to seek solace or celebration in a drink or two, the pattern here is one to cause concern. Clearly, it is tougher to keep a low profile in this age of near-constant social media surveillance; certainly when you are a strapping, six-foot-three fast bowler like Carse.

open image in gallery The latest incident is an unwelcome headache for new England captain Joe Root ( PA )

The profile of England’s squad has probably counted against them in some of the incidents, too, while their developing reputation creates something of a vicious circle. But it is surely fair to wonder if anyone is learning their lesson. One nightclub incident could perhaps be termed misfortune; three in such a short period not. These are not all callow adolescents, either. Would it be too much to ask that highly-paid professionals in their thirties not end up in these sort of environments with such regularity?

Both the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) and the Cricket Regulator continue their investigations. Internally, the handling of earlier incidents is understood to have caused some division. More broadly, though, there is a question about cricket’s relationship with alcohol.

Strolling into view in the background of the slightly grainy footage of a handcuffed Carse is Stokes, present after helping Durham to victory with a typically all-action showing with bat and ball. Asked recently about whether the England team from which he had retired had an issue with drinking, the former Test captain sought to turn the spotlight and scrutiny on the sport itself.

open image in gallery Ben Stokes retired from England duty in June ( PA )

“I think cricket has a drinking culture and that hasn’t changed,” Stokes said on the For the Love of Cricket podcast. “We are in 2026 now, where the game has gone more professional over the years, and one thing that has just stayed within cricket is its relationship with alcohol. From club cricket it works its way up. It has just stayed there and has been embedded within the sport.

“The relationship between alcohol and cricket is just something that hasn’t moved on as the game has become more professional. For people who think the English cricket team has a drinking culture, I would say no. I would just say cricket has a culture that is associated with alcohol.”

Anyone involved in cricket at just about any level will recognise Stokes’s comments. Recreationally, the two are intertwined; post-match pints, open clubhouse bars, alcohol-fuelled initiations. For a sport with so much involvement from communities that do not drink, more still needs to be done to find ways of divorcing cricket from alcohol.

open image in gallery Ben Stokes and Brydon Carse are Durham teammates ( PA )

In 2020, Essex captain Tom Westley apologised after squad member Feroze Khushi, a 21-year-old Muslim, had a beer poured on him while celebrating success in the Bob Willis Trophy on a balcony at Lord’s. Other, more concerning, stories from within club cricket followed. Long gone, maybe, are the days of David Boon wearing the 52 cans he allegedly drank on a flight from Sydney to London like a badge of honour, but even the end of James Anderson’s Test career was toasted with the seam bowler necking a pint of Guinness in front of a supporting throng of fans on the outfield.

At the professional level, scientists in sport are often surprised at how readily and regularly athletes will consume or glamourise alcohol. In elite environments, almost every element of a sportsperson’s life is micromanaged; every calorie counted, every physical effort measured. One nutritionist who has worked across a range of sports believes that the amount of drinking is lower than ever, yet still stands in contrast to development elsewhere.

“I am seeing a shift, and a trend [to limit alcohol],” the nutritionist explains. “The one thing we want them to do after a game is recover. Everything we provide for them after a game is anti-inflammatory so they can recover as quickly as possible. Alcohol is pro-inflammatory. It is poison that goes into the body. What I wouldn’t be doing is advocating going out having a beer, going and getting drunk. But the reality is these guys are human. I can’t sit there and say, ‘you are banned from having alcohol’.”

open image in gallery The England fast bowler Mark Wood is teetotal ( Getty )

While one would not expect a sweeping band of teetotallers – and Mark Wood is one notable recent example – it is perhaps surprising that there are not more, given the lengths certain individuals will go to with the aim of ensuring peak performance. Stokes would not necessarily be an abstemious sort, but he stopped drinking during 2025 as he recovered from a hamstring injury ahead of the Ashes. It would be naive to think that all would wish to follow a similar lead but perhaps desperate times may call for desperate measures.

News.title: Newcastle and Liverpool serve up thrilling tribute to Kevin Keegan
News.content:
It is fitting that Newcastle United vs Liverpool is a Premier League opening weekend fixture following the death of Kevin Keegan at the age of 75 last month.

All corners of St James’ Park will pay tribute and show their appreciation for the former player and manager who means a great deal to both sets of supporters.

Fans will find a printed message from the Keegan family on the back of black and white cards on their seat, which they will hold up to display a mural before kick-off.

As well as playing for both clubs, Keegan was Newcastle’s manager when they were beaten by a last-gasp Stan Collymore goal at Anfield in April 1996, a 4-3 defeat remembered as one of the great Premier League games.

This fixture usually delivers entertainment, and with new managers Matthias Jaissle and Andoni Iraola promising front-footed, ‘vertical’ football, there should be goals. That was certainly the case last August, when Newcastle fought back from two down with 10 men, before Rio Ngumoha scored a memorable winner.

It has been a summer of tumult for Newcastle, losing manager Eddie Howe, as well as key players Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes. There has been bullish talk of “Newcastle 2.0” from David Hopkinson, the club’s chief executive, and the club believe they have found a promising coach, but fans have understandably revised expectations downwards.

Liverpool are a difficult team to read; champions only 18 months ago but brittle last season, which resulted in Arne Slot’s dismissal. Iraola’s appointment is a shift back towards Jurgen Klopp’s style. That will be music to the ears of Anfield regulars, but holes remain in the squad. Central midfield has not been replenished; they need a Mohamed Salah replacement, and their strength at full-back is questionable. Much will depend on how 21-year-old central defender Jérémy Jacquet fares alongside Vigin van Dijk but he impressed in pre-season.



Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Frustrated Russell fails to make up ground as Norris wins incident-packed Dutch GP
News.content:
George Russell had another frustrating Sunday as the Dutch Grand Prix weekend slipped by with him failing to reduce his deficit to leader Kimi Antonelli. In a thrilling finale to the 72-lap race at the Dutch seaside, Lando Norris took his second victory in a row with two bold overtakes in one lap.

Yet compatriot Russell was irritated by Mercedes team orders for him to let Antonelli through into second place in the closing stages. It was a decision he believed risked a double podium for the team and threatened to put him even further behind his team-mate in the standings, with two charging Ferraris close behind. It was a race that, once again, fell away, despite Russell doing little wrong.

“Is he [Antonelli] fighting for the win or is he planning to catch Norris?” he asked, when the McLaren driver was 11 seconds down the road – the margin he would win by. “Yeah – we just lost a double podium here, mate,” was his response after moving aside.

Whilst Norris, who lost his lead from pole to Antonelli on the first lap, sealed the victory with two superb overtakes on lap 54 – first the Italian and then Lewis Hamilton – Russell had to mount a stout defence from Hamilton to secure third. It was against the odds, as both Ferraris, like Antonelli, were on fresh rubber after pitting under a late virtual safety car. Like Russell, Hamilton was critical of his team for their strategy choices.

Russell’s first podium finish since Silverstone – with his sprint victory on Saturday – means he at least retakes second place in the championship from Hamilton, but trails Antonelli by the same 59 point-gap he had after Hungary. That is despite him looking the faster and more comfortable Mercedes driver on Friday and Saturday.

News.title: Enzo Maresca tinkers his way to nervy Man City win
News.content:
Few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning. Enzo Maresca’s City started their Premier League season with a win, in the end, but three points masked the scale of the job he faces.

The narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image. That macro reading overlooks the number of distinct issues with City that Maresca must fix. A new midfield has to be recruited then blooded, a jittery defence needs settling down, and Phil Foden clearly requires help to recover the form which made him Premier League player of the year as recently as 2024.

All of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff. Josko Gvardiol scored an injury-time winner after City had trailed for most of the match, much of it a sloppy slog for the home side, who went behind in the 26th minute. The introduction of Rayan Cherki for Nico O’Reilly revived some familiar attacking effusiveness.

A lesser-spotted VAR-aided double celebration capped a tense but ultimately joyful day for Maresca. Marc Guéhi equalised from Cherki’s well-taken corner in the final minutes, then the expanded Etihad Stadium rapturously celebrated Gvardiol’s apparent winner, only to see it flagged offside. Video assistant Paul Howard intervened to show Gvardiol was onside from Cherki’s pass, before City’s fans, players and staff shouted twice as loud for twice as long to salute a morale-boosting victory.

News.title: How to spend a weekend in Lake Garda
News.content:
Lake Garda’s glittering wind-swept waters have long attracted poets, artists, writers and politicians, from DH Lawrence to Wolfgang Goethe – not least Mussolini, who ran the Italian Socialist Republic from the lakefront town of Salò on the western shore.

Fringed by the Dolomites to the north, Italy’s largest lake is Mediterranean both in feel and in flavour, with a mild, temperate climate and a decidedly slow pace of life. Hills are carpeted in olive trees and vineyards, while citrus groves are thick with plump, juicy lemons. In lakefront villages, restaurant tables spill out onto pretty waterfront squares, while boats zip across glimmering waters.

The lower basin is punctuated with sandy coves and gentle rolling hills, while travelling north, the lake takes on a new appearance, with hills replaced by sheer jagged cliffs that plunge into the waters. The northern shore is swept by mountain winds that create the perfect conditions for watersports, with windsailing, kitesurfing, and flyboarding making this a premier destination for outdoor enthusiasts.

News.title: How to spend a perfect weekend in Lake Como
News.content:
An hour drive north of Milan, Lake Como is the most glamorous of Italy’s lakes, hemmed in by the snow-capped Alps with picture-perfect villages on the water. Milanesi pop here for the day for a breath of fresh air and to soak up the fabulous vistas, while international visitors – the Clooneys, the Kennedys – have long been drawn by the grand lakefront hotels and the elegant mahogany Riva boats that zip along the lake’s deep blue waters.

Smart hotels and expensive boats aside, Lake Como is rich in culture, with opulent villas that once belonged to artists, writers, opera singers and explorers. Pliny the Elder, author of the first encyclopaedia, was born here, while 19th-century soprano Giuditta Pasta is known to have entertained composers Bellini and Donizetti in her lakefront residence on the eastern shore.

Though famous spots such as pretty Bellagio still pull in the majority of visitors, the lake has retained its authenticity, with plenty of sleepy fishing villages, such as Laglio, Torno and Nesso, home to rustic, family-run trattorias serving up traditional hearty fare, including risotto al pesce persico (risotto with perch).

News.title: Erling Haaland cuts off his trademark blond hair
News.content:
It is a new-look City in more ways than one this term with head coach Enzo Maresca looking to kickstart a new era following Pep Guardiola’s exit.

Maresca is hoping for an immediate return to form in City’s Premier League opener after a chastening 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in the Community Shield last week.

So far, only Elliot Anderson has arrived but Maresca is hopeful the club will be active in the transfer market. Rodri has left for Barcelona while Savinho is closing in on a move to Tottenham.

“I’ll try to find a new Rodri – it is what it is,” the former Chelsea manager said. “Rodri, before he arrived here, he didn’t win the Ballon d’Or, he didn’t win the Champions League, he didn’t win the Club World Cup. Then he joined the club and then after he achieved many important things. Now the target for us is to try to find the new Rodri.

“When David Silva was here, everyone was worried - Kevin [De Bruyne] arrived. When Sergio Agüero was here, everyone was worried – Erling [Haaland] arrived. When Ferdinando left, Rodri arrived. It’s just about this.

“When they leave, you need to be good and recruit the next one. They are all similar – David, Kevin, Fernandinho, Rodri, Agüero, Erling. It’s just normal, it’s a change. It’s not a problem, just go again and try to do the right things.”

News.title: Same old Spurs given reality check of epic proportions
News.content:
The players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur. The same Tottenham that finished each of the last two seasons in 17th. The same Tottenham that folded in adversity. The same Tottenham that opposition fans loved to laugh at.

Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.

But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.

The Spurs supporters who have become sick of being made the butt of their rivals’ jokes had to listen to Brentford fans singing “Thomas Frank, he’s laughing at you” in reference to the Dane’s unhappy spell in north London.

The impending arrival of Savinho will take Tottenham’s spending over £300m, but none of their big-money debutants at the Gtech Community Stadium hit the ground running.

There was only one man who looked anything close to a £100m player and it was not Sandro Tonali.

Tottenham’s first-ever £100m signing was completely upstaged by Brentford’s Mamadou Sangaré on his first competitive start for the club, as Spurs were run ragged.

News.title: All Blacks stun Springboks in statement win
News.content:
Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry did not begin with the year’s greatest game, but a New Zealand victory against the odds, at high altitude in Johannesburg, has poured intrigue and interest on to a series which was already brimming with them.

The All Blacks’ recent record at Ellis Park, the Springboks’ spiritual home, is by no means shabby – this was their fourth victory from the last six visits – but few fancied Dave Rennie’s galvanised Kiwis on Saturday, against the back-to-back world champions, after a week which had been dominated by chat of officials and law interpretations.

Yet, this stunning victory was almost as comfortable as it was surprising. New Zealand outscored their hosts by five tries to one and, by the end, a 13-player Springboks outfit – both Marco van Staden and Cobus Reinach were sin-binned within a minute of each other – were left chasing shadows in an Ellis Park which had been stupefied into silence.

It was at the beginning of that 13-player period when New Zealand put the game to bed, with Will Jordan crossing for his second try. But the damage had already been done by a cast of Kiwi conquerors. Ardie Savea, captain and No 8, could not have delivered more for the cause; Luke Jacobson and Tupou Vaa’i on the flanks were more than deputies to Savea; the locks, until Josh Lord’s unfortunate departure just before half-time, were magnificent; and, behind them, Cam Roigard continues to look every bit the equal of those phenomenal French scrum-halves. The New Zealand midfield got the upper hand on their much vaunted counterparts, too, on the day of Damian de Allende’s 100th cap for South Africa.

Sports.title: Arsenal discover Julian Alvarez price tag as Atletico Madrid perform U-turn on transfer
Sports.content:
Arsenal discover Julian Alvarez price tag as Atletico Madrid perform U-turn on transfer

Julian Alvarez endured a frosty reception during Atletico Madrid's opening game of the season as his side refuse to sell to Barcelona, but Arsenal remain in the wings

View 2 Images Arsenal remain interested in Julian Alvarez with Atletico Madrid refusing to sell to a La Liga rival

Atletico Madrid internally believe that the only way Julian Alvarez will leave this summer is if Arsenal sign him - despite previously being adamant he wouldn't be sold.

‌



Alvarez faced a hostile reception as Atletico played at home over the weekend with the Argentine making it clear that he wants to leave the Spanish capital. He's made it known, without naming them, that his "dream" would be to join Barcelona.

‌



Atletico though are adamant they will not sell to a fellow La Liga rival, which leaves Barcelona's hopes of signing the forward extremely unlikely. Real Madrid expressed an interest earlier this summer, but Atletico didn't believe their offer to be genuine.

‌



Arsenal are the only non-Spanish side interested as they look to add star quality in the final third. The Athletic has been told that the only scenario Atletico foresee which ends with Alvarez leaving would be if Arsenal made a €150million (£128m) offer.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

It appears unlikely that the Gunners, despite their continued investment in their squad, would table such a bid. Arsenal have Viktor Gyokeres and Gabriel Jesus as genuine No.9s, although the latter is tipped to leave. Kai Havertz is more of a false 9 and is currently the preferred option to lead the attack.

‌



Gary Neville claimed on Sky Sports that adding Alvarez would see the likes of Martin Odegaard go to another level, given the way the Argentine would change the dynamic of the team's attack.

Despite the toxicity that was evident during Atletico's clash at the weekend, Diego Simeone underlined the need for the club to be united if they want to win titles.

View 2 Images Arsenal have been linked with a move for Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez. (Image: (Photo By Oscar J. Barroso/Europa Press via Getty Images))

‌



He said: “I’m not here to give advice. What I have to do is concentrate on my work, which is, from a sporting sense, to give my best for Atletico Madrid. The only thing I know is that if Atletico Madrid want to win a title, we need to be together, we need to have forwards, and we need to have important forwards. And for that, we need to work on it as a result, everyone, on what we need.”

Goalkeeper Jan Oblak echoed that as he told DAZN: “Julian is here, he’s with us in the team and while he’s with us, we’re going to support him and we want him in the best way. Unfortunately, it’s a situation that isn’t comfortable for anyone, but hopefully all that is sorted out and at the end of the season we can all be happy.”

Atletico’s refusal to engage in talks with Barcelona has forced their sporting director Deco to eye up other striking options. Last week he maintained that the Catalans would sign a striker, especially after the departures of Robert Lewandowski and Ferran Torres.

Article continues below

He told local outlet TV3: “We have solutions in the team (for the central striker role), but we will probably make a move before the end of the transfer window." Reports claim Inter Milan’s Lautaro Martinez is on their shortlist, but the Italian side see their captain as an unsellable asset.

Sports.title: Atletico Madrid dressing room stance on Julian Alvarez transfer noise as Arsenal chase heats up
Sports.content:
Atletico Madrid dressing room stance on Julian Alvarez transfer noise as Arsenal chase heats up

Arsenal transfer target Julian Alvarez was booed on his return to action for Atletico Madrid with Jan Oblak speaking out on his situation

View 2 Images Julian Alvarez has the support of the Atletico Madrid squad after being booed amid his uncertain future (Image: (Photo by Alberto Gardin/NurPhoto via Getty Images))

Julian Alvarez has the support of the Atletico Madrid squad according to goalkeeper Jan Oblak after he was booed on his return. The Arsenal transfer target has been pushing for a move away but Atletico have no plans to sell to his dream club Barcelona which has opened the door for a return to the Premier League.

‌



The Argentine was absent for their La Liga opener earlier this week but was named in the squad for the visit of Villareal. Diego Simeone brought him on in the second half with Atletico scoring a late equaliser in front of their home supporters.

‌



While the majority of Atletico's players went around the pitch and clapped their fans, Alvarez was instructed to leave the pitch. As he trudged down the tunnel accompanied by club officials, he was heavily booed and jeered.

‌



Oblak has now spoken out on the incident and his future while also confirming he has the support of Atletico players despite the uncomfortable situation.

He told DAZN: "We all need to be united. Julian is here, he's with us in the team and while he's with us, we're going to support him and we want him in the best way.

"Unfortunately, it's a situation that isn't comfortable for anyone, but hopefully all that is sorted out and at the end of the season we can all be happy."

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

When pressed about the whistles directed at Alvarez and what advice he might offer him, Diego Simeone said: "I'm not here to give advice. What I have to do is concentrate on my work, which is, from a sporting sense, to give my best for Atletico Madrid.

"The only thing I know is that if Atletico Madrid want to win a title, we need to be together, we need to have forwards, and we need to have important forwards. And for that, we need to work on it as a result, everyone, on what we need."

‌



View 2 Images Atletico Madrid boss Diego Simeone has spoken about the Julian Alvarez situation

Simeone also disclosed that the decision to prevent Alvarez from approaching the home supporters came from senior figures at the club.

He added: "People at the club told me that the club decided he shouldn't go near the stands or the fans. It was the club's decision to keep him away and separate him so he could go to the locker room."

Article continues below

Atletico have no intention of selling to Barcelona and would apparently only authorise a transfer to Arsenal for a nine-figure sum.

The Gunners seem unlikely to meet that valuation, but offloading Gabriel Martinelli to Al Hilal for a record fee could provide them with sufficient funds to table a bid that Atletico might accept, given the Alvarez situation is becoming increasingly difficult to manage.

Sports.title: Anthony Gordon makes immediate impact on Barcelona debut as he hails 'dream' start
Sports.content:
Anthony Gordon makes immediate impact on Barcelona debut as he hails 'dream' start

Anthony Gordon came off the bench to make his debut for Barcelona away to Elche on Sunday, providing two assists in the space of four minutes in a thumping 5-0 victory

View 2 Images Anthony Gordon didn't take long to show what he can do (Image: Francisco Macia/Getty Images))

Anthony Gordon enjoyed a 'dream debut' for Barcelona on Sunday, as the England star made an instant impact. Gordon, 25, joined Barca in June for a cool £70million after three-and-a-half successful years at Newcastle.

‌



The winger started on the bench as Barcelona began their La Liga title defence with a trip to Elche. Ex-Leeds forward Raphinha broke the deadlock with 14 minutes on the clock before summer signing Karim Adeyemi, preferred to Gordon in the starting XI, doubled Barcelona's lead on the brink of half-time.

‌



Gordon entered the fray shortly after the hour mark and only needed two minutes to set Raphinha up for his second of the night. Four minutes later, Gordon burst through on goal but had Fermin Lopez alongside him.

‌



The 25-year-old unselfishly chose to pass, giving his team-mate a simple finish. Lopez then made it 5-0 in the closing stages to bag himself a brace.

Gordon was asked after the win whether it was a 'dream debut' for both him and Adeyemi. "Of course," he replied. "I think you always want to win. It's always about the team first, especially with this club.

"But big congratulations to Kareem because he performed a great performance. He got his first goal. He worked really hard in some defensive transition. So, really happy for him."

Gordon seems to have already settled in Barcelona, too, saying: "I feel so good since I've arrived. I said in in the interview then that the guys have made me feel so welcome. I feel at home already. The city is amazing. The the people are so friendly and I think I would get better and better the longer I'm here."

‌



Will Anthony Gordon be a success at Barcelona? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

Reflecting on the victory, he added: "It was a top performance. I think it was the perfect start, five goals scored and none conceded. We played some lovely football, scored great goals and, more importantly, I thought the defenders made some excellent last-minute challenges and blocks."

‌



Hansi Flick was also pleased with his side's display, having won the La Liga title in each of his two seasons in charge. "We're delighted with the fantastic start we've made; it gives us confidence," the German said.

"I'm pleased with the 5–0 win and the three points. I was concerned about turnovers. We had to control the ball, and in the end, a clean sheet is fantastic, and five goals is great."

Barca's next game is at home to Athletic Bilbao on Thursday. Gordon will have the chance to play a competitive match at the Camp Nou in Barcelona colours for the first time.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher adamant Liverpool tactic 'cannot work' as issue rears its head
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher adamant Liverpool tactic 'cannot work' as issue rears its head

Jamie Carragher has called out Liverpool's midfield after Newcastle continued to catch them out on the counter attack with the former Red citing it as an issue for some time

View 2 Images Jamie Carragher has continue to flag issues with the Liverpool midfield (Image: (James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images))

Jamie Carragher continued to bemoan the make up of Liverpool's midfield during their draw at Newcastle insisting it "cannot work" given the players they pick.

‌



The Reds needed a last minute penalty to rescue a 2-2 draw, but were behind for the majority of the contest at St James' Park. Both Newcastle goals were scored on the counter attack with pace and direct running cutting through Liverpool on the transition.

‌



Andoni Iraola started with Florian Wirtz as his 10 and Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai sitting in behind. The Reds have lacked a natural defensive midfielder for several years, and their issues with containing quick breaks has been apparent since last season.

‌



Newcastle were able to expose those and Carragher was left frustrated, insisting the problems were clear to see in pre-season and will remain whilst Liverpool continue to play with their current three-man midfield.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

After Anthony Elanga put Newcastle in front after four minutes the Sky Sports pundit said on social media: "LFC midfield all bombing forward happened all pre-season, madness!"

‌



Yoane Wissa was allowed to travel almost half the pitch before laying on Joe Willock to put Newcastle ahead, and Carragher was seemingly repeating himself. He posted: "Again! This midfield cannot work, I said it before a competitive ball was kicked."

Back when Liverpool were winning the Premier League and Champions League under Jurgen Klopp they had a midfield that consisted of Fabinho, Georginio Wijnaldum and Jordan Henderson, which gave the team the balance they were looking for.

View 2 Images Newcastle enjoyed success on the counter attack

‌



They have all departed Anfield and Carragher has been flagging for some time that Liverpool no longer have the profile of midfielder who is more defensive. Instead, he called out the amount of attacking players in their starting XI and claims top teams don't operate with the end-to-end style that is often seen in Liverpool games.

"Liverpool have too many attacking players on the pitch, they just want to bomb forward," he said on the Overlap before the season kicked off. "And it’s the same in pre-season at Liverpool this season - it’s just a basketball game. No top team plays football like that. I don’t believe it."

Sports.title: Unai Emery makes Ollie Watkins feelings clear after star missed Aston Villa's drubbing
Sports.content:
Unai Emery makes Ollie Watkins feelings clear after star missed Aston Villa's drubbing

Ollie Watkins was left out of Aston Villa's squad to face Brighton on Sunday, with the 30-year-old pushing to join Saudi Arabian side Al-Hilal before the transfer window closes

View 2 Images Unai Emery's response - or lack thereof - was telling (Image: Stan Sport)

Unai Emery hinted that Ollie Watkins refused to play in Aston Villa's humiliating 4-0 defeat to Brighton as the saga surrounding the striker's future turned sour. Watkins, 30, was absent for Sunday's drubbing, with Villa conceding all four goals inside the opening 31 minutes before going down to 10 men.

‌



It was a nightmare start to a Premier League season ahead of which Villa have lost several key players. Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans, Morgan Rogers and Lucas Digne have all left the Europa League winners for pastures new.

‌



And their rebuild looks set to get even tougher, as Watkins pushes to join Al-Hilal. The Saudi Pro League side have agreed personal terms with the England international, although they've seen four bids rejected.

‌



Al-Hilal's most recent offer came in at £45million and it's thought that £50m would be enough for Villa to accept. But Emery said that 'silence' was the best way to respond to questions regarding Watkins' future and whether he refused to be involved on Sunday.

"This question is for him," the Villa manager replied. "I can answer only with my silence. I think you can call him and you can call his agent and he can respond. He can only explain his answer, I can't.

"The players here show their commitment and that is really fantastic. This is the way."

Watkins' absence left Emery without a recognised striker, with Brian Madjo having picked up an injury. Emiliano Buendia was used as a makeshift centre forward against Brighton, who steamrolled Villa.

‌



When asked about the situation, Emery added: "Two strikers are injured and another striker gives his answer."

The Spaniard went on to say: "This problem [with the transfer market] we had every season and every season we overcame it. It's something we have to accept and always we reacted, especially the players.

"This is something hard for us every year but we are calm. With this result, it's more difficult to explain but calm, work, be positive and find solutions for the next week and after the transfer window."

In his pre-match press conference on Friday, Emery made it clear that he didn't want to sell Watkins. "We have an issue with him, it's clear," he admitted.

"He is our player. We have had offers for him, I don't want to sell him but it can change because if it's a good option for him and the club and I can replace him in the squad, this is the routine we have and we did before with the players who are leaving."

Sports.title: UEFA chief Aleksandr Ceferin destroys Gianni Infantino over FIFA sale saga – 'Plan is dead'
Sports.content:
UEFA chief Aleksandr Ceferin destroys Gianni Infantino over FIFA sale saga – 'Plan is dead'

Gianni Infantino has come under increased scrutiny since the 2026 World Cup after controversially plotting to sell stakes in FIFA competitions to private investment firms before he backed down

View 2 Images Aleksandr Ceferin and Gianni Infantino do not see eye to eye (Image: Nick Potts/PA Wire)

UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin has hit out at Gianni Infantino over his ill-fated plan to sell stakes in FIFA competitions to private investment firms. The Swiss Italian is under growing pressure after his controversial idea sparked global outrage.

‌



The move saw European football's governing body, UEFA, threaten to boycott all FIFA events, including the World Cup. Infantino was eventually forced to withdraw his plan, but pressure on the 56-year-old has not gone away.

‌



UEFA were joined by Concacaf, the federation for football in North and Central America and the Caribbean, as well as the Asian Football Confederation (AFC), in a joint letter accusing FIFA of a "fundamental breach of trust" and "deception".

‌



Trent Alexander-Arnold delivers brutal verdict on World Cup sell off plan READ MORE :

Jean-Philippe Mateta calls in FIFA in bid to rip up Crystal Palace contract READ MORE :

European football's governing body has since said it has lost confidence in Infantino, while the football associations of all the home nations have withdrawn support for the former UEFA general secretary.

And Ceferin has spoken strongly to the Rest is Politics podcast on why Infantino's decision was so flawed. The Slovenian believes it was worse than the controversial European Super League plan, which saw Europe's biggest club sides threaten to break away before it collapsed in April 2021.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



He said: "I think this plan is even worse than the Super League plan.

"Super important clubs wanted to do their own league, which is wrong, and would destroy football. But in this case, football would be literally sold.

"I'm absolutely sure that the plan is dead. It's hard to to imagine what kind of people would sell the sport that belongs to everyone. We will not allow that to happen."

‌



View 2 Images Gianni Infantino has come under criticism (Image: Nick Potts/PA Wire)

Ceferin claims that UEFA had no prior knowledge of Infantino's plan. The 58-year-old says he learned about it through the media while on holiday with his family.

"He didn't contact me since this happened," Ceferin said. "They [FIFA] play on, you know, '[how] arrogant Europe is against us: They have enough money, but I help the small and the poor'.

‌



"But I think someone should remind him that he is a European, and that he was supported by UEFA, which he forgot."

Questions are now being raised over a potential successor to Infantino ahead of FIFA's presidential election in March. However, Ceferin has ruled himself out.

"I'm not interested because of two reasons," the UEFA president said. "One reason is that I love UEFA and I love working here, and I think that at a certain point it's time also to enjoy life a bit.

‌



"And the second point is, my credibility is much, much, much higher if I'm not interested in the position."

Infantino has also come under pressure over his closeness to United States President Donald Trump. Sports.title: Lewis Hall transfer response live on TV shows Newcastle's true stance over Man Utd move
Sports.content:
Lewis Hall transfer response live on TV shows Newcastle's true stance over Man Utd move

Newcastle United left‑back Lewis Hall has been linked with a move to Manchester United this summer, but the Magpies have stood firm

View Image Lewis Hall is wanted by Man United (Image: Getty Images)

Newcastle United boss Matthias Jaissle has dismissed talk of Manchester United chasing Lewis Hall insisting there is no substance to suggestions the defender has a chance of joining them. Former United star Peter Schmeichel told Magpies boss Jaissle about his old club eyeing the 21‑year‑old, and got a firm response.

‌



Schmeichel was on punditry duties for ViaPlay's coverage of Newcastle's 2-2 draw with Liverpool on Sunday and said: "We're [Man United] after your left-back."

‌



Jaissle initially misinterpreted the remark, before responding: "No chance! No chance!" The German could not have been more emphatic - Hall is not for sale. Hall remains one of the most highly regarded young full‑backs in the Premier League, widely viewed as a future England regular.

‌

His omission from this summer's England World Cup squad stunned many and only fuelled speculation over his future at St James' Park.

Reports have hinted at frustration on Hall's side, and with Michael Carrick actively seeking a new left‑back, United have been linked. But Newcastle's stance and Jaissle's tone suggest the noise around Hall may be running ahead of reality.

‌



Nevertheless, having already parted with Bruno Guimaraes, Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon, it's extremely doubtful Newcastle would offload Hall this summer, with merely days remaining of the window.

Carrick's side are seeking to strengthen the left-back position in their squad, but now appear as though they'll need to identify other alternatives. Barcelona defender Alejandro Balde is amongst those being touted for a switch to Old Trafford, and was notably absent from their squad for Sunday night's clash with Elche.

Barca manager Hansi Flick addressed that absence and said: "I spoke with Alejandro Balde today and said to him that I think you're not here 100%, so it's best that you stay at home and clear your mind. We will talk again tomorrow.

‌

"But I have NOT told Alejandro Balde to leave. I spoke with him this morning, I told him to think about it and that we'll talk again tomorrow."

Hall played the full match against Liverpool, but his afternoon soured when he brought down Victor Munoz in the penalty area.

Speaking on Sky Sports commentary duty, Gary Neville said: "There was no touch on the ball, and it looked like a penalty - and it is. Hall has been incredible but that is not going to be overturned.

"He’s got low, he’s been really sharp in his defending and in the final seconds… I think Hall knows deep inside that it was a penalty."

Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Alejandro Balde gives transfer green light and announcement imminent

Manchester United will look to bounce back from a Premier League opening day defeat to Hull City

Manchester United could have a busy week in the transfer window. Michael Carrick will need to shift focus back to improving his squad following a dismal away defeat to Hull City.

‌



The Red Devils were beaten 2-0 by the newly-promoted side thanks to goals from Nobel Mendy and Semi Ajayi. Carrick has admitted "disappointment" in the final result but insists the team will get back to their best soon.

‌



He said: "It's just one game, we're disappointed we haven't won. It's not more than that, it's not less than that. We've got to soak it up and come back stronger."

‌



The United boss will add yet another midfielder to his ranks this week after securing a long-term Premier League target. Carrick is also exploring his left-back options as one star says yes to joining the Red Devils.

Sports.title: Saints skipper Hastings gets three-game ban for punch
Sports.content:
St Helens captain Jackson Hastings' season could be over after being handed a three-match ban for violent conduct following his sending off in their win over Castleford Tigers on Saturday.

Hastings was dismissed in the first half of the 36-12 victory after punching Castleford's Tyler Dupree, who was sin-binned for the same incident.

Commenting on Hastings' dismissal, Castleford director of rugby Chris Chester told Sky Sports: "Scott Murrell just jumped (in the way of Dupree). We all know the rules, you can't punch people in the face."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Super League clash between St Helens and Castleford Tigers.

The win keeps Saints' play-off hopes alive, though they are currently on 28 points and seventh in the standings, one place outside of the play-off positions with three games to go.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player There were jubilant scenes at the full-time whistle as St Helens kept their play-off hopes alive with victory over Wakefield Trinity, with players and supporters celebrating together in the stands.

It means that should they fail to leapfrog one of Hull KR (sixth, 30 points), Leigh Leopards (fifth, 32 points) or Wakefield Trinity (fourth, 32 points) down the stretch, Hastings will have played his last match of the season.

Current Super League leaders Leeds Rhinos, as well as Wigan Warriors - tied on 38 points but with an inferior point differential - and Warrington Wolves, two back in third, have already qualified for the play-offs.

Sports.title: Why Celtic, Rangers, Hearts, Hibs, Motherwell face a make-or-break week
Sports.content:
All five of Scotland's European representatives are still standing as we prepare for the second legs of the play-off rounds, but only Celtic are guaranteed UEFA league phase action.

They have the cushion of Europa League football if they throw away their commanding lead against LASK in their Champions League tie, but there is no such comfort for Hearts, Rangers, Hibs and Motherwell.

The Jambos have already failed in their bid to qualify for Europe's top two club competitions, and need to win away to Rapid Vienna to secure a place in the Conference League.

Rangers are in the same situation, having crashed out of Europa League qualifying, meaning a place in the third-tier competition is their only chance.

Both Hibs and Motherwell have already come through two Conference League qualifying rounds. The Easter Road side are in a far better position than the Steelmen ahead of this week's games...

Will Celtic secure Champions League return?

Image: Celtic take a commanding lead into the second leg of their Champions League play-off

Just 12 months ago, Celtic failed to score in 210 minutes against Kairat Almaty before crashing out at the play-off stage on penalties.

What followed was a season of turmoil before Martin O'Neill returned to win a league and cup double. Now he has the Hoops on the brink of a return to Europe's elite competition.

The Champions League is all about big players producing big moments. Benjamin Nygren and Camilo Duran served up goals of the highest quality at a packed Parkhead to give them a commanding 3-0 first-leg win against LASK.

Image: Camilo Duran scored a stunning double against LASK

Duran scored five goals in the competition last season for Qarabag, and he is already proving he was worth the £6m fee.

The Colombian striker has pace and skill, and looked at home on the big stage. Fellow summer signings Mika Baur and Kasper Hogh also shone, with early suggestions this might be the summer the Hoops got their signings right.

Let's not forget Nygren, Celtic's top scorer last season. He opened the scoring, taking his tally for the season to four goals in four games.

O'Neill did urge some caution ahead of Tuesday night's game, with LASK showing enough to suggest it is not done yet.

If Celtic impress in attack again while avoiding any defensive lapses, the famous Champions League anthem will be back in Glasgow until after Christmas.

Can Hearts take another step towards becoming European regulars?

Tony Bloom has made no secret of his high hopes for Hearts.

The minority shareholder has already managed to split the Old Firm, and he has the Champions League in his sights.

Firstly, they have to qualify for the league phase of European tournaments regularly, and the Conference League is in their sights.

Image: James Wilson celebrates his goal against Rapid Vienna in the Conference League play-off first leg

Having failed to get past Sturm Graz in Champions League qualifying and Benfica in the Europa, they can still secure a place in the third-tier competition.

The Jambos take a 2-2 draw to Austria for the second leg of their play-off against Rapid Vienna on Wednesday night. To get through, they need to find their balance between attack and defence.

They have conceded 15 goals in European competition this season while scoring just four times.

The reward for that will be participation in the main phase of the Conference League for the third time in five seasons and, with it, a financial boost of at least £4m.

Can Rangers take last European chance?

Image: Ryan Naderi scored Rangers only going against Jablonec at Ibrox

Rangers manager Derek McInnes admitted his side will need to "be better" after their narrow 1-0 win against Jablonec in the first leg of their play-off.

Failure to reach the Europa League means the best the Ibrox side can achieve in Europe this season is the Conference League, a competition they have never played in before.

The boos rang out after a frustrating first half at Ibrox, but they did turn to cheers with Ryan Naderi's goal giving them hope heading into the second leg in the Czech Republic.

They did not make it easy for themselves, especially after Cammy Devlin's straight red card minutes after coming on, but the visitors never really troubled them.

Rangers dominated possession and had 13 shots on target compared to the opposition's five.

The fans will be hoping their failure to take chances does not cost them in the return leg as they aim to secure a ninth straight season competing on the European stage.

Historic season for Hibs?

Image: Hibs secured a goalless draw away to Gent

Hibernian are on the brink of club history - a first European league phase qualification.

A goalless draw away to Gent in the first leg of their Conference League tie has left them on the brink of securing a place in the league phase of the competition.

After beating KF Malisheva, and then seeing off North Macedonian outfit Shkendija over two legs, David Gray's side face the final hurdle of qualifying for the second straight season. Last season, they lost out to Legia Warsaw after extra time.

Image: Owen Elding missed an early penalty for Hibs

Hibs dealt well with the pressure in the away leg against Gent but were left to rue Owen Elding's first-half penalty miss.

The Belgian side, who have started their Pro League season with back-to-back wins, failed to pose any great threat to the Hibees, who will return to Leith believing this is their season.

Too late for Motherwell?

Image: Regan Charles-Cook gave Motherwell a dream start against Freiburg

When Regan Charles-Cook fired Motherwell ahead just two minutes into their tie against Freiburg, the Fir Park faithful probably started to dream of their first appearance in the group stage of European competition.

They caught the Germans out. However, when their opponents finally found their feet, they showed their own version of the attractive, free-flowing football the 'Well fans have become accustomed to under boss Alfred Johansson and his predecessor Jens Berthel Askou.

Image: It was a tough night for Motherwell against Freiburg in the first-leg of their play-off

Having reached last year's Europa League final, Freiburg spent a reported £30m in the close season and are one of those backed to go far in the competition.

They kept Motherwell goalkeeper Alex Paulsen busy. He impressed, but they still fell to a 3-1 defeat.

Freiburg were certainly worthy winners in Lanarkshire and will be overwhelming favourites to complete the job at the Europa-Park Stadion on Thursday.

Sports.title: Alvarez booed by Atletico fans amid Arsenal interest - so will he leave?
Sports.content:
Julian Alvarez was booed by Atletico Madrid supporters on Sunday after all the transfer window noise around him - does that mean a move to Barcelona or Arsenal is any closer?

The Argentine forward cut a disappointed figure when his own fans turned on him during Atleti's 2-2 draw with Villarreal.

And with Arsenal and Barcelona circling ahead of the September 1 deadline, what will happen now? Here is a state of play about the forward's future...
