Sports.title: Aston Villa fans turn on Ollie Watkins and wife Ellie after manager hinted he REFUSED to play to force £34m move to Saudi Arabia's Al-Hilal
Sports.content:
Aston Villa fans turn on Ollie Watkins and wife Ellie after manager hinted he REFUSED to play to force £34m move to Saudi Arabia's Al-Hilal

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Aston Villa fans have expressed their anger after Unai Emery hinted that Ollie Watkins refused to play amid speculation over his future.

Watkins, 30, was left out of Villa's squad for their 4-0 defeat by Brighton on Sunday in their first Premier League game of the season despite the club’s only other forwards, Brian Madjo and Tammy Abraham, being out injured.

Villa say they have rejected four offers from Saudi Pro League club Al-Hilal for Watkins, the latest of which is thought to be around £34million, a price the Premier League side will not sell at.

As far as Villa are concerned, it is understood Watkins is neither ill nor injured. However, he is not thought to have trained fully last week. Daily Mail Sport contacted Watkins' representative for comment on Sunday.

Speaking after the game on Watkins’ position, Emery answered: ‘This question is for him. I can answer only with my silence.’

Asked whether Watkins was refusing to play, Emery said: ‘I think you can call him, you can call his agent and he can respond. He can only explain his answer, I can’t. We had two strikers injured and another striker – it’s his answer.’

Aston Villa fans have hit out at Ollie Watkins (pictured with wife Ellie) amid speculation over his future

Several fans expressed their anger at Watkins amid reports linking him with a move away

And, following those comments, several Villa supporters hit out at Watkins.

Commenting on photos of him and his wife Ellie on her Instagram account, one fan said: 'Ellie please don't let Ollie leave please.'

Another added: 'Tell Ollie to not leave,' with a further fan saying: 'The kids are better in England. Please don't go.'

On Watkins' post of his family holiday in the Bahamas, several Villa supporters also commented by posting multiple snake emojis.

Another shared: 'Congrats on selling your soul Ollie,' before a further supporter said: 'Respect totally gone.'

A further infuriated fan added: 'Saudi? Why bro?'

Their frustration came after Villa put in one of their worst performances under Emery as a new-look side were torn apart by Brighton, with Joao Gomes sent off on his Premier League debut for the club as the Seagulls went 4-0 up in just over half an hour.

Due largely to UEFA financial rules, Villa have sold about £250million worth of talent this summer.

Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne and Ezri Konsa have all departed, and Watkins and Emi Martinez (another absentee on Sunday) could follow.

Saudi Pro League side Al-Hilal are said to have had four offers rejected for the English forward

All six were mainstays of the Villa team who beat Freiburg 3-0 in May to lift the Europa League.

Villa have often struggled when the transfer window is open and Emery joked: ‘I think the transfer window should always be closed.

‘In the last three years, until the transfer window closes, we have had problems like we are having now. The players have the mentality I want – not complaining, not blaming, and trying to be patient, even with results like today.

‘We have had this problem (with the window) every season and we overcame it. But it’s something hard for us every year.’

Sports.title: OLIVER HOLT: Michael Carrick should have been backed to the hilt by Man United this summer. Instead the club's dawdling and crowded hierarchy has hung him out to dry
Sports.content:
It was, Hull City manager Sergej Jakirovic said, as easy and relaxing for his goalkeeper as drinking a cup of afternoon tea. Of all the analysis of the lack of threat posed by the updated Manchester United side as they stumbled into the new season with a defeat on Humberside, it was the most damning assessment of all.

In a 2-0 loss at the home of a promoted team widely tipped to go straight back down, Michael Carrick’s team were outmuscled in defence, overrun in midfield and as meek as mewling kittens in attack. It was the equivalent of ‘can’t bat, can’t bowl, can’t field’ on a football pitch.

It is way too early to make sweeping predictions about where United will finish this season but there was widespread and understandable dismay about the level of the performance, and worrying signs of an apparent failure to build on the progress that Carrick made with the team last season.

United had momentum on their side in May. They finished third. They were back in the Champions League. With Pep Guardiola leaving Manchester City, it was predicted that they would be Arsenal’s closest challengers this season. Instead, there has been a creeping feeling throughout the summer that momentum has been lost.

There has been a feeling that, yet again, the manager of the football club has been let down by the crowded hierarchy above him in the food chain. United had a rare chance to build from a position of relative strength this summer and the mood music already suggests that they blew it.

Michael Carrick can only watch as his Manchester United team are taken apart by promoted club Hull City on Saturday

A side that cannot move on from Harry Maguire, who is 33, is a side with issues

If it is not yet another false dawn, then it is a missed opportunity. The summer was a time for United to make an impression. Instead, it feels as if they have stood still. Youri Tielemans is a fine player but he is not the midfielder who will make the difference between third place and champions.

Are either he or new arrival Carlos Baleba an improvement on Casemiro, who has departed for Major League Soccer? Baleba, who is set to sign from Brighton for around £70million, is a player of rich potential who should bring energy and bite but his progress stalled on the south coast last season.

His last-minute acquisition suggests either confused planning or thwarted ambitions elsewhere. So does the failure to strengthen a defence that was twice undone by set-pieces at the MKM Stadium and looks like a weirdly debilitating mixture of creakiness and naivety. A side that cannot move on from Harry Maguire, who is 33, is a side with issues.

When the big players moved this summer, United missed out. Elliot Anderson went to Manchester City, Morgan Rogers went to Chelsea, Bruno Guimaraes went to Arsenal, Anthony Gordon went to Barcelona, Marc Cucurella went to Real Madrid and Sandro Tonali went to Spurs.

It is hard to shake the idea that United have been left behind. Or at least caught dawdling on the start line. This was the summer they could least afford that to happen. They had a good summer last year when they overhauled their attack with a clutch of good signings but so far, this has been an underwhelming window. They have been feeding off scraps.

It has refocused attention on minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and his lieutenants, Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox, and a transfer policy that is starting to look flawed. They fixed the roof last summer and now they’re trying to install a new kitchen. But the foundations are built on shifting sands and they have ignored those completely.

After another tumultuous campaign last season, when Ruben Amorim was fired and Carrick performed such a fine rescue job, this was the summer when he should have been backed to the hilt and United should have shown the faith in him that his achievements in his four months in charge demanded.

Instead, it feels as if that support has been muted. The acquisition of Baleba is a step forward and United are now being strongly linked with Barcelona's 22-year-old Spanish left back Alejandro Balde, but they are shopping at John Lewis, not Harrods. It is hard to shake the feeling of anti-climax.

Youri Tielemans is a fine player but he is not the midfielder who will make the difference between third place and champions

United's summer signings, including Andrey Santos (right), feel underwhelming, as if the club is feeding off scraps

‘Come on, that’s ridiculous,’ Carrick said to former Middlesbrough and Swindon Town forward Jan Aage Fjortoft when Fjortoft, who is now an accomplished presenter for Viaplay, suggested that United had lacked Hull’s passion in the first half of the game on Saturday and conceded two goals before the interval.

It was rare to see Carrick bite like that. It did not feel like a loss of composure but more like a glimpse, ironically, of the passion that runs through him. He was right to stand behind his players, too: an away game at a newly promoted side in front of dedicated fans, hungry for a defrocking, has been the undoing of many an aristocrat.

United do not lack passion. But what is more worrying for Carrick is that they lack quality. They lacked the quality to withstand what Hull threw at them and they lacked the quality to offer more than the occasional threat to the newcomers’ defence. Konstantinos Tzolakis, the goalkeeper his manager referenced, supped on tea, not sympathy.

A beautiful tribute to King Kev

It has been, in many ways, an unnerving summer for the fans of Newcastle United. Liverpool supporters, too, are not quite sure what to expect after the arrival of a new manager to try to repair the disappointments of last season.

But all those concerns and even the result itself, a fittingly exciting 2-2 draw, were secondary to the tribute that the supporters of both teams provided for Kevin Keegan at St James’ Park on Sunday afternoon.

Keegan, who died last month, was one of the great figures of English football, a European Cup winner for Liverpool and a transformative character, both as player and manager, for Newcastle. He was adored in both cities and by both sets of fans.

And the joint farewell that the clubs gave him, both as a spectacle and in song, at their game was a beautiful and moving show of dignity and devotion to a man who brought so much joy to so many. Keegan represented much that was the best of our game and so did the tribute to him.

St James' Park nailed the tremendous and emotional tribute to Kevin Keegan on Sunday

Time running out for Wirtz

I want Florian Wirtz to succeed at Liverpool because I saw enough of him before his arrival in the Premier League to know that he is a sublime player.

Liverpool supporters did not see enough of that player last season, though, and he made an underwhelming start to the new season at Newcastle on Sunday.

Wirtz deserved the patience that was extended to him last season. He would not be the first player to struggle with the pace and the demands of English football. But time is running out for the £115million man to show what he can do.

Sports.title: A scary Alexander Isak issue, the punditry duo who outshone struggling Wayne Rooney and who from Man United's 'spine' is still on the beach? IAN LADYMAN on My Football Weekend
Sports.content:
A scary Alexander Isak issue, the punditry duo who outshone struggling Wayne Rooney and who from Man United's 'spine' is still on the beach? IAN LADYMAN on My Football Weekend

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Without doubt the worst moment of Liverpool's dismal title defence season came when Hugo Ekitike ruptured his Achilles at Anfield against PSG last April. Not only did it rule a talented forward out until 2027, it left Liverpool relying on Alexander Isak this season and that already feels scary.

Watching Isak at St James' Park yesterday was painful. Where once – during his time at Newcastle - there was certainty and instinctive confidence, there is now only hesitancy and doubt.

Isak used to take penalties for his old club but when Liverpool won one in the 96th minute yesterday, I almost hoped he wouldn't take it. He didn't.

But Liverpool need him. They really need him and that already feels like a problem for Andoni Iraola as he tries to navigate the early weeks of his time as Liverpool manager.

As Liverpool laboured in the latter stages against Newcastle, Isak offered absolutely nothing but he stayed on the field simply because Iraola didn't really have any other option.

Alexander Isak must succeed for Liverpool - their early season prospects depend on it

Last summer – the summer of 2025 – saw a number of No 9s arrive at our big clubs. Isak to Liverpool, Benjamin Sesko to Manchester United, Liam Delap to Chelsea and Viktor Gyokeres to Arsenal. None have had it easy so Isak is not alone.

Indeed as the Premier League returned this weekend, none bar Isak started for their teams. Sesko and Gyokeres were on the bench and Delap has been frozen out entirely by new coach Xabi Alonso at Chelsea.

The difference is that United, Arsenal and Chelsea have alternatives. They can afford to start their season with big name strikers as impact players. Iraola and Liverpool do not have that option.

Cody Gakpo – criminally under-rated by some members of the Liverpool fanbase – delivered with a big goal for Liverpool yesterday and could – at a push – play through the middle. Florian Wirtz – who faces challenges of his own at Anfield – could feasibly operate as a false nine. But neither is a convincing alternative.

What Liverpool really need is for Isak to start playing like a £125m centre forward – or indeed any kind of centre forward at all. Currently he looks miles off.

It was never going to be easy returning to St James' Park where even Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle was whipping up the crowd's vitriol towards a player who once scored 54 Newcastle league goals at more than a goal every other game.

It will feel more straightforward for him when Liverpool host Nottingham Forest at Anfield next Saturday lunchtime.

But at the moment Isak looks like a player who doesn't trust either his body or his mind and that has to change very soon.

Iraola doesn't have the option of asking him to find his form gradually. That was last season's luxury.

It really has to happen now. Liverpool's early season prospects may depend upon it.

Jaissle must look in the mirror

Newcastle coach Jaissle looks as though he will be a lively and entertaining presence on the touchline. But the German was wrong to blame referee Stuart Attwell for the late penalty decision that denied his team victory. The contact from the otherwise excellent Lewis Hall on Liverpool substitute Victor Munoz was clear.

Indeed Jaissle may wish to examine his own part in what happened given that the foul came in time added on by Attwell for a totally unnecessary Newcastle substitution.

Jaissle's decision to replace Yoane Wissa with Fabian Schar in the last minute of added time was clearly designed to waste some precious moments. But all it did was prompt Attwell to add 30 seconds on and it was after 15 of those that Munoz ran at Hall to win the spot-kick.

New guidelines this season mean that players must leave the field within 10 seconds of their number being raised or risk a booking. This means that the classic 'time wasting' substitution is even more pointless than ever.

Is MOTD losing its identity?

It felt strange to see Mark Chapman at Newcastle for Sky the day after he had hosted the season's opening Match of the Day. It is something that chips away a little at the identity of the BBC's flagship show.

TNT, meanwhile, chose to use The Athletic's ace news breaker David Ornstein as one of their pre-match panellists at the Hull-Man Utd game which felt a little like a desperate attempt to jump on the back of his enormous social media following.

As for Wayne Rooney, he continues to struggle to look truly comfortable in the MOTD chair. Joe Hart and Danny Murphy were on this occasion a better combination on the Sunday show than Rooney and Alan Shearer had been 24 hours earlier.

Joe Hart and Danny Murphy were better than Wayne Rooney and Alan Shearer as pundits

A wake-up call for Carrick

Michael Carrick will now know that it really feels like to be a Manchester United manager after his team's lame defeat on Humberside.

Last season was a free hit for Carrick after he succeeded Ruben Amorim as an interim at Old Trafford. Now that he has the job, it is completely different. This is his team and therefore his responsibility.

It was on the one hand hard not to admire Carrick's frankness in his post-match interviews.

When, for example, it was suggested by former Middlesbrough striker Jan Age Fjortoft – now an excellent analyst for foreign rightsholder Viaplay – that his team had lacked 'passion'. Carrick almost bit his head off.

'That is ridiculous,' said Carrick. 'You played football. You [should] understand.'

On the other, Carrick will soon come to learn just how every single word he utters – especially after defeat – will be picked apart by a fanbase that grows ever more impatient for a league title.

For example, he spoke ahead of the Hull game about his team's spine offering him cause for comfort only to see one of the players he name-checked – centre half Harry Maguire – start the season as though he was still on the beach.

The sooner central defenders learn to concentrate on the ball at set pieces the better. When the first Hull goal went in, for example, Maguire was still so intent on holding his man that he actually had both arms wrapped round team-mate Noussair Mazraoui.

It was schoolboy stuff.

Harry Maguire started the season as though he was still on the beach for Man United

Who can be the new Sunderland?

Hull's victory may yet transpire to be a rare highlight in a hard season but it is impossible not to be pleased for a group of supporters who have been through so much since they last watched Premier League football a decade ago.

Indeed both Hull and fellow promoted club Ipswich have followed Sunderland's example of last summer by recruiting heavily to try and repurpose themselves for top-flight football.

Sunderland fielded almost a new team as they flew high last season and a year on Hull have arrived in the Premier League with seven new players – three were in the team that beat United - while Ipswich fielded seven newbies as they beat the Wearsiders at Portman Road.

Ipswich are among the biggest spenders in the Premier League, having shelled out more than £150m. As Sunderland prepare to play European football this season, it seems they may have started something.

Savinho deal doesn't add up

Tottenham have also spent heavily but after their thumping at Brentford it may be a while until we see what they will actually look like under Roberto de Zerbi.

De Zerbi is still without a number of his best players – guys like Dejan Kulusevski, James Maddison, Micky van de Ven and Pedro Porro were not fit to start on Saturday – while one of his anticipated new signings – the Egyptian wide player Omar Marmoush – was actually on the bench for Manchester City yesterday.

So there is much still to come for Spurs fans even if there will be pressure on Tottenham's new executive team for their signings to work out.

Paying Newcastle £100m for Sandro Tonali feels rather top heavy but that pales when compared to the £75m Tottenham have agreed to give City up front for the Brazilian winger Savinho.

The 22-year-old arrived at the Etihad for £30m two summers ago and has made only a modest impact with two Premier League goals and twelve assists.

So who at Tottenham has decided that a 150 per cent increase on value feels like a good deal?

It already feels like one of the strangest transfers in recent Premier League history and if it doesn't work Spurs fans will want answers.

Roberto de Zerbi has seen a number of expensive additions arrive at Tottenham

Arteta spot-on with Martinelli

Arsenal's squad depth is increasingly impressive – the likes of Eberechi Eze, Noni Madueke, Max Dowman, Gyokeres and Martin Zubimendi were all on the bench as the champions beat Coventry – which is why Mikel Arteta feels comfortable in moving on Gabriel Martinelli.

Gunners legend Ian Wright claims Arteta's treatment of the Brazilian has been unnecessarily brutal. Martinelli was not involved at all on Friday or indeed at the Community Shield a week earlier.

But Arteta's track record at ruthlessly shipping players out when they have served their purpose is there for all to see.

The likes of Kieran Tierney, Granit Xhaka and Oleksandr Zinchenko all played significant roles in Arsenal's gradual return to eminence under the Spaniard. Indeed all three captained the club at some stage.

But all were invited to further their career elsewhere once their shelf life was reached. It can feel a little cold-hearted at times. But it has worked for Arsenal and that's what matters.

New hope for England

England assistant manager Anthony Barry – last seen struggling to hold back the tears at half-time of England's World Cup win over France – was on his native Merseyside to watch Everton down wasteful Crystal Palace and there was lots to take in.

A fabulous goal from the talented Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and an assured display from Adam Wharton will have reminded Barry and his boss Thomas Tuchel that it's possible to do something other than pack an England squad with wingers.

But Barry will also (hopefully) have noted a decent afternoon from talented Everton central defender Jarrad Branthwaite.

The Cumbrian is one of the most naturally gifted centre halves in England but has seen his progress stalled by injury. He is 24 now and it would help England enormously if he stepped up.

Ezri Konsa and new Manchester City 'midfielder' Marc Guehi (what on earth was all that about yesterday?) were very much 6/10 at the World Cup and could do with competition that isn't called Dan Burn.

Glasner needs history lesson

Former Palace manager Oliver Glasner is now at Nottingham Forest and that still feels like an odd swap, given Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis goes through managers like I go through tissues in hay fever season.

After an opening defeat to Leeds at the City Ground, Glasner suggested that it was impossible for him to suddenly make his team play like Real Madrid in the 1970s.

It was a strange thing to say, not least because Real were not winning big European trophies in that era.

A team who were? Forest, of course.

The club's two European Cup wins came in 1979 and 1980.

Oliver Glasner made strange comments about how Nottingham Forest could play

Still too many kid gloves

It was heartening to see a Premier League weekend pass without any notable VAR moments. Long may Howard Webb's 'high bar for intervention' continue. But he said this last season, too, and we know what happened.

Much of the responsibility for change continues to rest with the players, though, and that's particularly the case when it comes to all the messing about at corners and other set pieces.

As we watched Man City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma wrestle with a Bournemouth player at a corner on the TV in the Newcastle press room yesterday, a voice from the back piped up.

'It's like watching kids in a playground,' she said. It was perfectly put.

Farewell King Kev

Alan Shearer – said to be scaling back his TV schedule this season – was in Newcastle to witness a fabulous and moving tribute to the late Kevin Keegan by two of his former clubs at St James Park.

It really was a super effort by Newcastle and Liverpool and it was fitting that Keegan's family and grandchildren were in the stadium to witness it.

Sometimes football manages to get things very right indeed.

Sports.title: 'Come on, that's ridiculous!': Man United boss Michael Carrick snaps at ex-player interviewer as pressure hits on first question about his team's 'passion' after collapsing at promoted Hull City
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick snapped at a reporter's 'ridiculous' opening question after Manchester United's shock defeat by Hull City on Saturday.

The United manager was affronted when asked if his players had lost against the newly promoted club due to a lack of 'passion'.

United's Premier League season got off to a nightmare start as goals from Semi Ajayi and Nobel Mendy – both stemming from set-pieces – put them to the sword in Yorkshire.

Carrick was interviewed afterwards by Viaplay broadcaster Jan Age Fjortoft, the Norwegian who played for Swindon, Middlesbrough, Sheffield United, and Barnsley in the 1990s.

'Would you accept that there was a lack of passion in the first half?' asked Fjortoft.

'Oh come on, that's ridiculous,' Carrick hit back.

Michael Carrick said it was 'ridiculous' to suggest his Manchester United team lacked passion in their 2-0 defeat by Hull City

He was vexed by the question posed by Viaplay reporter and former play Jan Age Fjortoft

“Come on, that’s ridiculous.”



Michael Carrick wasn’t happy when asked if there was a lack of passion from #mufc in their first half vs Hull.



via @ViaplayFotball pic.twitter.com/zyca5r5iSr — utdreport (@utdreport) August 23, 2026

'That's not how you would assess it?' asked Fjortoft.

Carrick replied: 'Come on, you played football, you understand, that's a ridiculous thing to say. Just because you got beat doesn't mean you don't care about it.'

Fjortoft said: 'I'm not saying that you didn't care about it. If you look at it, they came with passion, that's what I mean. I understand that you care about it, but would you accept that they took you on that front, so to say?'

'No, no. Their two goals came from set plays. Other than that, we had opportunities,' Carrick said. 'That was where the game was. I don't think it was passion or anything to do with that. I think it was just their moment that made the difference in the game.'

Fjortoft said: 'Is it these duels? Is that what you mean? That these two duels were the goals? Because they had chances. There were consequences there from the game that you could see that they would get at you.'

'It’s a game of football, it’s a Premier League game,' Carrick replied.

'It’s their first game at home, and we’ve seen it many times before. You know, I said it before the game because it was always going to be a tough game.

'And set-plays, yeah, that’s it. We’ve been decent over a period of time at dealing with them, and today we didn’t.

Any title talk for Manchester United was quickly dulled by their lacklustre performance

Semi Ajayi gave the hosts the lead after a kerfuffle in the box in the 17th minute

Nobel Mendy made matters worse for United when he added Hull's second after 38 minutes

Marcus Rashford came off the bench wearing the number nine shirt but was unable to change the match

'We can look into that, we can dissect it. We certainly won’t get carried away with the positives or the negatives. We never do. So I think we can stay calm and understand what we need to get better at.'

It was a humbling experience for Carrick, who lost just two of his 17 matches in interim charge of United.

They started with a new-look midfield in the form of Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, but neither was overly convincing and the former even got nutmegged at one point.

Carrick did a fantastic job to lead United into the Champions League and the hope is that they will imitate that. Carlos Baleba is soon arriving from Brighton for £70million to further bolster their midfield.

Reporting on the match at the MKM Stadium, Daily Mail Sport's Manchester United reporter Chris Wheeler called any talk of a title challenge a 'joke'.

Wheeler wrote: 'Even in his worst nightmares, Carrick couldn't have foreseen this: an opening-day humiliation at the hands of a team that sneaked into the Premier League via the Championship play-offs in May, and have been prepped for their return to the top-flight with a summer spend of just £70million on 12 players – the same as it is costing United to sign Carlos Baleba from Brighton.'

He added: 'After a summer of guarded optimism over the signing of Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans, the new midfield failed to launch.

'Both players were replaced midway through the second half on their Premier League debuts with United two goals down, having been eclipsed by Matt Crooks and Slater, a mere £50,000 signing from Sheffield United in 2022.

'Instead, it was the business that United haven't done that becomes the main talking point. The new striker that hasn't arrived. The missing defensive cover for Luke Shaw. Baleba, the third midfield signing, coming in too late to start the season.

Considering Carrick only lost two of his 17 games after taking over in January, this was a serious setback. He talked in the week about touting United as title contenders being 'a jump'. On this evidence, it's a joke.'

Sports.title: Harry Maguire is caught tackling his OWN TEAM-MATE in new angle of Man United's defensive horror show - as Luke Shaw's comments spark concern about weaknesses
Sports.content:
Harry Maguire is caught tackling his OWN TEAM-MATE in new angle of Man United's defensive horror show - as Luke Shaw's comments spark concern about weaknesses

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Harry Maguire's defending is again under scrutiny after the Manchester United star wrestled with his own team-mate before Hull's first goal at the weekend.

The centre-back had his arm around Noussair Mazraoui before the man he should have been marking, Semi Ajayi, bashed the ball into the net.

Had the grappling not have taken place, either Maguire or Mazraoui could have reacted and fought for the ball, which had bounced off the post into the danger area.

But perhaps the confusion makes sense after Luke Shaw raised the alarm over United's lack of preparation for set-pieces under Michael Carrick.

'Disappointing, I think we knew Hull’s strengths,' Shaw said. 'Set-plays and wide positions and crosses into the box.

'At times we did defend well, but the goals, set-plays, not good enough. We knew they were going to be good from set-plays and ultimately it’s cost us the three points today.

Harry Maguire held onto Noussair Mazraoui as Hull City scored their first goal on Saturday

Luke Shaw said afterwards that Manchester United had not prepared enough for set-pieces

Maguire has had similar moments before, such as when he brought down Shaw in 2020, leading to a Tottenham goal

'Really disappointing. It’s not us and we knew it was coming. I think as a whole, as a group, collectively, we could prepare better. Especially knowing how good they are at set-plays and what their dangers are.

'I think also going forward we were lacking that cutting edge today to score the goals and try to fight our way back into the game.'

United conceded a second goal stemming from a set-piece later in the first half when Nobel Mendy netted his first Premier League goal.

Football fans on social media were certainly confused by what they had seen.

'Maguire has done it again,' said one on X.

'Maguire please don't bring back the old version of yourself,' said another.

'He thought it was still pre-season training,' one joked.

Others stood up for the Englishman, with one saying: 'No Maguire slander would be tolerated. Man was our second best player today after Mbeumo.'

Semi Ajayi gave the hosts the lead after a kerfuffle in the box in the 17th minute

Nobel Mendy made matters worse for United when he added Hull's second after 38 minutes

Another shifted blame from Maguire, saying: 'All of them are standing like b***** statues and that's what p***** me off. Nobody charged. Nobody. Pathetic when it comes to passion.

This is not the first time Maguire has committed friendly fire and obstructed a team-mate.

He accidentally 'fouled' Shaw in 2020 against Tottenham, which resulted in a goal; once kicked Paul Pogba in the head, which forced him to leave the pitch bleeding; and appealed for a handball against team-mate Nemanja Matic in the box.

In high pressure moments, with the match moving at such speed, it is easy to become confused, but his repeated blunders in this department have left supporters befuddled.

The 33-year-old, who missed out on the World Cup, played for Hull between 2014 and 2017.

He joined United from Leicester in a record £80million deal in 2019 and, in April, signed a fresh one-year deal with the club. United also hold the option to extend it by a year.

His wages have dropped from around £180,000 per week to £120,000 in line with the club's new salary structure.

Sports.title: Ronnie O'Sullivan gives honest take on snooker future - 'There's nothing I can do'
Sports.content:
Ronnie O'Sullivan gives honest take on snooker future - 'There's nothing I can do'

Ronnie O'Sullivan is through to the last 32 of the Wuhan Open after beating Ashley Carty 5-2, but he was critical of his performance and feels powerless to do better

View 2 Images Ronnie O'Sullivan was typically candid in his assessment (Image: Tai Chengzhe/VCG via Getty Images)

Snooker legend Ronnie O'Sullivan has admitted that there's 'nothing he can do' to improve on his 'pretty bad' form. Despite winning his opening game at the Wuhan Open 5-2 against Ashley Carty, O'Sullivan was downbeat.

‌



The seven-time world champion made a high break of just 59 and was fortunate not to be punished by Carty, who missed a string of opportunities. O'Sullivan reckons that he hasn't been at his best for four years, with his performance against Carty coming as no surprise to him.

‌



"My performance was pretty bad really," the Rocket said. "You have to call it out. I'm not going to lie. I'm not going to try to delude myself and say there was some good stuff.

‌



"It has been pretty bad for a long time, so I expect to play pretty bad every time I go out there. I know I don't have anything to prove and that is what everyone keeps telling me.

‌



"However, for my own selfish reasons, I miss playing well and dominating the table, beating anyone who is in front of me. I miss that feeling, but there is nothing I can do about it."

O'Sullivan doesn't have long to wait until his next match, facing Chinah's Yao Pengcheng at 7am UK time on Tuesday in the last 32. His chances of making a deep run at the Wuhan Open have been boosted by Wu Yize's early exit.

The world champion suffered a shock 5-4 loss against Artemijs Zizins on Monday. Latvian youngster Zizins has been awarded a clash with Stephen Maguire at the same time slot as O'Sullivan's match.

‌



Last month, O'Sullivan revealed that he's set himself a deadline of 2028 to beat Stephen Hendry's record for World Championships. The 50-year-old is currently level with seven and told World Snooker Tour: " I'd love to win another World Championship.

Can Ronnie O'Sullivan get back to his best? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Ronnie O'Sullivan was unhappy with his display against Ashley Carty (Image: Tai Chengzhe/VCG via Getty Images)

‌



"I've got two attempts at it. Three years previous, I wasn't cueing well enough, so I feel like if I can find a bit of cueing find some form at Sheffield… if I don't do it this this season or the next season, then it'll definitely never happen.

"But I'm pleased with my career. I'm happy with how things have gone, and I just want to try and enjoy these next two years. I'll reassess it in 2028 and if things are really going well, and I've surprised myself, then maybe you can extend it but you have to be realistic. I'm definitely not going to be playing qualifiers put it that way.

"I'm not going to play qualifiers. You won't be seeing me go down to Barnsley trying to win qualifying matches and all that sort of stuff. I have to be realistic. If that happens, then obviously that's the end of my career. But hopefully, I can keep going for at least another two seasons."

Sports.title: Virgil van Dijk sends Liverpool chiefs transfer message with Andoni Iraola in agreement
Sports.content:
Virgil van Dijk sends Liverpool chiefs transfer message with Andoni Iraola in agreement

Liverpool have one week left to make more signings, with Andoni Iraola yet to get his hands on the marquee winger that he's been craving since taking over at Anfield

View 3 Images Virgil van Dijk wants a stronger dressing room (Image: George Wood/Getty Images)

Virgil van Dijk wants to see Liverpool make 'quality' signings in the final week of the transfer window. It comes after Reds boss Andoni Iraola promised fans that the club will 'definitely' add to their squad before next Monday's 11pm deadline, having admitted in pre-season that he needed more options.

‌



Liverpool have only made one permanent signing this summer in the form of Victor Munoz, with Ronald Araujo's move from Barcelona only a loan and their £60million deal for Jeremy Jacquet being agreed with Rennes back in February. Iraola has been desperate to sign a winger all window, with Paris Saint-Germain's Bradley Barcola top of his shortlist.

‌



But with PSG demanding £145million, Liverpool are being forced to consider alternatives. The Reds saw two bids for Brighton star Yankuba Minteh rejected last week, the latest of which was £60m.

‌



Speaking after Liverpool's dramatic 2-2 draw away to Newcastle on Sunday, Van Dijk affirmed that he has 'full trust' in the club to get their recruitment right The Reds captain also made it clear that he and his team-mates need to shoulder the responsibility for improving on last season's 'very unacceptable' campaign.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"Everyone wants to see quality arrive regardless," Van Dijk said. "I fully trust the club and the board to make the right decisions, that's the only thing I can say. Let's see what they do.

"Regardless of what happens, we are Liverpool and we have to give everything. For us, we have to show a reaction from last year. We have nothing to prove to the outside world, in my opinion. It is to ourselves. The way we train, the way we approach games, it is down to us to show a reaction.

"Last year it was very unacceptable, but that was last year. I don't want to talk about that - we are looking forward and looking to improve. Hopefully, next week it will be very close to what [Iraola] wants us to do."

‌



Having snatched a point at Newcastle in their first outing, Liverpool continue in the Premier League with a home game against Nottingham Forest in Saturday's early kick-off. And Van Dijk knows that their new manager will make sure they've put in the hard yards on the training ground first.

Who should Liverpool sign before the transfer window closes? Let us know your pick in the comments section.

View 3 Images Andoni Iraola is still waiting on a winger (Image: Molly Darlington/Getty Images)

‌



"Like I say, we work on it every day," the Dutchman reiterated. "We do long hours on the training ground and that will only benefit all of us, including our loyal and trusted supporters. It is so early in the season that if we start panicking regardless of what could have happened today then we won't be in a good place.

"It is down to us to make sure we improve quickly, and that is what we try to do on the training ground. There were some good things, but also things that we have to improve.

"I think if we have to answer questions from the outside world, I don't think that's on us. What we have to do as players at Liverpool Football Club is be much better than we were last year. That is the responsibility everyone has to feel.

‌



View 3 Images Liverpool have bid £60million for Yankuba Minteh (Image: Crystal Pix/MB Media/Getty Images)

"Obviously, there are some changes that are happening in the club and that is clearly visible. Some players have left, some players have come to the club, and it is down to us to be as good as we can as soon as possible, and challenge on all four fronts, hopefully as soon as possible.

"I think it is absolutely normal in any type of profession or work that if you come in new and you have new plans and ideas that it takes a bit of time. It is down to us to do it as soon as we can. We want to improve, we want to win, we want to do better. That is what we are going to try and do from tomorrow."

Sports.title: Gabriel Jesus' Arsenal transfer route closed as suitor turns to £25m-rated Chelsea star
Sports.content:
Gabriel Jesus' Arsenal transfer route closed as suitor turns to £25m-rated Chelsea star

Arsenal star Gabriel Jesus could leave this summer but has turned down Napoli's advances, leaving the Italian club to turn their attention to one of Chelsea's forwards

View 2 Images Gabriel Jesus could leave Arsenal this summer (Image: Getty Images)

Gabriel Jesus' Arsenal future is in doubt and Napoli had eyed the Brazilian, but have since switched attention to one of Chelsea's out-of-favour frontmen.

‌



Jesus has been at the Emirates since 2022 and, despite being a regular initially, he has fallen down the pecking order and now entered the final year of his contract. His departure could take place this summer but he made it known he didn't want to move to Italy.

‌



Napoli were keen but after being turned down have turned their attention to Marc Guiu at the Blues, reports Sky in Italy. New boss Massimiliano Allegri is keen to bolster his forward ranks after seeing Romelu Lukaku leave for Galatasaray.

‌



Guiu was signed from Barcelona in 2024 but has struggled for opportunities ever since heading to west London. His only regular minutes came in the Europa Conference League, when he scored six goals in seven games as Chelsea won the tournament in 2025.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

The 20-year-old was loaned to Sunderland last season but recalled after just 26 days following Liam Delap's injury, however he remains on the outside of the first-team. He started just five games and played only 527 minutes of football under Enzo Maresca and Liam Rosenior.

‌



His fortunes are unlikely to change despite Xabi Alonso now being in charge with Joao Pedro the team's first choice striker. This summer they've added veteran frontman Danny Welbeck to provide cover, which leaves Guiu facing a lack of minutes.

The striker is not short of interested parties with Napoli facing competition from clubs in Spain and Germany. Chelsea value the striker at £25m - which would represent a notable profit on the £5m they paid to sign him.

View 2 Images Marc Guiu is not in favour at Chelsea (Image: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC)

‌



Napoli finished second last season but have embarked on a new era with Allegri replacing Antonio Conte. The Italians have signed Rasmus Hojlund on a permanent deal following his loan from Manchester United but remain keen on more additions.

The Italian side would more than likely need to sell before they can buy and Dutch winger Noa Lang has been tipped to leave. That could free up the funds to pursue Guiu. Napoli and Chelsea have already done business this summer with Benoit Badiashile heading to Italy on loan.

Sports.title: Golf news: Rory McIlroy reacts to 'stupid' decision as star clashes with fan
Sports.content:
Golf news: Rory McIlroy reacts to 'stupid' decision as star clashes with fan

The BMW Championship crowned a new winner on Sunday as Rory McIlroy found himself in title contention once again on the PGA Tour

View 4 Images Wyndham Clark won the BMW Championship 2026 at Bellerive Country Club (Image: Getty)

Wyndham Clark almost let an almighty lead slip but held on to win the BMW Championship by three strokes on Sunday. Rory McIlroy had closed the gap on the American heading into the final few holes, but Clark upped his game to seal the £2.6million top prize.

‌



The BMW Championship was held at Missouri's Bellerive Country Club for the 2026 edition, with Scottie Scheffler the defending champion. However, it was his compatriot Clark who got off to a fast start with an opening 64, alongside the likes of McIlroy and Gary Woodland.

‌



The US Open winner then took up the solo lead after round two and didn't look back. Despite entering the last day five shots clear of McIlroy, the Northern Irishman did close the gap. But three birdies on the final three holes from Clark meant McIlroy had to settle for third and Patrick Cantlay finished as runner-up.

‌



However, McIlroy made an error on 17 that he later branded "stupid" as Mirror Sport brings you all the latest news from the world of golf.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Rory McIlroy blows chance to pocket £1.64m as he reacts to BMW Championship collapse READ MORE :

'Typical' Rory McIlroy called out as LIV Golf stars divisively invited to Alfred Dunhill READ MORE :

Rory McIlroy's "stupid" decision

Having cut Clark's lead down on the final day, McIlroy entered the par-five 17th just one stroke behind the American. But he found the rough off the tee and went bunker to bunker after a misexecuted lay-up.

‌



View 4 Images McIlroy came up just short (Image: Getty)

McIlroy's tournament hopes were ended with a bogey, and he lamented his decision whilst speaking to CBS Sports. He said: "I tried to get it up a bit too far. I should have been taking that left bunker out of play.

"If you're going to lay it up, lay it up, so just another stupid decision with a lay-up on a par-five that cost me. I can't be too disappointed. I'm probably not playing well enough to be disappointed that I didn't win.

‌



"I had my chances on the back nine and hit a lot of good putts that didn't go in. Wyndham Clark stepped up when he needed to. His birdie on 16 was huge and the way he played the last three holes, he showed a lot of character."

Golfer clashes with a fan

LIV Golf Indianapolis also took place over the weekend, and on Saturday, the iconic Bubba Watson had an altercation with a rather unruly fan.

Watson was playing his round with Lee Westwood and Bryson DeChambeau at Chatham Hills when a fan screamed as Westwood was in his pre-shot routine.

‌



View 4 Images Watson had an interaction with a fan (Image: Getty)

The Englishman had to step back and compose himself once more when his playing partner, Watson, took umbrage at the act. A clip that has surfaced online appears to show Watson exchanging words with the fan in an agitated manner.

"Oh, you don't want to say anything now? Say something, I'm looking at you, say it," Watson said, before staring the person down and walking towards the green.

‌



LIV rookie makes history

Watson, Westwood and DeChambeau were joined at LIV Indianapolis by HyFlyers GC rookie Michael La Sasso. And although many a star name graced the field, La Sasso came out on top.

The American shot an incredible 60 in Round Two to launch him into contention, and although Jon Rahm was on his tail during the final day, he held on, becoming the youngest winner in LIV Golf history.

View 4 Images La Sasso claimed LIV victory for the first time (Image: Getty)

Article continues below

As uncertainty lingered, with Saudi Arabia's PIF no longer funding LIV beyond the season that concluded on Sunday, La Sasso was soaked in champagne by his team-mates.

"I had a bunch of buddies texting me last night asking if they should fly in, and I said I was going to win anyway, but you might as well come for the show," said La Sasso. "It ended up working itself out."

Sports.title: Billionaire bookie boss Denise Coates revealed as owner of £600k Dan Skelton jumper
Sports.content:
Billionaire bookie boss Denise Coates revealed as owner of £600k Dan Skelton jumper

The founder and CEO of Bet365, who is one of Britain’s wealthiest women, is now listed as the owner of the four-year-old Push The Limit who won at Glorious Goodwood when trained by Ralph Beckett

View 3 Images Denise Coates: has become a racehorse owner

Billionaire bookmaker boss Denise Coates has joined the ranks of racehorse owners for the first time.

‌



One of Britain’s most successful business people, she is the founder and chief executive of online brand Bet365 and has a net worth of £9.5 billion. She is the eldest daughter of Peter Coates, chairman of Stoke City FC, gaining experience working in her father’s betting shop before establishing Bet365 as one of the world’s largest online betting operations.

‌



In 2024, with her husband Richard Smith, she registered Coates-Smith Racing lp with Companies House as an ‘owner of horses’ and has now acquired the first racehorse.

‌



Push The Limit won two of his six starts on the Flat when trained by Ralph Beckett, including a valuable handicap at last year’s Glorious Goodwood meeting.

He was then bought at the October Sales by champion trainer Dan Skelton and Ryan Mahon for £609,000. The gelding has now been registered to Coates-Smith Racing and with a Flat rating of 103 could be an exciting prospect over jumps.

Skelton, speaking to the Nick Luck Daily Podcast, said: “We feel very lucky to have the family’s support. We did lots with the horse last year but we just felt that physically he was still to turn a corner and switch on to full jumps mode.

‌



View 3 Images Push The Limit: has joined champion jumps trainer Dan Skelton

“He did jump very, very nicely but we felt like a bit of time, given he was such a young horse, would be no negative whatsoever.

“He is only a four-year-old and I think it’s the best thing we’ve done is give him that time. He is moving particularly well, looks great, he’s quite a flashy character - he’s chestnut with white socks - and we did like everything we saw.

‌



“By the time you get mid-way through the season there was only half of it to go and you’re better off having a full run at novice season. Everybody was quite happy to give him a bit of time. Physically I can only say that has definitely been the right thing to do.”

View 3 Images Dan Skelton: became champion jumps trainer for the first time in April (Image: David Davies/PA Wire for The Jockey Club)

Skelton said Push The Limit could make his debut in October.

Article continues below

“I don’t think he’s a horse that wants really soft ground. I’d like to get him out, once we do get some rain in the country, and I’d imagine he’d be ready to run mid or end of October and take a view from there.

“On the track he looked very good and from what we’ve seen at home we like him as well – pretty exciting stuff.”

Sports.title: Rory McIlroy blows chance to pocket £1.64m as he reacts to BMW Championship collapse
Sports.content:
Rory McIlroy blows chance to pocket £1.64m as he reacts to BMW Championship collapse

Rory McIlroy was tied for the lead with three holes to play at the BMW Championship but fell short, missing out on a significant sum after finishing third

View 2 Images Rory McIlroy failed to pocket an extra £1.64m at the BMW Championship (Image: Getty Images)

Rory McIlroy has admitted he's worried about his swing heading into the season‑ending Tour Championship after missing out on an extra $2.24m (£1.64m) by finishing third at the BMW Championship. He birdied three of his final four holes in the third round to close within five shots of leader Wyndham Clark, earning a spot in last Sunday's final against the US Open champion.

‌



McIlroy drew level with Clark on the final day but despite being tied for the lead with three holes remaining, the Northern Irishman slipped to a third‑place finish, four shots back. Clark finished with three straight birdies to secure a three‑stroke win and his third PGA Tour title of the season.

‌



Reflecting on his performance, McIlroy admitted: "I'm closer [with his game] than I was at the start of the week. I'm still not in a spot where I'm super happy with where my game is or where my swing is, so I just have to keep working on it.

‌



'Typical' Rory McIlroy called out as LIV Golf stars divisively invited to Alfred Dunhill READ MORE :

Rory McIlroy's heartbreaking admission as he misses significant family milestone for career READ MORE :

"It's nice to know, even when I'm not super happy with everything, I can still piece it together and get it around and still give myself a chance to win tournaments."

The world No.2 gained two shots on the opening hole, then recovered after dropping shots at the fourth and seventh. He embarked on a strong spell, reeling off three birdies in four holes from the eighth onwards.

That enabled him to draw level as Clark faltered and played his opening 10 holes three over par. Clark surged ahead with a 15-foot birdie on the 16th, before picking up two additional shots at the par-five 17th.

‌



He registered a birdie while McIlroy dropped one. Clark then added another birdie at the final hole to extend his winning margin over Patrick Cantlay.

"I felt like most of my game held up today," McIlroy added. "Obviously, going out in the final group and you're working on some stuff, you're just hoping that everything stays the way it is.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



"I hit it well on the back nine. I gave myself plenty of chances. I just couldn't get a putt to drop there in those final few holes. I always felt like I needed to just get my nose ahead to really try to put the pressure on Wyndham [Clark] and I couldn't.

"We were tied there for a few holes and then when he made that putt on 16 for a two and I couldn't answer - that was obviously a huge moment in the round and in the tournament. Overall, encouraged with how I played this week and certainly something to build on going into East Lake."

Despite believing he should have secured victory, McIlroy refused to let disappointment creep in. "I can't be," he continued.

‌



"I'm probably not playing well enough to be disappointed that I didn't win. I had my chances on the back nine and hit a lot of good putts that didn't go in.

"Wyndham Clark stepped up when he needed too. His birdie on 16 was huge and the way he played the last three holes, he showed a lot of character."

Clark earned $3.6m (£2.64m), while McIlroy took home $1.36m (£1m). Cantlay, who finished second, bagged $2.16m (£1.58m).

‌



View 2 Images McIlroy finished third at the BMW Championship (Image: Getty Images)

McIlroy will now turn his attention to the Tour Championship at East Lake GC, which gets under way on Thursday, 27th August.

He'll be vying for the FedExCup title and the $10m top prize, with only the leading 30 players in the standings earning their place at the prestigious event.

Liverpool news: Bradley Barcola exiled by PSG as personal terms 'agreed'

Today's Liverpool latest sees a significant update on the Reds' summer-long chase of PSG winger Bradley Barcola

View 3 Images Liverpool have been handed an update on the future of Bradley Barcola (Image: Adam Davy/PA Wire)

Liverpool are up against the clock to make additions to their squad with the transfer window closing in a week's time. Spanish winger Victor Munoz, Barcelona loanee Ronald Araujo and French defender Jeremy Jaquet are the only new recruits at Anfield so far this summer.

‌



Curtis Jones left Liverpool last week, meaning the Reds have shifted their focus onto incomings. Liverpool have been linked with a move for PSG star Bradley Barcola for much of the summer, and a deal could be completed this week with the transfer window closing on September 1.

‌



A swoop for Yankuba Minteh of Brighton is also in the works after the Reds bid for the winger last week. There have been two major updates on Liverpool's pursuit of both players, and Mirror Football has taken a closer look.

‌



Barcola exiled

Barcola has been omitted from Luis Enrique's PSG squad for two recent games, as his future remains uncertain. According to RMC Sport, Barcola, and Ibrahim Mbaye, who has also been linked with Liverpool this summer, will not be involved in the club's matches until their situations are resolved.

Both players were left out of PSG's squad for their French Super Cup defeat to Lens last weekend as well as the club's Ligue 1 opener at Rennes on Sunday night.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
