World.title: INTERVIEW: How my role on UN panel on nuclear war effects can benefit Nigeria – Prof Rabia Sa’id
World.content:
Rabia Sa’id, a professor of physics at Bayero University, Kano (BUK), was appointed last year by the United Nations Secretary-General to a 21-member scientific panel studying the physical effects and societal impacts of nuclear war.

Established under UN General Assembly Resolution 79/238, the panel of some of the world’s premier scientists is evaluating existential global nuclear threats. It is scheduled to present its findings later this year. The findings are expected to inform international policy on nuclear risk reduction, global security, and humanitarian protection.

Professor Sa’id, from Kano State, is one of the first two female lecturers in BUK’s Department of Physics. Her strides have inspired young women across Nigeria to pursue careers in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM).

Beyond her foundational contributions to atmospheric, space weather, electronics, and particle physics, Mrs Sa’id is widely recognised for applying scientific solutions to real-world environmental challenges. Her notable achievements include developing eco-friendly fuel briquettes, reducing rural reliance on firewood, and combating regional deforestation, and leading pioneering, low-cost air quality monitoring initiatives that combine ground sensor data with satellite observations to enhance local climate tracking.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

In this exclusive interview with PREMIUM TIMES’ Ahmadu Maishanu in Kano, Sa’id speaks on her appointment, how Nigeria can leverage the opportunity it presents, and what the country stands to gain from the panel’s work.

Excerpts:

PREMIUM TIMES: What does your presence on this global panel signify for Nigeria’s standing in international science and global diplomacy?

Professor Rabia: Nigeria plays a key role as a voice within the United Nations. Also, Nigeria routinely pushes for UN Security Council reforms to secure permanent representation for African nations and to contribute to policies that ensure world peace; it is a signatory to the Agreement on the Peaceful Uses of Nuclear Energy and to the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons. I believe that even though I am on the panel in my individual capacity, it should still be positive for Nigeria’s standing in international science and global diplomacy

PREMIUM TIMES: How can your role on this panel benefit local scientific research, climate action, and policy development back home in Nigeria?

Professor Rabia: There is so much that I have learnt since the start of the panel work. I am an atmospheric physicist and climate action advocate, with expertise in nuclear nonproliferation. Being in the circle of eminent scientists across various fields related to nuclear impacts on climate, food sources, human health, agriculture, etc., provides valuable insights we can use to mitigate environmental impacts locally.

PREMIUM TIMES: Through your appointment as one of the pioneer female academics at BUK’s Department of Physics, you broke institutional gender barriers. What message does this UN appointment send to young women across Northern Nigeria and the rest of the nation?

I have always been a strong advocate for women’s participation in science careers, and I have demonstrated this through career talks in secondary schools across Kano and extended to other states in Nigeria. The message that this UN appointment sends to young women is that if they work hard and become visible, their work and expertise will speak for them, and they will not need to lobby.

PREMIUM TIMES: Women remain underrepresented in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics disciplines across Africa. How can this global platform bolster women’s inclusion in science?

Professor Rabia: The UN panel provides a platform for experts to meet across various scientific fields. One can interact, exchange contact information, and share ideas. It becomes a networking platform that one can leverage to connect with other women working in the same field in Nigeria. For example, my contact with the panel’s experts provides a platform to leverage for my students’ benefit. Reaching out to these experts is much easier now because we met in person, and they saw my capabilities firsthand. It serves as an excellent platform for collaboration, bolstering women’s empowerment, and driving other key benefits.

PREMIUM TIMES: How can Nigeria benefit from this global platform?

Professor Rabia: The primary work of this panel is anticipatory. While the UN always strives for peace, we must acknowledge that the threat of conflict remains real. In the event of a war, the panel’s main duty is to evaluate the potential consequences of a nuclear exchange. When Hiroshima and Nagasaki occurred during World War II, the world was caught unprepared. Today, given rising global geopolitical tensions, we must ask: if a nuclear conflict were to happen, what specific impacts should we expect? Unless we accurately predict these outcomes, we cannot properly prepare for them. This necessity prompted New Zealand to advance the initiative, resulting in the adoption of UN Resolution 79/238 to investigate these scientific impacts.

Although Nigeria does not possess nuclear weapons, it is a key signatory to the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons (NPT), and the findings of this investigation will benefit our nation. Nigeria can pursue nuclear energy to secure a stable electricity supply. Nuclear power provides a reliable, clean energy solution that aligns with global environmental protection goals, which is why many nations rely on it today. Critics in Nigeria often argue that a weak safety culture could lead to disaster. However, the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) enforces rigorous global safeguards designed specifically to prevent operational failures. The scientific research from this UN panel will directly inform and strengthen Nigeria’s own safety protocols for future nuclear infrastructure.

We already have a track record of safe operation. The Centre for Energy Research and Training at Ahmadu Bello University (ABU) in Zaria has safely operated a miniature neutron-source research reactor for years without incident. This proves that Nigeria possesses the capability to manage nuclear technology responsibly. Public anxiety surrounding nuclear power is understandable and surmountable; the fear stems largely from a lack of awareness. Nothing in life is to be feared; it is only to be understood. The technical safeguards available today ensure that nuclear power can be operated even more safely than our current energy infrastructure.

PREMIUM TIMES: Could you please share your experience so far and how you were nominated for the appointment?

Professor Rabia: Because of the network of scientists I have on different platforms and the visibility I have already built, I happened to be on the mailing list of some of these organisations. I received a notification for a call for nominations. Usually, such an opportunity comes with the requirement that you are nominated either by your institution or by the government of your home country. Most of the times, I shy away a little because I have tried on several occasions and found that the government or the institution already has its own candidate to nominate, making it very difficult.

However, in the case of this nomination for the UN Panel, your government can nominate you, your institution can nominate you, an expert can nominate you, or you can self-nominate. Knowing all the difficulties one can face when seeking a government or institutional nomination, I decided to self-nominate. I submitted the self-nomination form with all the required information. I was not very confident because I thought many institutions within Nigeria might have nominated other people, given that it is a high-level expert panel. I didn’t think I was going to make it, but I told myself that everything is worth trying.

Sincerely, I almost even forgot I had sent the nomination form, though I knew I beat the deadline, which was November 2024.

I didn’t hear anything until July 1, 2025. In fact, it was someone else who saw the UN press release and noticed my name among the 21-member panel selected for appointment by the United Nations Secretary-General, António Guterres, to study the effects of nuclear wars. That person sent it to me on WhatsApp. I opened it and thanked God Almighty for the opportunity.

After that, I looked at the names of the other experts on the panel, and it was unbelievable. There was the Deputy Director General of the International Atomic Energy Agency, directors who have been with the World Health Organisation, agricultural scientists, and many other prominent scientists whose papers I had read but never expected to meet. I was really excited; at one point, I kept looking at the list to make sure it was actually my name (laughter). Finally, I realised that it was indeed me, and I had truly been selected. I then contacted the UN Nigeria House Resident and Humanitarian Coordinator in Nigeria, Mohamed Malik Fall, who responded to my message informing him of my appointment and hosted me at UN Nigeria House.

Panel activities began last December following its inauguration at UN Headquarters in New York. Since then, the panel has convened virtually on several occasions and held an in-person meeting in Vienna, Austria, in March. The next meeting is scheduled for Geneva, Switzerland, in September, alongside several consultations with regional stakeholders, ahead of the final report’s submission to the UN General Assembly in 2027.

World.title: Fidelity Bank gets extension to publish H1 2026 audited results
World.content:
Fidelity Bank Plc has announced a potential delay in the publication of its audited financial statements for the half-year ended 30 June, after securing an extension from the Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX).

The lender said it secured an extension from NGX Group to 30 September to publish its half-year financial statements, according to a regulatory filing by its Company Secretary, Ezinwa Unuigboje, on Monday.

Fidelity Bank said the extension became necessary because the audit of its H1 2026 financial statements is still being finalised.

According to the bank, upon completion of the audit, the financial statements will be presented to the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) for approval before publication in line with the NGX Rulebook and other applicable regulations.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The financial institution said it obtained the NGX’s approval for the extension, subject to receiving regulatory approval from the CBN for the H1 2026 audited accounts.

“Premised on the foregoing, the approval of the NGX was obtained for an extension of time to September 30, 2026, subject to receipt of regulatory approval from the CBN for the H1 2026 audited accounts,” the lender said.

Meanwhile, Fidelity Bank said the trading window for its insiders and connected persons remains closed.

The bank said the trading restriction will remain in place until 24 hours after the publication of its half-year audited financial statements.

For Nigerian listed companies whose financial year ends on 31 December, H1 results covering January to June must be filed with NGX by the applicable half-year reporting deadline, subject to regulatory requirements for banks.

Fidelity Bank, one of the leading Nigerian financial institutions, reported gross earnings growth of 45.6 per cent from N1.04 trillion in 2024 to N1.52 trillion in audited financial results for the year ended 31 December 2025.

The growth reflected stronger topline momentum across core business segments of the financial institution.

It also recorded a profit after tax (PAT) of N242.4 billion, which was underpinned by a 38.7 per cent year-on-year increase in interest income of the lender.

World.title: Law School approves five new Law faculties, places Atiba University under 10-year moratorium
World.content:
The Council of Legal Education (CLE) has approved five universities to begin offering Law from the 2026/2027 academic session.

But it also placed Atiba University, Oyo State, under a 10-year moratorium after finding that the institution breached its regulatory requirements.

The five universities approved to begin Law are Amadeus University, Amazi, Abia State; Akwa Ibom State University; European University of Nigeria, Abuja; Oduduwa University, Ipetu-Modu, Osun State; and Peaceland University, Enugu State.

The council approved an initial quota of 50 students for each university’s 100 Level intake.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

In a statement posted on Sunday on its Facebook page by Aderonke Osho, Secretary to the Council and Director of Administration, the council reached the decisions at its third-quarter hybrid meeting on 13 August at the headquarters of the Nigerian Law School in Bwari, Abuja.

The council stated that it considered reports from its Facilities Verification/Accreditation Panel before approving the five institutions.

“The Council, however, declined to grant approval to Maranatha University, Ibeju-Lekki, Lagos State, to commence the study of Law, owing to the numerous deficiencies identified during the verification exercise,” the statement said.

The approvals come about two months after the council released an updated list of 117 universities authorised to admit students into Law programmes.

In that list, the council warned universities against admitting students without its approval and cautioned prospective students against enrolling in unaccredited Law programmes.

“Students admitted into Law programmes in universities that are not accredited by the Council of Legal Education will not be eligible for admission into the Nigerian Law School,” read the statement.

It also warned that universities that admit students into law programmes without its approval violate regulations that govern legal education in Nigeria. It further declared that such institutions risk sanctions “in accordance with extant regulations and policy.”

Some universities get higher quotas

While expanding the number of institutions allowed to offer Law, the council also increased the admission quotas of some existing Law faculties.

Bowen University, Iwo, Osun State, Ajayi Crowther University, Oyo State, and Topfaith University, Mpatak, Akwa Ibom State, had their quotas increased from 50 to 100 students for the 2026/2027 academic session.

The council also approved revised quotas for North-Eastern University, Gombe; Elizade University; Chrisland University, Abeokuta, Ogun State; Joseph Ayo Babalola University, Ilesa, Osun State; and Olabisi Onabanjo University, Iwoye, Ogun State.

Some of the revised quotas will take effect from the 2027/2028 academic session.

Why Atiba got 10-year moratorium

The council’s decision on Atiba University was more severe.

It said the university’s facilities were “inappropriate and inadequate” for establishing and operating a Faculty of Law.

The council also found that the university had admitted and graduated students without obtaining the required approval.

It described the 10-year moratorium as a necessary regulatory measure to bring the institution into compliance with prescribed standards.

The decision comes against the backdrop of the council’s broader efforts to enforce accreditation requirements for Law programmes nationwide.

983 fail Bar Final resit

The council also approved the results of the May 2026 Bar Final (Resit) Examination.

Of the 1,955 candidates who sat for the examination, 983 failed.

A total of 885 candidates passed, while 55 obtained conditional passes.

The results of 19 candidates were withheld, while 32 candidates were absent.

Five candidates barred over misconduct

Five candidates found guilty of examination misconduct during the December 2025 Bar Final Examination were disqualified and barred from sitting the examination for 10 years.

The council also approved sanctions against two students found culpable of other acts of indiscipline.

In another disciplinary decision, the council withdrew the Best Graduating Student in Professional Ethics prize from its recipient.

The council noted that the decision followed the circulation online of a photograph showing the recipient in attire it considered inconsistent with professional standards and decorum.

Council chairman, Emeka Ngige, commended members for their contributions to legal education.

He thanked the management of the Nigerian Law School, led by its Director-General, Olugbemisola Odusote, for its continued work.

World.title: ‘I’ll do it all season’ — Chukwueze embraces new Milan role after Torino win
World.content:
AC Milan winger Samuel Chukwueze made an impressive start to the new Serie A campaign, helping the Rossoneri secure a 2-1 away victory over Torino on Sunday night.

The Super Eagles winger was deployed in an unfamiliar wing-back role by new manager Ruben Amorim but adapted brilliantly to the tactical demands, earning the official Man of the Match award from Serie A.

Chukwueze also made a decisive contribution in attack, providing the assist for Adrien Rabiot’s second goal as Milan secured all three points at the Stadio Olimpico Grande Torino in Turin.

His performance offered an encouraging early indication of how influential the Nigerian could be under Amorim, particularly in a system that requires him to combine his attacking qualities with greater defensive responsibility.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Speaking to DAZN after the match, Chukwueze expressed his satisfaction with Milan’s winning start but insisted the focus had already shifted towards the challenges ahead.

“Now we have to look forward, but I’m very satisfied,” Chukwueze said.

The 26-year-old also made it clear that he is fully prepared to embrace the demands of his new role and give everything for the team throughout the campaign.

Asked about the workload involved, Chukwueze promised to continue putting in the effort whenever Amorim calls on him.

“I’m ready, I can’t wait, and I’ll do it all season,” he added.

Chukwueze’s display will further strengthen his case for a prominent role in Amorim’s plans after the Nigerian returned to Milan following a productive loan spell at Fulham last season.

With his pace, attacking ability and growing willingness to contribute defensively, the winger could become an important weapon for Milan as they look to mount a strong challenge for the Serie A title.

For Chukwueze, however, the message from the opening weekend is simple: he is ready to run, fight and contribute wherever his new manager needs him.

World.title: Catalyst Symposium Holds “Alaigbo” Series in South-East, Empowers Youths
World.content:
The Catalyst Symposium, an initiative that empowers and nurtures emerging leaders across different sectors, has held its Alaigbo Series in Anambra and Imo States to ignite ideas, inspire creativity and empower youths from the region to make impactful contributions to nation building.

The Anambra event was held in Awka, the state capital, on Aug.13 , and was followed by the Owerri edition on Aug. 17 at the Guest House of the Federal University of Technology, Owerri (FUTO), Imo State, with both events attracting a vibrant audience of emerging leaders, entrepreneurs, young professionals, and students who filled the venues with energy and expectation.

These gatherings formed a powerful multi-city movement dedicated to catalyzing minds, igniting ideas, and empowering the sons and daughters of Alaigbo to move from survival to significance.

The atmosphere was charged with purposeful conversations as participants engaged deeply with practical insights on leadership, business growth, and regional transformation. The event set a strong tone for the entire Alaigbo Series and demonstrated the hunger for quality platforms within the South-East.

A major highlight of the Awka Edition was the combined contributions of Philip O. Ekwempu Esq., President of the Awka Chamber of Commerce, and Eze Chinonso, who served as a key speaker and panelist.

While Ekwempu delivered penetrating insights on “From Traders to Titans: Building Systems, Scaling Sustainably, and Creating Generational Wealth,” Eze Chinonso complemented the discourse with practical business perspectives that prepared the ground for his later special appearance in Owerri. Together, their sessions sparked meaningful dialogue on sustainable wealth creation and bold entrepreneurship in Alaigbo.

The smooth flow and high engagement of both editions were largely driven by the outstanding work of Dr Macaulay Barnabas, who served as the Event Host and Lead Moderator.

Behind the success of these editions stands the unwavering dedication and strong work ethic of the convener, Arogundade Dolapo. From meticulous planning and stakeholder engagement to hands-on coordination across cities, his commitment to excellence ensured that every detail was executed with precision.

Dolapo’s relentless drive continues to push The Catalyst Symposium beyond limitations and toward greater impact.

The Owerri edition, styled as the ‘Eze Chinonso Special’, carried unique emotional vibe as a homecoming for the special guest at his alma mater, the Federal University of Technology, Owerri (FUTO).

In addition to Eze Chinonso’s inspiring session, the edition featured “The Catalyst Pitch and Mentorship Programme, where 13 scholars from FUTO boldly pitched their business ideas.

These young innovators have been selected to undergo a structured three-week mentorship programme designed to refine their concepts, build practical skills, and position them for real growth.

Across both cities, the quality of engagement, the free access model, and the sense of community stood out clearly, as participants left with renewed clarity, expanded networks, and a stronger belief in the possibilities within Alaigbo.

These two editions have further strengthened The Catalyst Symposium’s growing footprint, bringing the total number of successful editions to over ten.

According to the organisers, as the sparks ignited in Awka and Owerri continue to spread, The Catalyst Symposium remains committed to expanding this movement, creating more platforms, and supporting the next generation of leaders who will drive the sustainable development and generational wealth of the South-East and beyond.

World.title: UNIPGC Africa, JodelaTV, EduCore to Train 2026 Batch of Content Creators ahead of Nigeria at 66
World.content:
Onuminya Innocent in Sokoto

As Nigeria prepares to mark its 66th Independence anniversary, the African Continental Chapter of the United Nations International Peace and Governance Council, UNIPGC AFRICA, has announced plans to host an intensive capacity building masterclass for social media and content creators across the country.

The 2026 Social media & Content Creator Capacity Building Masterclass is being organised in collaboration with JodelaTV and EduCore Impact Organization. It will be held live in Lagos as part of activities lined up for Nigeria at 66 Peace and Governance Conference/Awards.

According to the organisers, the workshop is designed to radically elevate the skills, professionalism, and income potential of digital content creators, and to position Nigerian talent to compete effectively in the global digital economy.

The Global President and Chairman of the UNIPGC Supreme Council, His Excellency, Ambassador Jonathan Ojadah, said in a statement that the initiative was borne out of the need to bridge the gap between creativity and structure in Nigeria’s fast-growing creative sector.

“The Nigerian creative industry is overflowing with talent, but talent alone is no longer enough to compete globally,” Ambassador Ojadah said. “This masterclass bridges the gap between raw creativity and structural competence.”

He added that the programme will equip participants with the technical optimization and narrative power required to build sustainable, influential digital enterprises from Nigeria, while also aligning with global standards of digital governance and storytelling.

The masterclass will take place during the Nigeria at 66 Peace and Governance Conference / Awards, a high-level dialogue focused on strengthening democratic governance, investment promotion and peace building systems in the country. The theme for this year’s commemoration is: From Conflict to Consolidation: Strengthening Democracy & Traditional Institutions through Solidarity.

Organisers said the training will cover key areas including content strategy, platform algorithm mastery, monetization, brand partnerships, digital storytelling for impact, and professional ethics for content creators and digital journalists.

Applications are now officially open to eligible participants. To qualify, applicants must be active content creators, digital journalists, bloggers, podcasters, or video editors based in Nigeria, with a verifiable online platform or portfolio of at least six months of active content.

World.title: UNICEF Mobilises Katsina Religious Leaders for Child Health, Vaccination Drive
World.content:
Francis Sardauna in Katsina

The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) has enlisted Imams, pastors and other religious leaders across the 34 local government areas of Katsina State to leverage their influence and religious platforms to promote child vaccination, nutrition, education, healthcare and protection.

The interfaith leaders were enlisted during the unveiling of UNICEF’s Faith for Life initiative in Katsina, designed to harness scriptural teachings from the Bible and Qur’an to promote behaviours that improve the survival and development of children.

Addressing the clerics, the UNICEF Social and Behavioural Change Specialist, Kano Field Office, Dr Ogu Enemaku, said the initiative launched in collaboration with the Katsina State Government, seeks to improve children’s health, education, vaccination and protection.

He explained that the interfaith-based initiative provides relevant scriptural messages on health, nutrition, education and child protection that religious leaders should incorporate into their sermons, teachings and community engagements.

He urged the religious leaders to obtain, study and effectively utilise the Faith for Life materials to educate their followers and encourage families to make informed decisions on issues affecting the wellbeing of women and children across the state.

Also speaking, the Deputy Director, Community Outreach and Development, National Orientation Agency (NOA), Abuja, Amaka Aninta, challenged religious leaders to leverage their platforms to prevent avoidable deaths among children and pregnant women.

She said when religious teachings emphasise on the protection and wellbeing of mothers and children no child will die from vaccine-preventable diseases and no expectant mother will lose her life due to poor access to antenatal care or malnutrition.

She therefore urged the religious leaders to lead campaigns encouraging parents to vaccinate their children, pregnant women to attend antenatal care and families to take action against malnutrition and other challenges affecting mothers and children.

She admonished the enlisted religious leaders to also use Friday prayers, Islamic schools and church services to sensitise their communities on child protection, family welfare and responsible parenting.

Earlier, the Acting Executive Secretary of the Katsina State Primary Health Care Agency, Dr Shema’u Kabir Abba, described religious leaders as “special guides and advocates” and critical partners in driving positive behavioural change in communities.

She said the government could not address the challenges confronting primary healthcare alone, stressing that influential and respected voices within communities were needed to improve maternal and child health and nutrition outcomes.

She commended the religious leaders for their continued partnership with the government and urged them to sustain their support for initiatives aimed at strengthening healthcare delivery across the state.

World.title: Bandits Abduct Monarch, Another Monarch’s First Wife, Others in Kwara Communities
World.content:
Hammed Shittu in Ilorin

About 10 suspected bandits have reportedly abducted the traditional ruler of Igbesi town and other residents of the town in Isin Local Government Area of Kwara State.

Also, a woman identified as Iya Ayoka, the first wife of the Baale of Dabu community in Ifelodun Local Government Area of the state, was reportedly kidnapped in the town.

The latest attack on Kwara South senatorial communities happened despite the recent establishment of the Nigeria Army battalion formation in Omu-Aran town in Irepodun LGA of the state.

THISDAY checks revealed that the monarch was said to have been abducted during a fierce attack by the suspected bandits over the weekend in the town.

It was gathered that the monarch and other residents were said to have been taken to an unknown destination while the suspected bandits were yet to call any of the families for ransom.

Also, the first wife of the monarch of Dabu community, popularly called Iya Ayoka, was said to have been abducted in the town in Ifelodun LGA of the state by suspected bandits.

The abduction of Iya Ayoka, according to THISDAY checks over the weekend, has further increased fears among residents of Dabu and surrounding communities, particularly amid concerns over the activities of armed groups operating in parts of Kwara South.

Residents have continued to call for urgent intervention by security agencies to prevent further attacks and rescue those already in captivity.

Sources also disclosed to journalists in Ilorin yesterday that the bandits were said to be using the TikTok account of another kidnap victim, a 23-year-old woman identified as Babatunde Fasilat, to make posts while demanding a ransom for her release.

Fasilat was reportedly kidnapped on July 26, 2026, in Wande community.

According to a source familiar with the incident, the bandits invaded the community and abducted Fasilat after her father attempted to defend her.

“Her father was shot, and the bullet penetrated the other side of his body.

“The bandits were four. While her father was trying to defend himself, they went to her room and kidnapped her,” the source said.

The source added that the kidnappers have demanded N20 million as ransom before Fasilat would be released.

“Now, they are demanding N20 million before they can release her, and they are using her TikTok account to make a post,” the source said.

The use of the victim’s social media account has raised further concerns among residents, as the kidnappers appear to be using the platform to communicate and put pressure on the victim’s family to meet their ransom demand.

When contacted, senior police officers in the Ifelodun and Isin LGAs of the state who spoke with journalists in Ilorin yesterday on condition of anonymity confirmed the ugly development.

They, however, said: “We have sent a signal to the state Police Command on the ugly development and the Command has swung into action.

World.title: YPP Raises Concern over Citizens’ Exclusion, Calls for Extension of Voter Registration
World.content:
Alex Enumah in Abuja

The Young Progressive Party (YPP) has called on the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to extend the Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) exercise over fears that eligible Nigerians who are yet to register could be excluded from participating in the 2027 general election.

The Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Chairman of the YPP, Hon. Abraham Simon Adedotun, and the party’s FCT senatorial candidate, Blessing Ufedojo Benyeogor, who made the call at the weekend, appealed to the electoral umpire to reconsider the closure of the registration exercise and provide another opportunity for eligible citizens to register.

In a joint statement issued to journalists in Abuja, Adedotun and Benyeogor claimed that the closure of the CVR could disenfranchise many Nigerians, particularly young people who had not yet completed the registration process.

Meanwhile, they charged INEC to remain an impartial umpire and take steps that would strengthen public confidence in the electoral process and Nigeria’s democracy.

Recall that the Commission had initially scheduled the 2025–2026 CVR exercise to run until August 30, 2026. The Commission subsequently revised the timetable, setting an earlier operational deadline and later extending the final phase to July 26, 2026.

On July 26, INEC said the registration exercise would close that day, urging eligible Nigerians who had not registered to take advantage of the remaining time. The Commission later ruled out another extension, saying further delays could affect its preparations for the 2027 elections.

Meanwhile, INEC had also introduced a self-service online registration option during the final phase, allowing eligible first-time voters to complete the registration process electronically.

It should be noted that besides YPP, other political actors and civil society groups have expressed concern about access to voter registration and the need to ensure that eligible citizens are not left out of the electoral process.

They urged that the electoral umpire consider the appeals of Nigerians who were unable to register and to explore measures that would give eligible citizens another opportunity to be captured on the voters’ register.

As preparations for the 2027 elections continue, the debate over voter registration is likely to remain a significant issue, particularly given the importance of ensuring broad participation and public confidence in the electoral process.

World.title: THE RENEWED CASE FOR CATTLE RANCHING
World.content:
The plan to set up modern ranching settlements is overdue

In a renewed push to end recurring farmer-herder clashes and transform the livestock sector in the country, the federal government has announced plans to rehabilitate 417 grazing reserves and establish modern ranching settlements in six major conflict-prone areas. The Minister of Livestock Development, Idi Maiha listed the flashpoint states of Benue, Plateau, Nasarawa, Kaduna and Adamawa, as well as the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) as priority areas, adding that a pilot scheme in Plateau State is already on to test a livestock production model aimed at reducing cattle movement.

To secure the buy-in of critical stakeholders, the government has sought the support of the Grand Patron of Miyetti Allah, Sultan of Sokoto, Muhammadu Sa’ad Abubakar, and consulted pastoral communities for the transition from nomadic livestock production to ranching. Nomadic livestock production is becoming increasingly unsustainable because of disappearing grazing routes due to farming, urbanisation and infrastructure development. The ministry therefore envisaged a ranching model that would transform grazing reserves into economic communities with housing, veterinary clinics, schools, healthcare facilities, solar power and earth dams for pasture irrigation.

We have on several occasions made this point: In the history of humanity, the stage of development at which man wandered for a livelihood belongs to the stone age. It was in the bid to stem the incessant violent clashes between herdsmen and farmers, that almost all the states in the southern part of the country as well as two states in the North (Benue and Taraba) banned open grazing by livestock. With little variations that take care of peculiarities in these states, the law prohibits movement of livestock and open grazing as well as the carrying of firearms or other offensive weapons by herders. But to end the nomadic culture, we need a short, medium and long-term plans that would involve all the stakeholders.

It is heartwarming that the real conversation about how to modernise the way we rear cattle in the country has started, especially considering the threat nomadism continues to pose to our national security. When in August 2021 former President Muhammadu Buhari insisted on his controversial pledge to revive the contentious grazing routes for herders, the decision pitted him against sections of the country where open grazing has been banned because of the criminality and insecurity associated with it. As we argued then, even if the grazing routes were still valid, they can only facilitate further clashes between settler farmers and migrant herders. Besides, by allowing some people, including foreigners, to roam the length and breadth of Nigeria, our territorial integrity is being violated. We also violate the rights of these animals and endanger the health of citizens through exposure to the elements and a cocktail of diseases.

While migrant cattle herding has ceased in most parts of the world, it is unfortunate that Nigeria is still saddled with the problem. Modern ranches have replaced roving herds while beef production has become a modern mechanised industrial undertaking. Breed improvement would enable herders to keep fewer but more productive animals, besides reducing pressure on land. The federal government should therefore create the platform for a wholesale discussion on the future of animal husbandry in relations to the transition from nomadism to ranching. A package of incentives, including soft loans, liberal access to land, training, and provision of inputs to herders and others can help facilitate the transition and ameliorate the challenges associated with it.

If done properly, we can then employ and re-train the herdsmen in modern settled cattle farming. The animals will be healthier; the handlers will earn decent incomes, have decent accommodation, own property, and have schools for their kids. Ancillary industries will also emerge, and employment opportunities will blossom. It is time to impose civilisation on cattle farming.

World.title: ‘We’re Reversing Nigeria’s Medical Tourism, Raising Life Expectancy’
World.content:
Blessing Ibunge in Port Harcourt

Founder of Save-A-Life Mission Hospital, Port Harcourt, Dr Richard Okoye, has said Nigeria can reverse its medical tourism trend and improve its poor life expectancy through sustained investment in technology, local healthcare capacity and collaboration with Nigerian medical professionals abroad.

Okoye, a medical scientist, said he chose to remain in Nigeria despite the mass migration of medical professionals, popularly known as “Japa”, and instead invested in building what he described as a world-class, fully digitalised healthcare system.

Speaking during a press conference in Port Harcourt yesterday, he expressed concern that Nigeria’s doctor-to-patient ratio had deteriorated significantly, particularly in rural communities, where access to medical care remains limited.

According to him, the challenge goes beyond the number of doctors leaving the country, adding that the migration also represents a depletion of expertise and quality in the healthcare system.

He said the situation had contributed to Nigeria’s low life expectancy, stressing that maternal and child health remained major determinants of the country’s health outcomes.

Okoye said his intervention began in 2014 when he conceived the idea of developing technology capable of embedding international standards of medical practice into healthcare delivery.

He disclosed that work on the technology commenced in the United States in 2016 and had since evolved into a digital healthcare ecosystem deployed at Save-A-Life Mission Hospital and in underserved communities.

He said the hospital uses real-time monitoring, electronic medical records, artificial intelligence-assisted clinical decision support and a situation room where doctors monitor patients continuously.

According to him, the hospital’s “My Home Clinic” application enables patients to book appointments, provide medical information before consultations and receive professional guidance remotely.

He said the system could also assist doctors with differential diagnoses, recommended investigations and medication choices while blocking prescriptions that could be harmful to patients with certain conditions.

“This technology is not meant to replace doctors. It is meant to ensure that whatever anybody is doing is within the international standard of medical practice,” he said.

Okoye added that the technology was also being adapted for rural communities where electricity and internet connectivity remained major challenges.

He said the hospital had deployed solar-powered systems and satellite connectivity in some communities in Abia State, allowing health workers to transmit patients’ vital signs to doctors in real time.

The initiative, he said, includes remote monitoring devices for blood pressure, blood sugar and urine tests, particularly to detect complications among pregnant women.

He also disclosed plans to introduce an advanced ambulance system into Nigeria in October, describing it as a mobile emergency-care unit equipped with technology that would enable doctors to monitor patients remotely while in transit.

Okoye said the system would help bridge the gap between primary, secondary and tertiary healthcare facilities through triage and real-time referrals.

Beyond technology, he said Save-A-Life was creating a system through which Nigerian doctors based abroad could support patients in Nigeria remotely, while also returning periodically to train and work with local teams.

He noted that the model was already attracting patients from other states and countries, with Nigerians in the diaspora able to monitor the treatment of relatives receiving care in Port Harcourt.

The hospital, he said, was also investing in advanced procedures and equipment, including robotic technology, to provide treatments that Nigerians previously travelled abroad to obtain.

Okoye said the ultimate objective was to reverse medical tourism by making high-quality healthcare available domestically.

He said the economic benefits extended beyond healthcare, arguing that a healthy workforce was essential to productivity and national development.

“Your prosperity is tied to your health. The productivity of any company is directly proportional to the health of the individuals that make up that company,” he said.

He added that Save-A-Life had received interest from state governments, including the Abia State Government, in deploying aspects of its digital healthcare model across communities.

Okoye said the hospital currently attracts only about 30 per cent of its patients from Port Harcourt, with the majority coming from other states and countries.

He expressed optimism that continued investment in technology, training and healthcare infrastructure would place Nigeria on an upward trajectory in life expectancy and reduce the number of Nigerians travelling abroad for medical treatment.

World.title: Kumuyi Re-Appoints Ex-Fashola’s Aide, Prof Ope-Davis, into Anchor Varsity Council
World.content:
Sunday Okobi

The Chancellor and Proprietor of Anchor University, Ayobo, Lagos, Pastor William Folorunso Kumuyi, has reappointed former Governor Babatunde Fashola’s aide and University of Lagos Professor, Tunde Ope-Davies, as a member of the university’s Governing Council. The reappointment, which took immediate effect, is for another term of four years.

The reappointment, according to a statement from the university, is a testament to Professor Ope-Davies’s invaluable service during the university’s formative decade, particularly in his unique capacity as the representative of the Host Community, an institution builder and thoroughbred university administrator.

It said: “Since the university was founded 10 years ago, Prof. Ope-Davies has been instrumental in bridging the gap between academia and the wider Lagos community, embedding Anchor University firmly within the fabric of its immediate environment.

“As a distinguished scholar from the University of Lagos, and often described as the Father of Digital Humanities in Nigeria, Prof. Ope-Davies has worked tirelessly to ensure that Anchor University is not just a centre of learning, but a partner in the development of its host community.”

His philosophy of connecting “gown to town has translated into tangible initiatives that have enhanced the university’s relevance and deepened its roots in the region.

The statement noted that Ope-Davies’ notable contributions include pioneering the institutionalisation of community engagement, most famously through the establishment of the university’s first Distinguished Public Lecture series delivered by the Speaker of the Lagos State House of Assembly, Rt Hon. Mudashiru Obasa.

“This initiative was specifically designed to contribute intellectual resources to public debates, foster relationships with local stakeholders, and position the university as a catalyst for national development. He has also promoted international collaborations between Anchor University and some institutions abroad.

“He has equally extended his Digital Humanities initiative at the University of Lagos to Anchor University,” it stated.

In his response to the reappointment, Prof. Ope-Davies expressed gratitude to the chancellor for the confidence reposed in him. He reiterated his dedication to fostering the relationship between the university and its environment, ensuring that the institution continues to thrive as a beacon of knowledge that serves the needs of its immediate community and the nation at large.

The reappointment, he said, signals continuity and stability for the Anchor University Council, as it prepares to build on the “solid foundation” laid over the last ten years to take the institution to new heights.

Motorists in Cape Town face different waiting periods depending on which testing centre they use, with some applicants able to secure a test within days while others face waits of more than three months.

The City said it works to keep waiting times as short as possible, but acknowledged that backlogs can occur, often because applicants fail to arrive for scheduled tests.



Residents have been urged to follow the City’s testing guidelines when applying for a licence.

World.title: “Bring back my money” – McKenzie gives SAFA 21 days to return VAR Millions
World.content:
McKenzie revealed that he had formally written to SAFA demanding the VAR money back. He requested 21 days to respond to his demand.

The minister said that period has now passed without the funds being returned, leaving him frustrated over the stalled project.

GAYTON MCKENZIE DEMANDS STATE MONEY BACK

Speaking after the South African Sport Awards at Sun City on Sunday night, McKenzie made his frustration with SAFA clear.



“I wrote SAFA a letter where I said they should return my money, the money of the state, because I am responsible for it,” McKenzie said.

The minister said SAFA asked for 21 days to respond, but claimed that the deadline passed without the association returning the money.

“I am angry, because what more can I do? I asked them in a letter, bring back my money, the money of the state.”



The funding was intended to help introduce VAR in South African football, but the technology has yet to become a reality across the domestic game.

McKenzie insisted that he had done everything within his power to support the project and said football supporters should not blame him for the delays.

“We were supposed to have had the VAR. So people shouldn’t look at me. I’m the minister that put it on the table that the VAR should be there. I did everything humanly possible.”



Also read: McKenzie says Pitso Mosimane deserves white coach salary



SAFA FACES PRESSURE OVER VAR

The minister has now indicated that he will escalate the matter to FIFA after failing to resolve the issue through his correspondence with SAFA.

“Now I’m writing to FIFA. I’ve already spoken to FIFA, but I’m writing to them,” he said.



McKenzie also accused SAFA of corruption, further intensifying the public dispute between the government and the country’s football governing body.

Those allegations remain claims made by McKenzie and have not been independently established. The latest development puts additional pressure on SAFA to account for the state funding and explain the status of the VAR project.

For McKenzie, however, the message is clear: the money must be accounted for. “Bring back my money.”

World.title: Wheels come off for illegal street racers in Mitchells Plain
World.content:
Three motorists have had their vehicles impounded after being caught participating in illegal street racing in Mitchells Plain over the weekend. Image: City of Cape Town website

Three motorists have had their vehicles impounded after being caught participating in illegal street racing in Mitchells Plain over the weekend.

The arrests formed part of a City of Cape Town Traffic Services operation conducted on Saturday evening targeting illegal street racing and other dangerous driving offences.

Officers arrested seven people for driving under the influence of alcohol, three for reckless and negligent driving, and one person for displaying a false licence plate.



Three vehicles were impounded for allegedly participating in illegal street races under the amended Traffic By-Law.

Welcomed the enforcement action

Mayoral Committee Member for Safety and Security, Alderman JP Smith, welcomed the enforcement action.

“It is very satisfying to see the by-law amendments in effect,” Smith said.

He said motorists previously faced little financial consequence after being arrested, as they could potentially return to the road soon after their release.

“Now, retrieving their vehicles is a costly and time-consuming exercise – even more so if it is linked to a criminal matter,” he said.

“Hopefully, this will make those scofflaws think twice in future about breaking the law and endangering the lives of others.”



Fee to be paid

Under the amended by-law, a vehicle impounded solely for a by-law transgression can be released once the applicable R2 500 fee has been paid.

However, vehicles linked to a South African Police Service (SAPS) case or criminal court matter must remain in the pound until the matter has been finalised.

A court order authorising the vehicle’s release must then be obtained, with the owner also required to pay the applicable impoundment release fee.

More than 60 000 fines issued

The street-racing operation was part of wider traffic enforcement efforts across the city over the past week.

Traffic Officers recorded 68 arrests, including arrests for driving under the influence, reckless or negligent driving and other offences.

They also issued 60 410 fines, executed 1 918 warrants of arrest and impounded 102 public transport vehicles.

Meanwhile, Metro Police officers made 136 arrests, including 43 for drunk driving, and issued 6 879 fines.

They also recovered 16 stolen or hijacked vehicles, as well as a firearm, an imitation firearm and various quantities of drugs.

The City’s Law Enforcement officers made a further 262 arrests and issued 12 978 notices.

Road accidents among weekend emergencies

The City’s Public Emergency Communication Centre recorded 2 593 calls for assistance over the weekend.

These included 120 cases of physical assault, 74 domestic violence incidents and 83 road accidents, 21 of which involved pedestrians.

Residents are urged to report emergencies or suspicious or criminal activity to the Public Emergency Communication Centre on (021) 480 7700.

Traffic and by-law-related complaints can also be reported through the Safety and Security add-on on the City of Cape Town App.

World.title: Sports Minister: Pitso Mosimane deserves white coach salary
World.content:
Sports, Arts and Culture Minister Gayton McKenzie has urged SAFA to pay Pitso Mosimane fairly. He is arguing that the decorated coach deserves the same starting salary as former Bafana Bafana mentor Hugo Broos.

SAFA’s National Executive Committee approved Mosimane’s appointment on August 8, but the association has not officially announced the coach because negotiations over his contract remain unresolved.

GAYTON MCKENZIE BACKS PITSO MOSIMANE

The delay comes at a difficult time for Bafana Bafana. The CAF Africa Cup of Nations 2027 qualifiers set to begin in September.



South Africa have been drawn in Group D alongside Guinea, Eritrea and Kenya. Bafana Bafana are scheduled to face Guinea and Eritrea in September before playing Kenya twice in November.

Speaking at the South African Sport Awards on Sunday evening, McKenzie questioned why SAFA had taken so long to finalise Mosimane’s contract.

“You know, I don’t understand what’s going on. I’m going to get a report because I have been told that Pitso Mosimane is our coach,” said McKenzie.



The minister then addressed the salary negotiations. He has said SAFA should not undervalue a successful black coach while paying white coaches more.

“Also, we must be honest. We come from a country where black people were paid less than white people. Those scars haven’t healed for many people. But we, as black people, cannot do the same thing that has been done to us, where we pay the white man more.”

McKenzie believes Mosimane’s coaching achievements justify a competitive salary, particularly after the coach won the CAF Champions League three times during his career.



SAFA URGED TO VALUE MOSIMANE

The minister insisted that Pitso Mosimane should not be treated like an inexperienced coach, highlighting his success with Mamelodi Sundowns, Al Ahly and other clubs.

“Pitso Mosimane is not a coach of the ABC Motsepe League. Let us be straight about that issue. It’s like we are scared of white people, where we pay them more, but when it comes to black people, it’s a different story,” he added.

McKenzie specifically called for Pitso Mosimane to receive at least the same starting salary that Broos received when he took charge of Bafana Bafana.



“Pitso Mosimane should be paid. The least they could do is start him with the same salary they started with Hugo Broos. Black people are still hurt that they were underpaid and undervalued; we cannot have that.”

With the AFCON 2027 qualifiers approaching, SAFA faces increasing pressure to conclude the negotiations. The latest report suggests the deal is done, and the official announcement is expected this week.

World.title: DA to grill Gayton McKenzie in parliament on Tuesday
World.content:
Sports Minister Gayton McKenzie is set to face renewed questions over the Department of Sport, Arts and Culture’s spending on its delegation to the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Image: ChatGPT

Sports Minister Gayton McKenzie is set to face renewed questions over the Department of Sport, Arts and Culture’s spending on its delegation to the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

McKenzie and department officials are scheduled to appear before Parliament’s Portfolio Committee on Sport, Arts and Culture on Tuesday, 25 August at 17:30.

READ | DA accuses Gayton McKenzie of crippling South Africa’s film and TV industry



The appearance follows a contentious committee meeting on 4 August, when members raised concerns about the Department’s presentation on the World Cup delegation and related expenditure.

Provide detailed account of spending

The Democratic Alliance (DA) has called on Gayton McKenzie to provide a detailed account of the estimated R31 million spent on the delegation and to explain the rationale behind the inclusion of 151 delegates.

DA spokesperson on Sport, Arts and Culture Leah Potgieter MP is expected to again press the Gayton McKenzie and his department for detailed information on the delegation.



Among the questions the DA wants answered are the full names, qualifications and relevant experience of all 151 delegates, as well as their respective roles and responsibilities.

The party also wants the department to provide an account of what each delegate did during the World Cup and details of meetings and engagements involving the minister and delegation members.

A detailed breakdown of the estimated R31 million expenditure is also being sought, including the costs attributable to individual delegates.



The DA is further calling for full disclosure of sponsorships received in connection with the delegation.

It also wants the department to demonstrate what tangible benefits South Africa received in return for the expenditure.

According to the party, the report should provide measurable outcomes relating to South African sport, arts, culture, tourism and associated industries.



The renewed scrutiny comes after committee members previously rejected what the DA described as an inadequate presentation and called for a more comprehensive report.

Justified

The committee is now expected to examine whether the department has supplied the detailed information requested and whether the expenditure can be adequately justified.

The World Cup delegation and its associated costs have attracted political scrutiny, with opposition parties demanding greater transparency over the use of public funds.



Gayton McKenzie and the department will have an opportunity to respond to the concerns when they appear before the committee on Tuesday.

The meeting is expected to place the focus firmly on how the delegation was constituted, how public money was spent and what measurable outcomes were achieved from South Africa’s participation at the tournament.

World.title: Springboks change half-backs for second All Blacks Test
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Springboks have changed their half-backs for the second Test against New Zealand on Saturday in Cape Town, promoting experienced duo Handre Pollard and Cobus Reinach.

Fly-half Pollard and scrum-half Reinach replace Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu, now on the bench, and Grant Williams, who is unavailable due to a "niggle".

The changes were predictable as Feinberg-Mngomezulu, playing only his second match after injury, and Williams performed poorly in a 33-16 first Test loss last Saturday.

A third alteration to the team that fell in Johannesburg is Ethan Hooker coming in on the left wing in place of Kurt-Lee Arendse.

Arendse, who went off concussed early in the match at Ellis Park, moves to the right wing in place of Cheslin Kolbe, another "niggle" casualty.

There could yet be a fourth change to the starting line-up. If flanker Siya Kolisi is passed fit after a hamstring injury, he will replace Paul de Villiers.

"Handre has delivered for us under extreme pressure, and we feel that is what he and Cobus have the potential to bring at the beginning of the game," said head coach Rassie Erasmus.

"Then we have Morne (van den Berg) and Sacha coming on later with their different styles of play that will be good for us this weekend.

"Cheslin and Grant suffered niggles last weekend, which ruled them out of contention for selection.

"We have bracketed Siya alongside Paul to allow us time to monitor how Siya comes through training this week."

Loose forward Pieter-Steph du Toit will continue as captain and is set to win his 100th cap on Saturday, one week after centre Damian de Allende reached the milestone.

Ox Nche, widely regarded as the best loosehead prop in the world, will make his 50th appearance for the Springboks.

The bench has been reshuffled with only two survivors from the first Test -- 'hybrid' player Andre Esterhuizen, a centre who can play as a loose forward, and prop Gerhard Steenekamp.

Among those promoted is Deon Fourie, who will celebrate his 40th birthday in September. He can operate as a hooker or flanker.

Should he take the field, Fourie will become the oldest Springbok to play in a Test, surpassing Victor Matfield and Schalk Brits, who were 38 years old in their final Tests.

South Africa (15-1)

Damian Willemse; Kurt-Lee Arendse, Jesse Kriel, Damian de Allende, Ethan Hooker; Handre Pollard, Cobus Reinach; Jasper Wiese, Pieter-Steph du Toit (capt), Siya Kolisi or Paul de Villiers; Ruan Nortje, Eben Etzebeth; Wilco Louw, Malcolm Marx, Ox Nche

Replacements: Deon Fourie, Gerhard Steenekamp, Thomas du Toit, Lood de Jager, Andre Esterhuizen, Cameron Hanekom, Morne van den Berg, Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu

Coach: Rassie Erasmus

World.title: Four arrested for Tete murder
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Police say they have arrested four people in connection with the murder of two-time boxing world champion Zolani Tete, who was gunned down last week.



Tete, 38, was attacked on Friday evening as he returned to his home in Mdantsane in the Eastern Cape.



A 27-year-old woman who was with him in the car survived but is in hospital, police said.



The four suspects arrested over the weekend are aged between 22 and 28, police said in a statement.

One has been formally charged with murder.



Tete won the IBF junior-bantamweight world title in 2014 and the WBO bantamweight world title in 2017.



In 2017, he entered boxing history when he took just 11 seconds to flatten his opponent with his first punch to retain his WBO bantamweight crown.



It was the fastest knockout victory in a world championship bout.



In 2023, the UK Anti-Doping Agency hit Tete with a four-year ban that ended on July 29 and he was preparing to return to professional boxing.



"South Africa has lost one of the finest fighters it has ever produced," Sports Minister Gayton McKenzie said in a statement.



"He was training for a return to the ring. He believed he still had something to give this country. He was right, but he will not get the chance now. He, and all of us, have been robbed."

World.title: Still on old SASSA card? Here’s what you need to do before 31 August
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Social grant beneficiaries have until 31 August to migrate to the new black card.

Postbank says more than 1.8 million beneficiaries have already migrated.

It is urging those who have not yet done so to act quickly.

Postbank says additional measures have been put in place at card replacement sites, to manage the expected increase in beneficiaries in the final days.

READ | SASSA faces growing demand as grant beneficiaries near 20 million

The card migration process is free of charge and beneficiaries are required to have a valid or temporary ID.

Cards can be collected from any province, even if that is not the province in which a person’s SASSA grant was approved.

To migrate from an old SASSA Gold Card to the new Postbank Black Card, take your valid South African ID (or temporary ID) and your current gold card to a designated card replacement site, major retailer (such as Shoprite, Checkers, Usave, Boxer, Pick n Pay, or Spar), or participating Postbank site.

World.title: Devi | Rentoza | 23 August 2026
World.content:
Need a new phone? A laptop? A fridge? It’s rarely as simple as adding something to your cart and checking out – with credit hard to come by and the cost of living only climbing.

Enter Rentoza, with a simple pitch: why buy when you can subscribe? Monthly payments give South Africans access to the tech they need – with ownership at the end.

But hundreds of clients say the dream subscription became a monthly nightmare.

From refunds missing in action to contracts with apparent end dates – yet the debits keep rolling, month after month.

Initially, Rentoza’s management seemed eager to lay it all bare. But that enthusiasm quickly hit the rocks. So, we did things the old-fashioned way – and set up a sting.

Let’s just say… our surprise wasn’t exactly well received.

World.title: Bring back the VAR money, Gayton McKenzie tells SAFA
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Sports Minister Gayton McKenzie has slammed the South African Football Association (SAFA) over delays in implementing the Video Assistant Referee (VAR) system and now wants the association to pay back the money he provided for the project.

McKenzie says he has asked SAFA to return the R13 million he gave the association to help fund the implementation of VAR.

“I wrote a letter to SAFA and said they must return the money. They asked for 21 days’ grace. I am just as angry, because what more can I do? I asked them to bring back the money of the state because I am responsible for it,” McKenzie said.

READ | Disputed decision set to reignite calls for VAR in SA

McKenzie had previously promised that VAR would be implemented during the current season, but the technology has yet to be introduced.

The Minister insists he has done his part and says SAFA has failed to act.

“FIFA’s rules state clearly that it has to happen through SAFA. I took journalists and administrators to Spain and the UK to compare which one is the best for us. I can’t do more as a minister. What else can I do?”

World.title: ‘ANC cannot be trusted to fix what it has broken’ - DA
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - The Democratic Alliance has slammed the ANC’s manifesto as "implausible".

The party says the ANC cannot be trusted to fix what it has broken.

The ANC launched its manifesto at the weekend ahead of the 4 November Local Government Elections, promising to turn around municipalities.

But the DA says the manifesto asks South Africans to believe that the same party that has presided over the collapse of municipalities across the country will suddenly fix them again.

“These promises are implausible and lack all integrity,” DA leader Geordin Hill-Lewis said in a statement.

“The ANC cannot be trusted to fix what it has broken."

“South Africans deserve a different future with local governments that work, and ultimately a DA-led national government that brings the same culture of accountability, competence and service to the whole country,” Hill-Lewis added.

READ | ANC launches election manifesto in Diepsloot

While admitting his party’s failures over the years, ANC president Cyril Ramaphosa promised South Africans that they will do better.

“There are municipalities, we must admit, that are in financial trouble. There are municipalities that have been weakened by poor leadership, political instability, corruption and the appointment of people who do not have the skills required for the work that they must perform.

“Now, as the ANC, we comrades accept responsibility both for the progress that has been made, but we also accept responsibility for the failures and shortcomings where we govern,” Ramaphosa said.

He added that if citizens vote for the party, work will begin immediately after election day.

But the DA maintains the ANC will not perform miracles in 100 days and fill every critical municipal vacancy within 120 days.

World.title: Shein grapples with EU backlash, but clients keep coming
World.content:
BEIJING - Shein's meteoric growth has made it a lightning rod for critics of ultrafast fashion in Europe, where officials are trying to rein in its operations in the name of social and environmental responsibility.

The probes, financial penalties and fierce debates have dampened but not fully curbed the enthusiasm of millions of clients in a key market for the China-founded online juggernaut.

The company's $1.7 billion stock market listing, announced on Monday, aims in particular to juice its international expansion.

- Short-lived Paris store -

Starting in 2012, Shein began online sales of its continually renewed stock of tops, dresses and other items, drastically undercutting the prices of its rivals -- to say nothing of traditional clothing stores.

Its European customer base rose to 156 million average monthly users by the end of last year, making Shein one of the continent's biggest e-commerce platforms alongside China's AliExpress (193 million users), and Amazon (around 180 million).

In November, the group made waves with its first-ever physical outlet, a dedicated space in the storied BHV department store in Paris.

Hundreds of customers lined up on its opening day, and dozens more people gathered to protest, requiring a heavy police presence to keep the tense situation from getting out of hand.

Demonstrators slammed what they called inhumane working conditions at Shein's suppliers, the environmental costs of selling clothes not made to last, and unfair competition against brick-and-mortar retailers struggling to stay open.

The company says it holds its suppliers to strict compliance standards and does not tolerate forced labour.

- Sex doll scandal -

It did not help that just a few days before the Paris opening, France's consumer protection agency said it had discovered childlike sex dolls for sale on Shein's platform.

Accusing the company of fostering child pornography, French officials asked the European Commission to open an inquiry under the bloc's wide-reaching Digital Services Act.

The EU investigation that opened in February 2026 targeted the sale of illicit goods "including child sexual abuse material" as well as what it alleged was Shein's "addictive design".

In June, French authorities imposed two fines on Shein totalling more than 22 million euros ($25 million), citing problems with product traceability, environmental labelling and delivery times.

The next month it secured an EU-wide halt on the sales of items with crocodile logos -- deemed a counterfeit of France's famed Lacoste brand of polo shirts.

Overall, Shein has paid over 210 million euros in various French fines over the years, and Italy has also imposed fines alleging misleading environmental claims.

In June, the BHV's new owners said they would part ways with Shein, calling the decision to welcome a physical outlet a "strategic error".

- Regulatory pushback -

Shein has called the penalties "disproportionate and discriminatory", while China's commerce ministry says they violate World Trade Organization rules.

That did not stop the European Union from imposing duties on the billions of small, inexpensive retail parcels entering the bloc each year -- most of them from Chinese e-commerce sites.

Since July, a duty of three euros per item applies to packages valued at less than 150 euros, similar to a move last year by US President Donald Trump's administration against products originating in China.

But the EU fee applies to the type of item imported, not the number. So a person buying five T-shirts pays just three euros, but someone buying a T-shirt, jeans and socks would pay nine euros.

Brussels says the duty helps compensate for overwhelmed customs authorities given the popularity of e-commerce, in particular for clothes and other items from China and elsewhere that do not comply with EU standards.

According to the head of the European Parliament's trade committee, Bernd Lange, the number of small parcels from abroad have more than quadrupled to 5.88 billion since 2022.

Starting in November, the EU will impose a still-undetermined handling fee on such parcels.

It is far from clear how effective the duties will be, especially as online giants like Shein could build warehouses in Europe to limit the impact.

After France imposed its own duty of two euros on such parcels this year -- before the EU system kicked in -- the customs office estimated it brought in around 2.3 million euros per month.

That was far below the 33 million euros per month the government had expected in the 2026 budget.

World.title: Cummins eyes ODI return ahead of 'big' SA Test series
World.content:
MACKAY - Skipper Pat Cummins said he "can't wait" to play in Australia's first Test series in South Africa since the infamous "Sandpapergate" affair and he intends to use one-day games beforehand to prepare.

The next assignment for Australia after drawing a two-Test series against Bangladesh are three ODIs in Zimbabwe and another three in South Africa in late September.

They then play Tests in Durban, Gqeberha and Cape Town in October.

Cummins indicated he could miss the Zimbabwe leg, but would make himself available for some of the South Africa white-ball games.

It is likely to be a similar scenario for fellow quicks Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood.

"I'm not sure I should say this, but I think the focus is on the Test series," said Cummins after their innings and 51-run thrashing of Bangladesh in Mackay on Sunday.

"So a lot of the white-ball (series), and how we play that, would be with an eye to the red ball.

"So I'd imagine it'd be one, two, probably a maximum of three games out of those six."

Cummins, who remains Australia's official ODI captain, has played just two from a possible 28 matches in the format since the 2023 World Cup.

Hazlewood told reporters in Mackay he too expected to play some of the 50-over series while Starc said he would "do what he's told".

All three have prioritised Tests over limited-overs cricket in recent years.

The Tests in South Africa will be Australia's first in the country since a 2018 ball-tampering scandal rocked the sport.

Steve Smith was banned for a year and sacked as captain after conspiring to alter the ball using sandpaper during the third Test in Cape Town, while David Warner was suspended for 12 months.

Cummins called the series "big" with revenge on his mind after Australia lost the World Test Championship final to the Proteas at Lord's last year.

"We had a big series against them a couple of years ago in Australia (in 2022-23) and we probably exceeded expectations and played really well," said Cummins of their 2-0 series win.

"They got us back at Lord's last year and outplayed us. So it's going to be big in their home conditions and places we haven't played for quite a while.

"Even the difference between Durban to, say, Cape Town can be quite different styles of pitches.

"That's why I love playing Test cricket. It's all different conditions, different opponents, different parts of the world. Can't wait."

Only Cummins, Starc, Hazlewood, Smith, Nathan Lyon, and Matt Renshaw have played Test cricket in South Africa.

Opener Renshaw is likely to hold his place despite a tepid return in Mackay after three years away, with the big question whether Marnus Labuschagne should be on the plane.

The number three made just 36 runs in three knocks against Bangladesh and has not scored a century since 2023.

"I did say a couple of days ago -– and I think it still stands -– that he's been batting fantastically well off the field," said Cummins. "But it doesn't mean much. You've got to convert that into runs out there."

World.title: Why lawyer Angela Mulwa has been re-arrested
World.content:
City lawyer Angela Mulwa has this afternoon been re-arrested outside the Milimani Law Court. [Nancy Gitonga, Standard]

City lawyer Angela Mulwa has this afternoon been re-arrested outside the Milimani Law Court in connection with the murder of her stepmother, Dr Victoria Mutiso.

The arrest came shortly after the Director of Public Prosecutions Renson Ingonga recommended that the law be charged with the murder of the deceased.

World.title: Ndindi Nyoro begins nationwide political mobilisation ahead of 2027
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro after attending service at Gathuki-ini ACK Church on August 23, 2026. [Boniface Gikandi, Standard]

Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro has said he will take his campaign for national transformation across Kenya as he positions himself for the 2027 presidential race.

Ndindi said he was interested in leadership committed to addressing concerns in education, health, youth and unemployment, among other needs.

Nyoro, who is the People’s Party of Kenya leader, spoke at St Michael Gathuki-ini ACK Church in Kiharu on Sunday, where he called for respect and political maturity.

Addressing residents in Kiria-ini (Mathioya) and Gakira (Kangema), he urged politicians to engage in a responsible manner.

“I trust in God that after next year Kenya will be able to have leadership that will be responsible for improving citizens' standards of living,” he said.

He regretted that hundreds of university graduates in the area were yet to secure employment.

“I plead with Kenyans to support my course that is geared to transform the nation and ensure equality and transparency,” said the PPK leader.

Nyoro said that after engaging Murang'a residents, he will take his transformation campaigns to all parts of the country.

Speaking at Kiria-ini market, he said he would engage the people to seek their blessings.

“All along had been feeling the urge to lead the country, thus the need to come out in the open and fight for position,” he said.

On Monday, the MP announced his exit from the ruling United Democratic Alliance (UDA), declaring that he will join the opposition ahead of the 2027 General Election.

Nyoro, an economist serving his second term as Kiharu MP, said he will work with opposition leaders to push for what he termed real change in Kenya.

The legislator said all opposition presidential aspirants are welcome at rallies organised by the PPK.

His move marks a significant political shift as parties and leaders begin positioning themselves ahead of the 2027 polls.

World.title: City Hall in rush to expand drainage system ahead of El Nino
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja during an inspection tour of the ongoing drainage system expansion. [GPS]

Nairobi County has embarked on drainage expansion works aimed at mitigating floodwaters ahead of El Nino rains.

Governor Johnson Sakaja, while calling on city residents to remain alert and proactive, said City Hall has intensified preparations and accelerated identification of hotspots.

The governor on Friday said his administration is taking early and coordinated action to minimise the impact of heavy rains, urging residents to stay calm, pay attention to official information and follow guidance from the multi-agency team established to coordinate the city’s preparedness and emergency response.

“We are working proactively to address the challenges of flooding before El Nino hits the ground. We urge our people not to panic but to be alert and get information from our multi-agency team,” said Sakaja.

The Governor spoke during an inspection tour of several flood-prone areas in Nairobi, including the Mombasa Road-Bunyala Junction corridor and Globe Roundabout, which experienced significant flooding during previous heavy rains.

Sakaja said drainage works are already underway in the affected areas, with teams working to open up and deepen drainage channels, clear obstructions, and improve storm-water flow to prevent a repeat of the flooding witnessed previously.

His remarks come as weatherman warned of increased rainfall in the coming months, with Nairobi among the urban areas requiring heightened preparedness because of its exposure to flooding and the impact of heavy rainfall on roads, settlements and other critical infrastructure.

Sakaja said the county has so far brought together the disaster management teams, Kenya Red Cross, Kenya Urban Roads Authority (KURA) and Kenya National Highways Authority (KeNHA) under a coordinated programme worth Sh2.4 billion to strengthen Nairobi’s flood resilience.

Of the amount, Sh2 billion has been set aside for drainage and flood-mitigation works targeting 19 roads in flood-prone areas.

The projects are at an advanced stage, with tenders awarded and contractors expected to commence implementation after completion of the necessary processes.

Sakaja reiterated that the programme will complement ongoing county interventions under the Nairobi Regeneration Programme, which includes the rehabilitation and upgrading of critical infrastructure across the city.

“The Sh2 billion will support a comprehensive drainage overhaul that complements the ongoing Nairobi Regeneration Programme. Our goal is to permanently address the flooding challenges that have affected the city for many years,” Sakaja said.
