World.title: Baćina Lakes – Meet Croatia’s Freshwater Phenomenon
World.content:
August the 24th, 2026 – Baćina Lakes are Croatia’s freshwater phenomenon, with water warmer than that in the sea and the ability to swim year-round.

If you’ve ever driven from Makarska down toward Dubrovnik, you’ll have passed by them. You probably glanced left for a second, spotted a blue patch amid the greenery, and continued on toward the sea. Yet there, just a few kilometres from Ploče, lies something no other Croatian town has: seven lakes within the boundaries of a single town. They are called the Baćina Lakes and bear names that sound like a list from an old book: Oćuša, Crniševo, Podgora, Sladinac, Šipak, Plitko Lake, and Vrbnik.

Putni kofer writes that six of them are interconnected by narrow passages, so you can paddle or boat from one into another, while Vrbnik, which is also the smallest, is completely separate from the rest. Together they cover about 138 hectares.

they’re warmer than the sea

The Baćina Lakes form a cryptodepression, meaning their surface is only slightly above sea level, while their bottoms lie deep below it. Although they are just a step from the sea and surrounded by permeable limestone, the lakes are freshwater. Some springs are nevertheless directly connected to the sea, so salt water appears in the deeper layers. In the Klokun area near Plitko Lake there is a spring that supplies drinking water to the town of Ploče and the surrounding area.

During the scorching summer, the water in the lakes is noticeably warmer than the sea, with tourist sources citing a difference of roughly three degrees. Because of this, the swimming season here starts earlier and ends later than on the coast. The best-known bathing spots are those near the Mindel spring, and the hidden coves and small beaches are reached by kayak, paddleboard, or traditional Neretva boat.

links with queen teuta

Legend has it that the Illyrian Queen Teuta adored this area, and the lakes are still called Teuta’s pearls. Historians, however, have their own evidence and explanations. Near Sladinac Lake the remains of the Roman settlement of Praetoria have been found, along with the remains of an early Christian basilica from the 6th century and a necropolis of stećci tombstones.

Around the lakes a walking and cycling path about 15 kilometres long has been arranged, with benches, springs, and information boards. In 2020 the Public Institution for Protected Natural Areas of Dubrovnik-Neretva County installed 19 educational boards about dragonflies, amphibians, reptiles, and birds. Near the Oćuša spring there is a bird-watching hide, and the lakes also contain three small islets, one of which is named the Island of Love. The entire area forms part of the Natura 2000 ecological network, within two zones of the Neretva Delta, as a habitat for strictly protected and endemic species.

a worthwhile stop off on a long drive south…

A visit to the Baćina Lakes is truly an experience you will remember for a lifetime. Walking the paths that wind right beside the lakes will reveal scenes covered in water lilies, the reflection of clouds mirrored on the still water, and the song of rare birds that creates an almost meditative atmosphere.

Here you can also swim in crystal-clear water that provides refreshment during the great heat, and a special experience comes when the sun sets and the whole landscape is immersed in golden and pink tones. Then the lakes take on an almost fairy-tale appearance. It is a perfect moment for a photograph, but also for simply enjoying the silence of nature.

In the heart of the summer season, a parking space at the viewpoint along the main road is almost impossible to find. Down by the lakes themselves, however, there are usually no crowds. Most travellers photograph the view and drive on, while those who go down to the water, sit in a boat, or cycle a loop are completely enchanted and, like us, probably think: “How is this place not far better known?”

World.title: Croatia Isn’t Facing a Fuel Shortage, But Prices Will Rise
World.content:
August the 23rd, 2026 – Croatia isn’t facing any sort of genuine fuel shortage, but experts are warning that prices will definitely rise.

Diesel shortages aren’t a realistic threat to Croatia, but prices will very likely rise again, warns energy expert Jasminko Umičević. He sees the problem in the lack of refining capacity in Europe and disruptions in supply. Poslovni reports that energy expert Jasminko Umičević spoke about the situation on the energy market, potential shortages and price movements for HRT.

Owing to disruptions on the global oil market and supply problems, concern is growing about the availability of diesel. Energy expert Jasminko Umičević believes there is no real danger of shortages in Croatia, although prices could remain high. “I don’t think there’s any real fear that shortages will occur. I believe high prices will continue, and that is the biggest problem. Regardless of the fact that the diesel market is very tight, especially across Europe. The main reason at this moment is the Strait of Hormuz and all the problems that stem from it,” says Umičević.

He also sees a problem in the structure of European refineries, which do not have sufficient capacity to produce diesel, while Europe has significantly higher consumption of this fuel than, for example, the United States. “European refineries are under-capacitated for sufficient diesel production, because the European market is a diesel market. Today we are in a situation where Europe has reduced its refining capacity by 30 percent over the last 20 years or so. Under the motto: better to import than to produce. And these are the results now,” he stresses. An additional problem for supply is the change in the sources from which Europe obtains all of its diesel.

“Previously the main source was Russia. After the sanctions everything shifted to Arab countries. Now we have a problem with the Arab countries. And recently there have been major problems, after the Ukrainian ones, with the new tactics of destroying refineries. That’s why there is no diesel. The market is tight, it’s always like that – when supply is lower, prices are higher,” he explains.

rijeka’s refinery still isn’t operating at full capacity

For Croatia in particular, the Rijeka refinery is particularly important, but its operation was briefly disrupted on Friday by a lightning strike on a substation. Umičević believes that if the problem is only with the substation, the fault could be fixed relatively quickly, but stresses that this is a situation that should not be ignored. He added that the Rijeka refinery is in any case not yet operating at full capacity because certain tests are still expected to be completed, and it should reach full capacity next year. “Especially now, the Rijeka refinery is not operating at full capacity, because the completion of some tests is still expected. Only next year will Rijeka operate at full capacity. But what is important right now is that there is production, so we aren’t dependent on imports,” he noted.

diesel prices will probably increase again

Diesel prices could rise again from next week, Umičević believes. Although the oil price has fallen in the meantime, the diesel price has remained high and continues to rise. “I think prices will rise again next week, for a very simple reason – the diesel price is rising, as is the petrol price. What is absurd, or a paradox, is that oil prices have not risen as much as the diesel price in particular,” says Umičević. “At the beginning of the Iran-US conflict in the Strait of Hormuz the oil price was around 71 dollars per barrel, and at its highest it reached 126 dollars. The diesel price then rose from around 750 to 1,300 dollars. After the situation calmed down, oil fell to around 90, and today it is around 94 dollars, while the diesel price has remained practically the same and continues to rise,” he states.

He nevertheless expects that any price increase will not be large, but notes that the final decision also depends on the Government.

“there will be enough gas, but the price of it is another thing”

As for gas, Umičević believes that the goal of filling Croatia’s Okoli storage facility to 85 percent by the 1st of October is realistic. “A month or a month and a half ago we were at around 51 percent full. Croatia has enough gas and a relatively good mix of sources – we have the LNG terminal, domestic production (which is smaller, admittedly), and diversified other sources. I think it is realistic for Croatia to reach 85 percent,” says Umičević.

He added that one of the problems is that the gas price on the futures market is lower than the current one, so storage users do not find it profitable to buy gas now at higher prices. “The key problem is that future gas prices are lower than current ones. That’s why it doesn’t pay for storage users to buy now at high prices and later sell at lower ones. However, the Government has taken certain decisions, and HEP has been given the task of filling the storage to 85 percent,” he said.

He believes there is currently no reason for concern about gas quantities, but stresses that the question of price is something else. “There will be enough gas, just as there will be enough diesel, the only question is at what price it will be sold at. Gas prices have seriously fluctuated, and after the initial summer price increase the situation has stabilised somewhat. When everything is averaged out, there should not be a significant increase in the gas price either, especially because the state already subsidises the price,” he concluded.

World.title: German Tourists Cause Fire Inside Poreč Apartment Ending With €400,000 in Damage
World.content:
August the 23rd, 2026 – German tourists have caused enormous damage after causing a fire inside a Poreč apartment. As if that wasn’t enough, he allegedly stuck his middle finger up at the owner after the act.

German tourists caused a fire in a Poreč apartment inside a family home two weeks ago, according to a police investigation. The fire destroyed almost the entire apartment, and owner Markica Kikić estimates the damage at around €400,000. Kikić has now revealed new details of the entire incident. Index reports that he claimed that some of the guests obstructed the firefighting efforts during the blaze and is also deeply dissatisfied with the police response. “The guests simply got in the way, obstructed and interfered with putting out the fire. In the meantime the police arrived and somehow managed to move them aside,” Kikić said.

“he was getting in my face and even stuck his middle finger up at me”

He claims that one of the guests still did not calm down even after the police arrived. “One of those people was sticking his middle finger under my nose and getting right in my face. The police were removing me from him instead of throwing him out. He wasn’t registered and had no right to be on my private property. The police removed me and gave them priority,” he alleged.

Kikić also claimed there were major shortcomings in the police’s handling of the whole situation. “Believe me, there were major failings on the part of the police. They gave them documents so they could fill in their own names, surnames and the rest themselves. They didn’t take them in. The police didn’t even take a statement from them. They signed and left,” he claimed. He considers the situation was serious enough to require a stricter police response.

“This is a criminal offence of endangering life and property. In such a case, as far as I as a layman know the law, the person has to be taken in and detained,” Kikić said.

he was coming back from the beach when he noticed the flames

As a reminder of previous reports on this bizarre incident, Kikić recounted that on returning from the beach he found the apartment in flames and was particularly shocked by the behaviour of the guests whom the police link to the outbreak of the fire. “They continued with their meal, toasting, raising glasses and bottles. They even got in our way while we were frantically buying hoses so we could try to put out the fire,” he said. He stated that this year’s tourist season is over for him and that he does not know whether he will manage to renovate the apartment even by next year. “For at least the next two years, I’m financially ruined,” he said.

The owner also described the sheer scale of the damage done by the fire inside the apartment. “The entire kitchen was handmade, from the highest-quality materials. All the furniture was high-quality, luxurious, paid for a lot of money. All of this is destroyed. This is a real catastrophe,” he said, adding that the apartment had been completely furnished and renovated. “An absolutely astronomical amount of money was invested in this. Everything was made of expensive materials, there were designer paintings inside with signatures,” he said.

the police say the fire started in the kitchen

The police investigation established that the fire broke out in the kitchen while a 44-year-old German citizen was preparing food.

“Due to the transfer of heat from the stove to the pan and then to the wooden structure, the fire spread to the rest of the apartment,” the police stated. Police suspect the 44-year-old woman of the criminal offence of endangering life and property by a generally dangerous act. The competent state attorney’s office will decide on further steps. The German family has in the meantime left Poreč, while the owner has been left to deal with the consequences of the fire.

Lawyer Zvonimir Matić earlier explained that the owner must first make a proper assessment of the damage, after which he can demand compensation from the German citizen in question. “The most important thing for them now is to make a quality assessment of the damage. After that they will submit a claim to the German citizen to compensate for the damage. If she does not do so, the owner will be able to file a lawsuit with the competent court in Poreč. It is important that the law is on their side,” Matić said.

“booking.com demanded that i pay for their alternative accommodation!”

Kikić had also hoped for help from the platform through which the apartment was booked, but claims Booking.com’s response further surprised him. “An hour later I received an email from the platform informing me that they had moved the guests to other accommodation, even to the most luxurious hotel, and that I had to pay for their accommodation,” he alleged. Booking.com earlier stated that they were checking the circumstances of the case and that the guest had been placed on the blocked users list while the check is ongoing.

Kikić claims that problems with the guests began the day after their arrival, when they started bringing additional people into the apartment. “When I tried to warn him, he simply arrogantly got in my face and said that he had booked the apartment and that they could do whatever they wanted in it,” he recounted. The owner estimates the damage to stand at around €400,000 in total.

World.title: Župa Dubrovačka – An Oasis Between Dubrovnik and Konavle
World.content:
August the 23rd, 2026 – Župa dubrovačka, or the Parish of Dubrovnik, is an area located between Dubrovnik and Konavle, known for its beaches, peace and distinctly less hustle and bustle.

In the extreme south of Dalmatia lies an area that is often overshadowed by its famous, world-renowned neighbour. Yet no matter how powerful the shadow of Dubrovnik may be, this region stubbornly continues to tell its own (much more relaxed) story. Putni kofer writes that that story is made up of a series of “chapters” written by the local, very old villages.

ONE OF THE MOST BEAUTIFUL PARTS OF THE DUBROVNIK RIVIERA

First, let’s get better acquainted with a few basic facts. Župa dubrovačka is located between Dubrovnik and Konavle, with the border towards the latter marked by Duboka Ljuta – a place where, according to legend, fairies used to sing noisily at night to scare away newcomers and keep all the beauty just for themselves. It spans an area of around 2,300 hectares and has about six thousand inhabitants. It’s separated from the very centre of Dubrovnik by just six kilometres and sits in a firm embrace of rolling hills on one side and the sea on the other. Župa dubrovačka is called one of the most beautiful parts of the Dubrovnik Riviera.

Its history is long and dates back to around 6000–4000 BC. One of the pieces of evidence from that time – a stone tongue-shaped chisel – is still kept in the Dubrovnik Museum. Illyrians once lived here, Greeks passed through the area, and later the Romans eventually ruled it. In the 7th century, however, Župa dubrovačka came under Dubrovnik’s control. Its natural beauty had long caught the eye of the Dubrovnik nobility, who built their summer residences there.

KUPARI – THE OLDEST TOURIST RESORT

Over time, Župa dubrovačka also grew in tourism terms, attracting visitors slowly but surely. Tourism began to develop there after the First World War and experienced a boom in the 1960s and 1970s, when a series of hotels were built in the area.

In this “tourism” sense, Kupari must be mentioned. This place is cited as the oldest tourist resort in Župa dubrovačka, and the first hotel was built there in 1920. The place got its name from the Kuparica tile factory, which operated as early as the 13th century. It is also known for one of the most famous beaches near Dubrovnik, as well as for a hotel complex that stood abandoned for a long time and has now been demolished. A new hotel is supposed to rise in its place. The only thing in the complex that was not demolished is the first hotel in the history of Župa – Hotel Grand – which is protected. It is due to be restored.

SREBRENO aND MLINI

East of Kupari lies Srebreno. This ancient fishing village, which was popular among Dubrovnik nobles who built villas there, is mentioned as early as the 13th century and is today the administrative centre of the municipality. It is also considered one of the best-known bathing spots in the area, along with Soline. That settlement got its name from the salt pans. One of the most recognisable places in Župa dubrovačka, however, is pretty little Mlini. The name was not given without reason. There used to be a series of mills in the village (mlin in Croatian), of which only one has been preserved to this day. Mlini is now widely regarded as one of the best-known tourist destinations in this compact area. It’s often referred to as one of the most beautiful settlements in Župa dubrovačka.

PLAT IS KNOWN FOR ITS BEAUTIFUL COVES

Bracodbk

Plat, another place in Župa dubrovačka, lies further south, towards Konavle. It is known for its beautiful coves and beaches, and its name Plat (formerly called Belenum) is first mentioned in 1400. It is home to several interesting little churches, for example the Church of St John, which stands on the hill above the village and where so-called mammoth spruces once grew. The thickest of them had a trunk circumference of more than two metres.

The Church of Our Lady of the Assumption was guarded by huge cypresses about 21 metres tall. The giant cypresses and spruces are gone, but near the latter church there are stećci (medieval tombstones), including one that is said to be the most beautiful in the Dubrovnik area. Finally, it is certainly worth stepping a little away from the coast itself and exploring the hinterland of Župa in general, the old villages, vineyards and olive groves, and the ancient stone houses.

World.title: Split Port: Passengers Wait in 40 Degree Heat With No Shelter From Sun
World.content:
August the 23rd, 2026 – Split Port is rapidly turning into a proverbial pizza oven as passengers have to wait in 40 degree heat with no shelter from the sun whatsoever.

At Split Port, passengers must wait to board in temperatures above 35 degrees in the shade, while on the scorching asphalt and with high humidity the perceived heat regularly exceeds 40 degrees. Lukrecija Zderic reports for Index that all of this takes place without a canopy under which people could take any form of shelter. With all the belongings they’re carrying on their journey, they must stand on the burning asphalt, exposed to the insufferable strength of the summer sun, with almost no shade available.

Parents with children, the elderly, and those waiting for the ferry try to find at least a scrap of shade under the smaller palm trees. Ferries come and go, the queues move, and passengers wait in the sun with no place to hide from the heat.

The problem becomes even greater when the catamaran or ferry is delayed and passengers don’t know exactly when it will arrive. This is precisely what happened to one of our readers, who wished to remain anonymous. With her family she had to wait in the port, in the sun and without adequate shelter, and she told Index how disappointing the whole situation was.

“It was a working day and we were supposed to travel by catamaran to Korčula. Unfortunately it was late, but that wasn’t the only problem. The biggest problem is that in Split’s port you almost have nowhere to shelter from the sun. The berths for the catamarans are far from the main, and practically the only, canopy in the port,” our interlocutor said.

“There’s often no space in the cafe or bar, and if you don’t know exactly when the catamaran will arrive or which berth it will dock at, which happens frequently, you can’t even move away to look for a shady spot. It was a heatwave, it was extremely hot, and with children it was a truly terrible experience,” the reader told us.

“if i hadn’t found shade, i’d have become unwell in the sun”

So we went to Split’s port to check whether the catamarans were late and how passengers spend their time waiting for them in the sun. Because the fact is that at the berths there is nowhere to shelter from the heat. During our arrival and the following three hours in the port, a large number of catamarans arrived and departed, and almost all of them arrived on time. The biggest delay we recorded was around ten minutes, which can hardly be called a serious delay, and it did not bother the passengers either. But what many would apparently gladly change is a simple thing – that instead of waiting on the scorching sun, they could wait for the ferry in the shade.

“It’s extremely hot, but it doesn’t bother me that much because I’m by the sea. It’s a bit inconvenient standing in the sun waiting for the ferry to Dubrovnik, so I try to find any little scrap of shade. This is more of a shadow, but it will do,” a tourist travelling to Dubrovnik told us.

“I saw that today it’s 35 degrees, and it’s the same in London, but I have to admit it’s much nicer here. Maybe because we’re on holiday, but if I hadn’t found a little shade, I would have gone crazy in the sun,” a tourist from England told us. Catamarans in Split’s City Port don’t all dock in one place; they use different berths along the operational quay. Some of them are located outside the main building of the maritime-passenger terminal. At the same time, works are underway in Split’s port on Sv. Duje Pier, where a new international maritime-passenger terminal is being built.

infrastructure upgrades – but nothing to deal with the issue of ensuring shade

Once completed, the project should take over part of the international traffic and free up Sv Duje Pier for domestic scheduled traffic, i.e. better connections between Split and the islands. But while the port infrastructure is being changed and expanded, the question remains whether the problem of protecting passengers who wait for catamarans in the open will also be solved, especially during the summer months and heatwaves.

While waiting for their catamaran, passengers try in various, and some quite inventive, ways to protect themselves from the sun. Umbrellas, caps and hats become the main defence against the scorching rays, while some hide in long sleeves and others seek refuge in the rare scraps of shade. The benches under the palm trees thus become sought-after spots, and passengers settle into every available bit of shade, however small.

“It’s very hot, we’re not used to this. We’ve put on long sleeves and are protecting ourselves with an umbrella. We hope our catamaran to Dubrovnik will arrive soon because it’s really hard to breathe here,” Japanese passengers told us. There were, however, also those who did not allow the heat to spoil their holiday mood.

“We’re from Germany and we’re only briefly in Split, and now we’re going to Hvar. We don’t have any special way of protecting ourselves from the sun; we simply try to find a little shade, although that’s not exactly easy here. We don’t want to complain – we’ve come on holiday, we’re by the sea and we’re going to one of the most beautiful islands. We won’t let a few minutes in the sun spoil our mood,” a married couple from Germany told us.

During the summer, Split Port is one of the busiest places in the city every day, yet there’s no respite from the intense heat. Back in 2024 alone, more than five million passengers passed through it on ferries and catamarans, of which more than a million on catamarans. This is a huge number of people who pass through the port every day during the season, and some of them wait for their catamarans precisely in the open, exposed to the sun and temperatures that during heatwaves exceed 35 degrees.

World.title: Iraq suggests a security council involving Iran, Saudi Arabia
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has officially suggested forming a joint security coordination council with Iran and Saudi Arabia to address what it calls a severe crisis of trust between the two regional powers.

The Security Affairs Adviser to the Prime Minister of Iraq, Qasim al-Araji, put forward the diplomatic initiative on behalf of Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s government to stabilize the region where Iraq strives to manage its own turbulent security climate.

Baghdad clearly planned the initiative to reconcile serious tensions between Riyadh and Tehran.

Tensions rose as Saudi Arabia intercepted multiple drones aimed at its oil facilities and capital. Riyadh denounced Iran-backed militias that operate from inside Iraq.

The idea comes during a very unstable period, including recent US-Saudi joint airstrikes targeting Popular Mobilization Forces’ (PMF) sites in Iraq and leading to serious criticism from Baghdad for sovereignty violations.

Baghdad is also pressuring Tehran for waivers for oil tankers from Iran’s navigation restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz.

Additionally, al-Araji underlined Iraq’s transition to ultimate domestic sovereignty.

With the scheduled withdrawal of the US-led international coalition forces from Iraq, Baghdad is adopting a strategy to put all armed factions and weaponry under strict state supervision, consolidating the country’s ultimate authority over war and peace choices.

Neither Saudi Arabia nor Iran has released a formal public response to the Iraqi initiative.

World.title: Iraq foreign reserves decline 11.6% to $86.17B in June 2026
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Official financial statements from the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) show that Iraq’s foreign exchange reserves declined to $86.175 billion at the end of June 2026, marking a decrease of $11.257 billion (-11.6%) compared to the $97.432 billion recorded at the close of 2025.

According to reserve records published on Monday, August 24, 2026, the contraction followed an early-year peak above $102 billion before downward momentum set in through the second quarter.

Monthly Reserve Trajectory (H1 2026)

End of 2025 Baseline: $97.432 billion

January 2026: $101.082 billion

February 2026 (Peak): $102.131 billion

March 2026: $100.341 billion

April 2026: $97.809 billion

May 2026: $93.673 billion

June 2026:$86.175 billion(Month-over-month drop of $7.498 billion)

The overall drop reduced the local currency value of the total portfolio from 126.661 trillion IQD at the end of 2025 to 112.027 trillion IQD by June 30, 2026—a net decline of 14.634 trillion IQD (-11.6%).

Reserve Component End of 2025 (IQD) End of June 2026 (IQD) Net Change Change (%) Investments & Securities 93.266 Trillion 81.998 Trillion -11.268 Trillion -12.1% Monetary Gold Reserves 31.488 Trillion 29.415 Trillion -2.073 Trillion -6.6% Cash Vault Holdings 1.907 Trillion 0.614 Trillion -1.293 Trillion -67.8% Total Equivalent Value 126.661 Trillion 112.027 Trillion -14.634 Trillion -11.6%

The reserve reduction aligns with broader fiscal pressures in the first half of 2026, during which lower oil revenues widened the state budget deficit and prompted the central bank to meet elevated domestic foreign currency demand.

While liquid investment instruments fell by 11.268 trillion IQD to absorb trade financing and foreign wire settlements, cash assets held in central bank vaults rebounded moderately in June (up to 614 billion IQD from 366 billion IQD in May), even as overall foreign exchange reserves adjusted downward to $86.175 billion.

World.title: National Security Adviser Al Aboudi meets U.S. Envoy on arms control
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi National Security Adviser Qasim Al-Aboudi met on Monday, August 24, 2026, with the Chargé d’Affaires of the U.S. Embassy in Baghdad, Joshua Harris, to discuss bilateral security cooperation, regional de-escalation, and Baghdad’s ongoing measures to restrict weapons exclusively to state control.

According to an official statement issued by the National Security Advisory, Al-Aboudi reaffirmed that the Iraqi government remains committed to maintaining national stability, mitigating broader regional tensions, and regulating the state monopoly over arms.

Key Discussion Pillars & Security Priorities

State Monopoly Over Arms: Al-Aboudi emphasized the government’s systematic implementation of regulatory frameworks designed to consolidate all weapons under official state security command.

Institutional Governance & Sovereign Decision-Making: Underlined Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi’s administrative vision focused on strengthening national defense and security institutions to support independent sovereign policymaking and economic recovery.

Counter-Terrorism & Intelligence Sharing: Reviewed shared security mechanisms between Baghdad and Washington, focusing on counter-terror operations, joint training, and strategic intelligence exchange.

Regional De-escalation: Discussed ongoing diplomatic and security initiatives to defuse regional friction and reinforce stability across the Middle East.

U.S. Diplomatic Backing: Harris affirmed Washington’s support for the Iraqi government’s security roadmap, institutional sovereignty, and regional stabilization initiatives.

The meeting between Al-Aboudi and Harris underscores consistent coordination between Baghdad and Washington on key security priorities, coming shortly after high-level diplomatic discussions on the U.S.–Iraq Strategic Framework Agreement.

By synchronizing counter-terrorism efforts with domestic initiatives to restrict unregulated weapons, Iraqi authorities aim to reinforce sovereign command structures, improve internal stability, and foster a secure environment for long-term economic investment.

World.title: Samarra Drug Company starts first domestic Moxifloxacin Antibiotic output
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The State Company for Drug Industries and Medical Appliances in Samarra (SDI), an affiliate of the Iraqi Ministry of Industry and Minerals, announced on Monday, August 24, 2026, the successful domestic production of Moxifloxacin, a broad-spectrum fluoroquinolone antibiotic targeting five distinct bacterial infections, marking its first addition to the company’s manufacturing portfolio.

In an official statement received by IraqiNews.com, SDI Director General, Chemist Mohammed Abdul Qader Al-Nuaimi, confirmed that the formulation marks a key step in expanding state pharmaceutical production lines and bolstering domestic medical security.

Clinical Scope & Key Indications

Moxifloxacin is a fourth-generation synthetic fluoroquinolone antibiotic designed to treat severe and complex bacterial infections in adult patients, including:

Community-Acquired Pneumonia: Lower respiratory tract bacterial infections.

Acute Exacerbations of Chronic Bronchitis: Bacterial flair-ups affecting chronic obstructive airway passages.

Acute Bacterial Sinusitis: Severe sinus and nasal inflammation.

Skin and Soft Tissue Infections: Complicated and uncomplicated bacterial dermatological and subcutaneous infections.

Other Complex Bacterial Invasions: Broad-spectrum systemic coverage against susceptible Gram-positive and Gram-negative pathogens.

Strategic Importance for National Drug Security

Import Substitution: Domestic manufacturing directly reduces the Ministry of Health’s reliance on foreign imported antibiotics, conserving foreign exchange reserves.

National Pharmaceutical Localization: Aligns with Iraq’s industrial localization roadmap aimed at strengthening the domestic supply chain for critical medications.

Supply Chain Reliability: Ensures stable, high-quality, and cost-effective medical supplies for state healthcare facilities and the local private retail market.

The launch of Moxifloxacin comes as part of the Samarra facility’s broader modernization drive to introduce advanced active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and expand local formulation capacities.

By localizing the manufacture of advanced broad-spectrum antibiotics, SDI continues to scale production lines to meet the clinical procurement requirements of Iraqi hospitals and healthcare centers.

World.title: Iraq to launch portal for 1M residential plots project in September
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The Iraqi government will officially launch the dedicated digital registration platform for its flagship “One Million Residential Plots” initiative on September 1, 2026, targeting citizens who have never previously benefited from state land allocations, government spokesperson Haider Al-Aboudi announced on Monday, August 24, 2026.

Al-Aboudi confirmed that the first batch of serviced land parcels—exceeding 250,000 plots developed in coordination with the private sector—is fully prepared across various governorates. The government is also evaluating structured bank lending programs to assist eligible citizens with residential construction financing.

Key Program Milestones & Eligibility Framework

Digital Application Launch: The official online registration platform will open on September 1, 2026, featuring integrated identity verification and automated auditing to cross-check eligibility.

Strict Eligibility Criteria: The initiative is restricted exclusively to Iraqi citizens who have not received prior land grants, housing allocations, or state residential real estate.

First Batch Scale: More than 250,000 fully serviced residential plots (equipped with water, electricity, sewage, and road networks) have been prepared nationwide under public-private development partnerships.

Construction Loan Mechanisms: The federal government, in coordination with state and private commercial banks, is assessing low-interest housing loan packages to support plot recipients in constructing single-family housing units.

The digital launch follows executive directives issued on August 9, 2026, by Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi, instructing ministries and provincial municipal directorates to initiate executive procedures in governorates where land zoning and site demarcation have been completed.

Municipalities have accelerated land surveying and partitioning over recent weeks. On August 18, the Karbala Municipality Directorate finalized all technical sorting and zoning requirements for its local allocation quota, preparing parcels for distribution as part of the broader national strategy to alleviate urban housing shortages and curb informal settlements.

World.title: Iraq tests return of Basrah crude sales through Strait of Hormuz
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq is resuming efforts to transfer more oil straight from its southern export ports, with state marketer SOMO seeking customers for September shipments as restricted tanker access via the Strait of Hormuz reopens.

The offering includes Basrah Medium and Basrah Heavy, with purchasers likely to pick up the petroleum from Iraq’s Gulf export facilities rather than using alternate transfer arrangements devised during the recent shipping interruption.

The decision follows a significant breakthrough over the weekend, when Iran granted transit through Hormuz for several tankers carrying Iraqi oil in response to persistent diplomatic pleas from Baghdad.

For Iraq, even a partial reopening is crucial.

The majority of the country’s petroleum typically departs via its southern Gulf ports, rendering the economy especially susceptible when tanker traffic through Hormuz is halted.

Baghdad has spent recent weeks looking for methods to keep exports and government revenues coming. International merchants have utilized smaller boats and ship-to-ship swaps to transport some Iraqi barrels beyond the Gulf, while the government has stepped up attempts to enhance export capacity via Turkey and explore future routes via Syria and Jordan.

SOMO’s recent offering may give an early indicator of whether oil merchants are willing to return to loading straight from Basrah, despite ongoing security and transportation hazards.

QatarEnergy is also testing the market with oil available for collection within Hormuz, indicating that regional producers are progressively investigating whether traditional Gulf shipments may restart.

However, tanker movements remain far lower than usual, indicating that Iraq cannot count on Hormuz recovering to its pre-conflict role.

This uncertainty has fueled Baghdad’s desire to diversify its oil infrastructure. Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi’s administration seeks to increase exports via Turkey’s Ceyhan port and create new routes to the Mediterranean and Red Sea.

For now, the top objective is to send as many Iraqi barrels to foreign consumers as securely as possible while also restoring the oil revenue on which the government budget is largely dependent.

The SOMO tender is therefore more than just a crude sale. It is an early test of whether Iraq’s key southern oil-export infrastructure can resume regular operations after the Hormuz crisis, which revealed one of the country’s most serious economic weaknesses.

World.title: Oman’s SalamAir adds Erbil as second destination in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — SalamAir, Oman’s low-cost airline, will commence direct flights between Muscat and Erbil on October 25, 2026, strengthening its footprint in Iraq after its debut into the Baghdad market.

The airline has launched ticket sales for the new flight, which will run twice a week between the Omani capital and Erbil.

One-way Lite fares will start at approximately $143 (187,000 Iraqi dinars).

SalamAir adds Erbil as its second Iraqi destination, capitalizing on the success of its current Muscat-Baghdad route.

The new link is designed to facilitate business, tourist, commerce, and family travel between Oman and Iraq, as well as provide travelers from Erbil with additional connections via Muscat to destinations in India and other regions of Asia.

SalamAir Chief Commercial Officer Steven Allen characterized Iraq as an important market for the airline, with Erbil providing an additional potential to meet expanding regional demand and improve Muscat’s position as a connecting hub.

The extension also offers another international link to Erbil International Airport, and it comes as Iraq welcomes more regional airline services as business and tourism flourish.

World.title: Ukraine backers gather as war escalates, air defence runs low
World.content:
Kyiv – Ukraine hosts a meeting of its key European backers on Monday to press for critical air-defence supplies and more pressure on Moscow, with Russian attacks killing more civilians than at any time since the first months of the invasion.

The meeting of the Coalition of the Willing will be jointly chaired by the leaders of Britain, France and Germany.

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham will be in Kyiv for his first international trip since taking office, and several other leaders are expected to join remotely.

EU Council President Antonio Costa is also due in Kyiv for the talks, which come amid the latest, deadly escalation of the war.

Russia has been pounding Kyiv with ballistic missiles in recent weeks, ripping open apartment blocks and killing dozens of citizens in the capital.

The escalating Russian strikes have pushed civilian deaths to their highest levels since the first months of Russia’s 2022 invasion.

After almost every attack — which sees tens of thousands hunker in the Kyiv metro system and many more in basements and other shelters across the city — Zelensky has issued public pleas for more air-defence support.

Ahead of the meeting, Ukraine has forged ahead with its campaign against Russia’s logistics sites, hitting multiple warehouses belonging to e-commerce giant Ozon.

Ozon reported fires early Monday at its warehouses in Krasnodar and Makhachkala, both in southern Russia, adding that sites in Adygeysk and Nevinnomyssk were evacuated due to threats of drone attack.

Russian authorities also said debris from a Ukrainian drone attack killed two children and wounded nine others.

– UK, French support –

Ukraine celebrates independence day on Monday, which also marks exactly four-and-a-half years since Russia invaded on February 24, 2022.

“Russia should be in no doubt of our resolve,” Burnham said in a statement before his arrival in Kyiv.

“We will not back down until there is a just and lasting peace.”

Diplomacy on ending the conflict — Europe’s largest since World War II — is effectively frozen.

Russia is demanding hardline territorial and political concessions that Kyiv has rejected as a capitulation that would only enable another Russian attack.

Burnham is set to announce that the British government is authorising defence firm MBDA to release classified information needed to help Ukraine and France set up local production of the long-range SCALP missile.

And on Saturday, French President Emmanuel Macron pledged Paris would deliver new interceptor missiles.

“It is crucial to provide Ukraine with all the necessary means to defend its skies and thwart this aggression,” Macron wrote on X.

The ballistic missiles Russia has been firing in their dozens are incredibly fast and travel with a high-arching trajectory, making them difficult to stop.

Kyiv’s homegrown weapons cannot shoot them down, meaning Ukraine is reliant on advanced systems — chiefly, US Patriot interceptors — to protect its skies.

But due to shortfalls globally since the US launched its war on Iran, Ukraine has been left exposed.

– Ukraine’s missiles shortfall –

Ahead of the meeting, Zelensky revealed the extent of the deficit, releasing usually closely guarded numbers.

He said deliveries of crucial Patriot interceptors had halved since 2023.

“Over the entire of 2023, Ukraine received 675 missiles, and over all of 2025 — 364, even though Russian missile strikes have increased,” Zelensky said.

“For 2026, as currently projected, it is 264,” he added, saying Ukraine was seeking a package of at least 300 for the upcoming winter.

The United States faces its own shortfall of the missiles during its war on Iran and has resisted releasing large numbers to Ukraine.

Zelensky said Russia could produce around 100 ballistic missiles a month.

Ukraine, meanwhile, has accelerated its own campaign of long-range strikes on Russian energy and logistics sites — including oil refineries and retail warehouses.

The Coalition of the Willing is a Franco-British initiative to deliver support to Ukraine and ramp up pressure on Russia.

Originally designed as a group of countries that would be willing to deploy peacekeeping troops to Ukraine in the event a ceasefire was reached, it has become a parallel forum for marshalling support to Ukraine as uncertainty persists over US commitments under Donald Trump.

World.title: Centre asks states, union territories to expand piped gas network
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Trying to accelerate the adoption of piped gas for cooking and industrial purposes, the Centre has asked states and Union Territories to provide district-level administrative support and appoint nodal officers to coordinate with gas distributors and oil marketing companies to expand the network.

Govt has also directed authorised city gas distribution companies and public sector oil marketing companies to establish PNG coordination committees to identify eligible housing societies and households and conduct outreach camps to accelerate piped gas connections.

In a letter to state chief secretaries, petroleum secretary Neeraj Mittal said PNG was crucial for Indiaâs energy transition and could help reduce dependence on cooking gas cylinders.

âPNG brings a safer, cleaner and more efficient cooking fuel, playing a critical role in advancing the countryâs energy transition objectives. Its accelerated adoption contributes to reducing the logistics burden associated with LPG distribution, enhancing consumer convenience, and improving utilisation of CGD infrastructure created through substantial public and private investment,â Mittal said in the letter.





While the potential for PNG is huge, its adoption so far has not matched the govtâs expectations. During the West Asia conflict, when energy supplies were disrupted and an LPG shortage loomed large, govt made concerted efforts to push PNG adoption by seeking the help of states and UTs and easing the regulatory framework for faster laying of pipeline networks. Govt is also trying to prevent households from retaining both LPG and PNG connections in areas where piped gas is available.

World.title: Digital financial inclusion key to boosting women's participation in India’s platform economy: ILO-NCAER
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Despite the flexibility offered by platform work, womenâs participation in Indiaâs growing platform economy remains constrained by limited access to formal financial services, gaps in digital literacy, safety concerns and restrictive social norms, an ILO-NCAER policy brief said on Monday.

The brief, âAdvancing Womenâs Digital Financial Inclusion in the Platform Economyâ, said women need access to a range of financial services throughout their platform-work journey, including start-up capital, short-term credit, insurance, savings and financial planning tools.

It highlighted cashflow-based lending as a key lever for inclusion, particularly because women are less likely to own land or property that can be used as collateral.

Digital records of platform payments can provide lenders with verifiable evidence of income and repayment capacity.

Addressing a Roundtable at the release of the Policy Brief, NCAER director general Suresh Goyal said, âA womanâs best protection is a little money of her own and access to credit and mobility are important conditions for women to have better employment opportunities. Platform economy has given that opportunity.â





The brief identified two ways to leverage womenâs digital footprints: using Indiaâs Digital Public Infrastructure, including the Account Aggregator framework, to make financial data portable, and enabling platforms to partner with lenders to offer loans, savings and insurance through their apps.

ILO country director Michiko Miyamoto said, âDigital financial inclusion must enable women to build income security, resilience, and sustainable livelihoods."

ILO Senior Specialist Radhicka Kapoor said integrating financial DPI with e-Shram records could further expand access, provided safeguards against algorithmic bias are built in.

The brief also flagged device ownership as a barrier, noting that womenâs digital access is often mediated through family members.

World.content:

Here are the top five stories of the day

Centre clarifies Indiaâs position on media access during Modi-Trump bilateral

The government said discussions regarding arrangements for leadersâ public appearances are a ânormal practiceâ, after US Ambassador Sergio Gor said India had specifically requested that reporters not be allowed to ask questions after PM Modi-Trump bilateral in June.

Gor said Trump initially agreed to the request but later opened the floor to reporters, turning the interaction into a 45-minute press conference. The meeting also covered the safety of Indian seafarers and bilateral trade negotiations.

Heavy rain lashed Delhi-NCR, causing widespread waterlogging, traffic snarls and flight disruptions, with 15 Delhi-bound flights diverted, including two international flights.

The IMD issued red and orange alerts for heavy to moderate rainfall, thunderstorms and winds of up to 40 kmph. Waterlogging was reported across several parts of Delhi, Gurugram and Noida, while Air India and IndiGo advised passengers to check their flight status before leaving for the airport.

Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay announced three free cooking gas cylinders a year for eligible beneficiaries, with the amount to be credited directly to their bank accounts.

World.title: 'Govt has played delay games': CJP announces march from India Gate to Delhi Police HQ on Sept 5
World.content:
Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke Photo credit: Reuters

NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has announced a youth march on September 5 in Delhi, accusing the government of failing to honour commitments that led to the withdrawal of the studentsâ protest at Jantar Mantar on July 25. The CJP said the government had failed to act on its assurance to withdraw FIRs against students and protesting students.The march will begin at India Gate and proceed towards the New Delhi Police Headquarters, according to a statement issued by the CJP National Working Committee, posted on X. The organisation said the protest would be led by families of deceased NEET victims and victims of alleged police brutality, with students and youth organisations expected to join.In the post, the CJP said, âThe Cockroach Janta Party strongly condemns the Union Governmentâs failure to honour the commitments made to Indiaâs youth on July 25, particularly those concerning the withdrawal of FIRs against students and protesters.ââWith the Government continuing to delay and avoid fulfilling its assurances, the CJP National Working Committee has decided to resume peaceful mobilisation,â it said.The CJP said the decision followed a review of the commitments it alleges were made by the government on July 25, after which nationwide youth protests were withdrawn.The statement said the committee had expressed âserious doubts over whether the Government intends to honour its word at allâ, alleging that the government had delayed action and avoided providing clear commitments.It also referred to proceedings before the Supreme Court, saying that on August 18, the court had sought a list of FIRs registered across the country so that it could consider dealing with them together. The CJP alleged that the government had not given a clear commitment on the issue.The organisation also added, âThis cannot continue. Our patience cannot be mistaken for weakness. Our good faith cannot become an opportunity for the Government to betray us.âAnnouncing the September 5 mobilisation, the CJP said, âWe announce a peaceful protest march from India Gate to the new Delhi Police Headquarters on 5 September, led by the families of the deceased NEET victims and victims of police brutality, and joined by students and young citizens from across the country.âThe group said it had returned to the streets because the government âappears determined to commit a âvishwasghaatâ with Gen-Z, the young generation of this country, and the families who have already lost their children.âIt further said, âWe withdrew a nationwide movement in good faith. A government cannot take the trust of an entire generation, use it to send them home, and then quietly retreat from its own word. We will not accept this attempted betrayal.âThe CJP has urged students, youth organisations and young citizens to gather at India Gate on September 5. âThe families who lost their children will walk at the front. Victims of police brutality will walk with them,â the statement said.The CJP, which describes itself as a youth-focused movement, has also raised issues including unemployment and examination irregularities.

World.title: 'Citizens have right to know': CJP demands states come clean on funding, facilities in govt schools
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Abhijeet Dipke, founder and convenor of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), has demanded transparency on government school funding, infrastructure and staffing. Addressing an open letter to the education ministers across states, he said citizens have a right to know what steps are being taken to improve public education.

He posed six questions to the ministers regarding the condition and facilities inside the government schools. He also asked them to publicly disclose details on infrastructure, teacher vacancies, funding, digital facilities and the workload of teaching staff.

Dipke posted a letter on his X account with the caption, "Letter to the Education Ministers of all states. The country needs to know what steps are being taken to improve government schools."

He asked the ministry to disclose spending on government schools and the number of additional schools required to provide children with reasonable access to quality education.

The six questions raised by Dipke are:

School renovations: How many government schools in the state have been renovated in the last five years, and how many currently require repairs or complete renovation? Teacher vacancies: How many teaching positions are currently sanctioned, how many are filled, and how many remain vacant? School funding: How much money has been allocated for government schools in the last five years, and how much of it has actually been spent? Need for more schools: How many additional government schools are required to ensure that every child has reasonable access to quality education? Non-teaching duties: Apart from teaching, what non-teaching duties and responsibilities are assigned to government school teachers? Basic and digital facilities: How many government schools currently have adequate access to computers and digital learning facilities, clean and functional toilets, and proper sports facilities and equipment for children?

Dipke's questions came against the backdrop of concerns over basic facilities in government schools. In his letter, he said children in many government schools still lack access to safe drinking water, functional washrooms and proper classrooms, while some reportedly do not even have basic benches to sit on.





"The visuals emerging from government schools and circulating on social media should make all of us deeply concerned. No child in this country should be forced to study in such conditions. They are being treated worse than animals," he said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

He argued that improving public education should be treated as an urgent priority and called for schools to be improved "on a war footing". At the same time, he said the public should first be given a clear picture of the existing situation.

Dipke stressed that his questions were not aimed at any particular political party or government.

"This is not about politics or any one government. This is about the future of our children," he said, adding that every child deserves "a safe classroom, clean drinking water, a functional washroom, a bench to sit on, and a teacher to teach them."

He urged the ministry to make the requested information public and take urgent measures to ensure that inadequate infrastructure does not deny children access to dignified education.

World.title: 'Monstrous, mindless': Chidambaram criticises 'One Nation, One Election' plan at House panel meet
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Former union minister

has opposed the proposed âOne Nation, One Electionâ framework before a joint parliamentary committee, calling the initiative âunconstitutionalâ, âmonstrousâ and âmindlessâ.

Chidambaram, who appeared before the panel examining the Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024, and the Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024, argued that synchronising Lok Sabha and state assembly elections could violate the constitutional framework governing elected legislatures.

Sources, quoted by news agency PTI, said the former home and finance minister told the panel that since legislatures are elected for five-year terms, curtailing their tenure would amount to a violation of the basic structure of the Constitution.

Chidambaram also said his conscience did not allow him to support the proposed legislation and argued that the government does not have the required two-thirds majority to pass the bills, sources told PTI.

The Congress leader described the proposal to hold nationwide elections simultaneously as a âmindlessâ exercise and strongly opposed the governmentâs push for simultaneous polls.

Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP Sagarika Ghosh, who is also a member of the committee, separately opposed the bills.





Ghosh said the proposal could give âunbridledâ power to the Election Commission, sources said.

The joint committee, headed by BJP MP PP Chaudhary, also heard representations from around 10 Padma awardees, including Tarlochan Singh, Navin Khanna, Meenakshi Jain and Niru Kumar. While some supported simultaneous elections, others opposed the proposal, warning that it could lead to âchaosâ in the country.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The two bills were introduced in the Lok Sabha in December 2024 and subsequently referred to the joint committee for detailed examination.

The proposal followed recommendations from a high-level committee headed by former president Ram Nath Kovind, which suggested holding Lok Sabha, state assembly and local body elections simultaneously in a phased manner. Union Home Minister Amit Shah was also a member of the panel.

India had earlier held Lok Sabha and state assembly elections together from 1951-52 through 1967. The cycle was disrupted after premature dissolutions of some state assemblies in 1968 and 1969, followed by the early dissolution of the Fourth Lok Sabha in 1970 and fresh general elections in 1971.

Since then, staggered election cycles have become the norm, with several Lok Sabha and state assembly terms ending before their full five-year tenure.

World.title: Why Vijay scrapped Chennai’s second airport plan at Parandur
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday announced that his government would abandon the proposed greenfield airport project at Parandur, saying the project would affect agricultural land and disrupt the livelihoods of farmers and residents.

The announcement was made in the assembly as Vijay said Chennai still needed a new airport to meet rising passenger demand, industrial growth and increasing cargo movement. However, he said the new airport should be located at a site where agricultural and residential areas would face minimal disruption.

"To fulfill the promise I made to the people that day... the steps taken to establish a new airport in Parandur will be abandoned by this government," Vijay said.

The government is now considering alternative locations and plans to conduct technical feasibility studies before finalising a new site.

Why Vijay rejected Parandur

Vijay said he had visited Eganapuram and other villages on January 20, 2025, and heard the grievances of residents protesting against the proposed airport in Parandur and 12 surrounding villages.

"I stand firmly with the people protesting against the airport to be established in Chennai's Parandur and 12 surrounding villages," he said.





The chief minister said farmers were the backbone of the country and backed those protesting to protect their agricultural land.

Vijay said he had also opposed the Parandur project at a public meeting in Vikravandi in October 2024, while making clear that he supported industrial development and the role of airports in it.

"However, this project should not be located in Parandur. The government must reconsider this project," he said.

He added that an alternative site should be identified where the impact on agricultural land and people's livelihoods would be minimal.

Chennai airport to be expanded

While dropping Parandur, the government said Chennai's existing airport would be expanded.

Vijay said the Meenambakkam airport, operated by the Airports Authority of India, currently has the capacity to handle around 30 million passengers annually. With the under-construction Terminal 3 becoming operational, capacity is expected to rise to 34 million passengers a year.

The government plans to expand the airport on its north-western side by constructing a fifth terminal, which is expected to handle another 20 million passengers annually.

The government is also considering alternative sites for a new airport, with technical feasibility studies to be conducted by expert teams.

Why Parandur was chosen

The Parandur project had received in-principle approval from the Civil Aviation Ministry in April 2025 for an International Greenfield Airport in Kancheepuram district.

The proposed project had faced opposition from residents of villages that were expected to be affected by land acquisition and construction.

However, the DMK has criticised the decision to abandon the project, arguing that it could hurt Tamil Nadu's industrial growth and investment prospects.

Former chief minister and DMK president MK Stalin said dropping the project would set the state's development back by several years.

"The announcement made today by the Hon'ble Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu to drop the Parandur International Airport project will set the state's development back by several years. Tamil Nadu's interests cannot be mortgaged for petty political considerations," Stalin said.

He also called the decision a setback to employment opportunities for Tamil Nadu's youth.

DMK warns of economic fallout

Former Tamil Nadu minister and DMK MLA Thangam Thennarasu also criticised the decision, saying the Parandur site was selected after studying options for establishing two runways.

"Possibilities for setting up two runways were all studied and only then Parandur was selected," he said.

Thennarasu argued that scrapping the project for political reasons could hurt the state's economy and push industries towards neighbouring Andhra Pradesh.

"It would be best to have the airport at Parandur. Dropping the Parandur Airport project for political reasons will cause economic damage," he said.

"Many industries will move towards Andhra Pradesh.

We have already lost the Hosur Airport," he added.

Thennarasu also said compensation had already been provided to people whose land was acquired for the project and cited the Land Acquisition Act while arguing that the acquired land should be used for its intended purpose.

DMK stages assembly walkout

The announcement triggered an immediate confrontation in the Tamil Nadu Assembly, with DMK MLAs staging a walkout after Speaker JCD Prabhakar denied DMK leader KN Nehru permission to respond to the statement, citing Assembly rules.

The opposition accused the government of making a policy U-turn that could affect Tamil Nadu's industrial momentum and prospects of attracting investment.

Vijay, however, maintained that the government supports airport-led industrial development but believes the proposed airport should not come at the cost of agricultural land and people's livelihoods.

A fresh threat letter was allegedly circulated on social media targeting Kashmiri Pandit employees serving in the Kashmir Valley, prompting the All PM Package Employees Forum Kashmir to seek enhanced security from the Jammu and Kashmir administration.In a letter to chief secretary of Jammu and Kashmir on Monday, the forum said the purported threat poster, allegedly issued by an outfit calling itself the United Liberation Council (ULC) and dated August 23, contains the names, addresses and vehicle numbers of some employees.The forum said the authenticity of the poster has not yet been verified by police or security agencies but warned that its repeated circulation was a matter of âgrave concernâ. World.title: Bengaluru: Man books 108 ambulance with fake murder call
World.content:
The Amruthahalli police have registered a case against an unidentified man for allegedly making a fake murder call to the 108 ambulance service and later abusing a staff nurse and ambulance driver over the phone.

The complaint was filed on Sunday (August 23, 2026) by Lakshmi Devi, who works as a staff nurse with the 108 emergency ambulance service. The case has been registered under Sections 212 and 352 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023.

According to the complaint, Ms. Devi was on night duty on August 19, travelling in the ambulance at around 10.22 p.m., when the 108 control room received a call from an unidentified person who allegedly claimed that a murder had taken place at B-Sector, Amruthanagar, Byatarayanapura, Bengaluru.

Acting on the information, Lakshmi Devi and ambulance driver Yogesh Kumar, along with police personnel from Hoysala-173, reached the location at around 11.08 p.m. However, they found no evidence of any murder or such incident at the spot.

The nurse subsequently obtained the caller’s details through the 108 control room and contacted the number to verify the information. During the conversation, the man allegedly abused Ms. Devi and Mr. Kumar, accusing them of not reaching the location he had provided and not performing their duties.

The complaint further states that the police informed them that the same person had allegedly made similar false calls on previous occasions, causing trouble to emergency services.

The nurse has requested the police to trace the person using the mobile number and take appropriate legal action.

World.title: ‘Where Is Rahul Gandhi?’: Telangana BJP over students’ fee reimbursement dues
World.content:
Telangana Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) president N. Ramchander Rao on Monday (August 24, 2026) challenged Congress senior leader Rahul Gandhi “who is travelling across the country and provoking students in BJP-ruled states”, to come to the State and give answers on the issue of fee reimbursement dues being withheld by the Congress government, if he has the courage.

Launching a 48-hour hunger strike at the BJP State office in Hyderabad in support of students demanding the immediate release of around ₹15,000 crore in fee reimbursement dues, the BJP leader accused the Congress Government of neglecting the education sector and jeopardising the future of nearly 40 lakh students in Telangana.

He criticised what he described as the “stubborn attitude and authoritarian approach” of Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy — who also holds the education portfolio — of having pushed the “education system into a severe crisis”. The non-release of fee reimbursement dues has caused widespread hardship for students studying in professional and higher educational institutions.

He further alleged that despite assurances given after criticism from the High Court, the government had failed to release even the promised ₹2,000 crore advance for the next academic year. Asserting that the BJP would continue its agitation until the issue is resolved, Mr. Rao said the party stood firmly with students across the State.

The BJP leader claimed that party workers had toured colleges across Telangana and collected signatures from nearly five lakh students who were unhappy with the Congress government’s failure to clear fee reimbursement arrears.

Mr. Rao also charged the police of lathi-charging polytechnic students — when they had raised their grievances, and the government of ignoring the ongoing agitation by Ayush and Homeopathy students seeking an increase in their stipends. Earlier, police denied permission to him to hold the protest at the designated ‘Dharna Chowk’ near Indira Park.

Several senior BJP leaders including MP Rekha Sharma, BJP Legislature Party leader Aleti Maheshwar Reddy, Legislative Council leader A.V.N. Reddy, MPs D. Arvind, Raghunandan Rao and D.K. Aruna, MLAs Palvai Harish and Venkata Ramana Reddy, and MLCs Malka Komuraiah and Anji Reddy, extended support to the protest and criticised the Congress government over the issue.

World.title: SFI district conference in Haveri today
World.content:
Students Federation of India will hold a district conference in Haveri on Tuesday. The theme will be universal and quality education, protection of democracy, harmony and comprehensive development of the district.

It will be organised at the Sabha Bhavan of the State Government Employees Association.

Member of Karnataka State Bar Council (KSBC) Basavaraj V. Korimath will inaugurate the conference.

The guests will include SFI State president Shivappa Ablikal, V.K. Gokak National Memorial Trust president and writer Satish Kulkarni, DYFI State secretary Basavaraj Pujar, Karnataka State Minorities Commission member Parimala Jain, lawyer Narayana Kale and SFI former district president Renuka Kahar and others.

SFI district president Basavaraj S. will preside over the event.

Arun Kumar Nagawat, Chaitra Koravar, Shobha Devaramane and others will address the gathering, said a release.

World.title: Direct paddy procurement centres opened in Erode
World.content:
The Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation (TNCSC) has opened direct paddy procurement centres in the Thadapalli-Arakkankottai irrigation areas here from Monday (August 24, 2026).

Collector S. Kandasamy said the centres have been opened to enable farmers to sell their produce directly to the government. Permission has been accorded to open 39 centres in the irrigation areas.

The centres are functioning at Kallipatti, Elur, Nanjai Puliyampatti, Puthuvalliyampalayam, Alukuli, Kasipalayam, N.G. Palayam, Karattadipalayam, T.N. Palayam, Kugalur, Pudukaraipudur, Karunkaradu, Perundalaiyur, Mevani, Nanjai Thuraiyampalayam, Kondayampalayam and Soundapur, among other locations. Based on the arrivals, the centres will function.

The procurement price has been fixed at ₹2,545 a quintal for Grade ‘A’ paddy, comprising a minimum support price of ₹2,389 and an incentive of ₹156. For common variety paddy, the price is ₹2,500 a quintal, comprising an MSP of ₹2,369 and an incentive of ₹131. Paddy will be procured through the e-Procurement system after biometric authentication of farmers. The amount will be credited directly to their bank accounts.

Farmers should produce a certificate from the Village Administrative Officer, patta, chitta, adangal, a copy of their Aadhaar card, a copy of their bank passbook and two passport-size photographs at the procurement centres, the Collector said.

World.title: Keralam CM Satheesan urges Modi to halt transfer of Mangaluru from Palakkad railway division
World.content:
Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan has urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to put on hold the Railway Board’s decision to transfer the Mangaluru area up to Ullal from the Palakkad railway division to the Mysuru division of South Western Railway from October 1.

In a letter to the Prime Minister, Mr. Satheesan said the decision, issued on August 21, was taken without consulting the Keralam government despite its implications for railway infrastructure and development in northern Keralam.

He said Mangaluru had been part of the Palakkad division for decades and the transfer would include Mangaluru Central, Mangaluru Junction and railway facilities serving the Mangaluru port, including Panambur, a major freight and container-handling centre.

Major revenue source

The Mangaluru area accounts for more than 90% of the Palakkad division’s freight revenue, estimated at ₹650 crore, and over half of its total revenue of about ₹1,650 crore, he said.

Removing the area would weaken the division’s financial base and affect resource allocation, infrastructure projects, train services and passenger amenities in Malabar, the Chief Minister said.

Mr. Satheesan pointed out that the Palakkad division had already lost the Coimbatore region when the Salem division was formed in 2007. The proposed transfer of Mangaluru will further reduce its jurisdiction and revenue base, he said.

Railway divisions, he said, were not merely administrative units as their boundaries affected connectivity, infrastructure investment, freight movement and passenger services.

Mr. Satheesan urged the Prime Minister to direct the Railway Ministry to reconsider the decision after consulting the Keralam government and other stakeholders. He also sought retention of the Palakkad division’s existing jurisdiction and greater investment and services for northern Keralam.

World.title: Telangana ACB traps state tax officer, senior assistant while taking ₹50,000 bribe in Nirmal
World.content:
The Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) on Monday arrested a state tax officer and a senior assistant in Nirmal district for demanding and accepting a bribe of ₹50,000 in connection with a GST audit.

The accused were Koppela Gadavari, state tax officer, Nirmal Circle, and Manthri Sai Krishna, senior assistant in the office of the Assistant Commissioner (State Tax), Nirmal.

According to the ACB, the officers initially demanded ₹1 lakh from a 65-year-old businessman from Mancherial for doing an official favour in connection with the audit of the records of Sri Laxmi Prasanna Jewelers for the financial years 2022-23 and 2023-24. Following repeated requests from the complainant, the demand was allegedly reduced to ₹80,000 and finally ₹50,000.

The ACB said the alleged favour involved issuing a favourable audit report that would facilitate the business showing a lower taxable turnover and GST liability, resulting in a corresponding loss of revenue to the Government.

During the trap laid by the Adilabad Range ACB officials on Monday, Gadavari received the ₹50,000 from the complainant and handed it over to Sai Krishna. The tainted cash was subsequently recovered.

The ACB said both officers had demanded and accepted illegal gratification by misusing their official positions to obtain undue advantage. The accused officers were arrested and are being produced before the Special Judge for SPE and ACB Cases concerned. The case is under investigation.

The ACB has withheld the complainant’s details for security reasons. The bureau appealed to the public to report demands for bribes by public servants on its toll-free number 1064.

World.title: BRS urges CM to withdraw decision to attach polytechnic colleges to Skill Varsity
World.content:
HYDERABAD

Senior leader of Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) and former MP B. Vinod Kumar requested Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy to review the issue arising out of the government decision to bring the polytechnic colleges under the Skill University through GO 97.

Speaking to newspersons here on Monday, he said the students of polytechnic colleges were protesting for the last 10 days demanding withdrawal/scrapping of GO 97 issued on August 16 with the objective to bring the technical education diploma colleges under the purview of Skill University.

The Act through which the Skill University was established had clearly stated that its role would be to issue degrees (certificates) and it had no recognition of the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE). Further, it was also stated that the univeristy would work in the private public partnership method and the students of polytechnics were strongly opposed to privatisation.

Stating that the system of polytechnic colleges was existing from prior to independence and it was strengthened further by the Jawaharlal Nehru government, he asked the government to establish separate engineering colleges for giving admission to the polytechnic students directly into engineering courses through an entrance test (ECET).

World.title: Chittoor Sugar Factory marriage hall reopens after renovation
World.content:
The renovated Kalyana Mandapam of the Chittoor Cooperative Sugar Factory at Doddipalle was inaugurated here on Monday, providing residents with an upgraded venue for weddings and other auspicious functions.

Chittoor MP D. Prasada Rao, MLA Gurajala Jagan Mohan, Joint Collector Adarsh Rajendran and Chittoor Urban Development Authority (CHUDA) Chairperson Kathari Hemalatha attended the programme.

Mr. Rajendran said that the marriage hall was in poor condition when he inspected it, with seepage, inadequate lighting and fans, and faded paint. As the facility had enjoyed considerable popularity in the past, efforts were made to restore its former appeal. Around ₹20 lakh was spent on basic renovation works after consultations with the Collector and by utilising available institutional funds, the Joint Collector said, adding that it would be a boon to the residents of Chittoor.

Meanwhile, MLA Jagan Mohan said the facility had adequate parking, a dining hall, rooms, and a spacious function hall, making it suitable for various events. He urged residents to fully utilise the hall.

Officials said increased patronage would generate revenue for the sugar factory and help support its employees. They also stressed the need to address the cooperative sugar factory’s long-pending financial and operational problems.

World.title: CDF Munir meets Iranian interior minister in Tehran; ISPR says visit part of Pakistan's efforts for regional peace
World.content:
Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi met with Iranian Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni in Tehran on Monday, state media in Pakistan reported.

The CDF and interior minister reached Tehran on Monday, Iranian media reported, after Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) described the visit “as part of Pakistan’s efforts to promote regional peace and stability”.

Iranian foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei said that the visit undertaken by CDF Munir and Naqvi was taking place as bilateral ties between Islamabad and Tehran “reach one of their strongest stages”, state broadcaster IRIB reported.

Baqaei added that the Pakistani delegation’s visit was unrelated to the visit of Oman’s foreign minister, who is expected to arrive today. He noted that “both visits will address regional security issues”.

ISPR said CDF Munir will “focus on promoting efforts towards peaceful, lasting and comprehensive resolution of the conflict in the Middle East” during the visit.

Iranian foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei on Sunday said CDF Munir was expected to travel to Tehran to continue efforts to bring peace and security to the region.
